deckhand.stance: Quadruped at rest — all four flat plantigrade palms down, heels flat — and he rears back onto his haunches (hind feet plus rump) whenever both forepaws are needed, standing full upright on his hind legs only in scared and cheer.
deckhand.wardrobe: Every one of the eighteen frames: yellow sou'wester rain hat on a knotted chin cord, navy rain cape with one brass clasp offset at his RIGHT throat, and one tan coil of rope that never leaves his body — riding his right shoulder by default, otherwise in a paw with the line running back to him, or wrapped around him.
deckhand.anatomy: He is a raccoon, so every hero pose transfers one to one — but paint Jimothy's body canon, not a trash panda: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY tail that never streams, curls out behind or ropes water. Plantigrade always: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down — never knuckles, never knuckle-walking. Standing four-square means all four palms are down and no limb is free, so any frame that holds a cup, a coil or an open-armed gesture is sat back on his haunches instead; that swap is already written into each frame below and must not be reversed. The animation work is the costume: the cape is cloth (wet vertical folds at rest, snapped flat behind him in the air, flogging in a run), the rope is line with real weight and sag, and the hat is tied on, so it slips onto its cord in flee, ko, dizzy and splash without ever separating from him.

frames.desc: Standing four-square facing camera, all four flat palms down, weight settled back on his heels, the tan coil riding his right shoulder and dragging that shoulder visibly lower than the other. Cape hangs in wet vertical folds, one fat bead of rain gathering at the front of the yellow brim, face calm and patient like a man watching for a boat that is nine minutes late.

Sat upright on his haunches, the coil lifted off the shoulder and cradled in both flat palms against his belly, cape gathered in wet folds over his hips and never spreading onto anything below him. Hat tipped back off his brow so the whole face reads, eyes half-lidded and content, looking somewhere past the camera at water we cannot see.

Still sat on his haunches with the coil resting across his own knees as a table and an unprinted paper tray of ferry-galley clam strips balanced on it, touching his chest — that is the joke. The back of one flat palm nudges the hat brim up while the other lifts a strip halfway to a full cheek, tartar sauce on the whiskers, cape hanging wet down his back.

Flattened low on all fours, palms flat and heels down, haunches up and loaded, cape slid forward over the shoulders and bunched at the neck. The coil stays lashed on his right shoulder and swings down against his ribs — nothing in the jaws — hat brim jammed to the eyebrows, eyes locked forward.

Fully airborne, limbs spread wide and belly forward, cape snapped dead straight behind him like a signal flag, hat held on by the taut chin cord, mouth open in delight. One end of the rope has sprung free into two open loops that stay tight behind his hips and overlap his body, the coil itself still on the shoulder.

Body low and the weight absorbed through the shoulders, one forepaw planted flat with the fingers spread while the other is already reaching up for the brim that has bounced down over one eye, whiskers forward. The coil has slid forward off the shoulder and heaps against his own forearm, cape flopped over the far shoulder, a tight burst of grit and spray coming off the planted palm alone.

Side-on sprint to the right, body low, legs at full stretch, cape streaming off to the left behind him. The coil is hooked over his right shoulder — the far one at this angle — swinging out of rhythm with his stride, the brass clasp showing at his right throat, one flat palm clamping the hat down.

Flat out to the right, legs fully extended, cape horizontal, the coil bouncing hard off his right hip with one loop just starting to unspool but staying inside his own outline. Hat mashed flat to the skull with the chin cord snapped straight back, eyes wide, short white speed streaks and torn rain kept tight behind his heels.

Held completely still and vibrating: sat back on his haunches with the hind feet planted and locked, both flat palms strangling a plain scorched paper cup at chest height, fur bristled, pupils gone to pinpricks under a trembling yellow brim, the coil quivering on his shoulder. Pale cream-white steam rips off the cup, short jitter lines hug his silhouette and gold-orange fire licks at his heels — the feet do not move.

Reared up on his haunches, both flat palms thrown open and mouth wide in pure astonishment, hat pushed back and cape flung open, a short bight of his own rope arcing off one paw and back to the shoulder coil. Gold bottlecaps, coins and fries come spiralling in along that bight like beads running down a mooring line, every one of them close enough to overlap his body — joy that things come to him, never grabbing.

Reared up on his haunches with arms folded and faintly smug, still wearing the rain hat and rain cape underneath anyway, because he has lashed a black ferry-deck umbrella to his own shoulder coil with a neat little hitch so both paws stay free. The canopy sits directly over his head with the lashing visible running down to the coil, rain shedding off the rim in short streaks that stop at shoulder height.

Crouched back on his haunches at the instant of impact, one forearm across his face and the other holding the coil up in front of him like a buckler, ears flat, one eye squeezed shut, hat brim pressed down, cape bunched at the neck. A blue-violet dome hugs him just past the ears and elbows with rain streaking off the outside and the rope fibres lit along their edges inside.

Up on his hind legs, hugging the coil to his chest like a life ring, head tilted back and up so the brim rides off his brow and the eyes go huge. Cape hem lifting, stubby tail rigid, a hard gull-shaped shadow falling across his chest and face only — nothing cast anywhere below him.

Sprinting hard to the left, mouth open in flat panic, hat blown back onto its chin cord and bouncing on his shoulders, cape flogging. Half the coil has unspooled into short flailing loops he has no time to gather, tucked behind his hip and kept inside his own outline, with red speed streaks close to his heels and two sharp shock marks over his head.

Up on his hind legs, both feet planted proud, one arm flung high with the rope still running down from that raised paw so the loop he threw hangs as a perfect open circle just above and slightly behind his head, overlapping his ears — a halo he tied himself. Mouth wide with joy, hat shoved back off the brow, cape thrown open and hanging low to keep his mass in the centre of the frame.

Flat on his back with his legs in the air, wrapped shin to shoulder in three neat turns of his own rope like a badly parcelled package, undone by the one thing he is good at — the face is wounded professional pride, not pain. The hat has come off onto its cord and lies against his ear with the brim tipped across one eye, the visible eye a dazed swooning half-moon, cape spread flat beneath him, gold stars circling above the brim.

Sprawled and sitting up crooked, spiral eyes, tongue out, hat spun around backwards on its cord and the cape twisted up under his chin like a bib. The coil has come undone around HIM — two loops round one ankle, one across his chest, the rest heaped against his own hip — which for a deckhand is the actual injury; stars circling his head, one connected silhouette, nothing loose beside him.

The instant of shock inside an exploding white crown of water that bursts up around his ribs: soaked, fur plastered flat, both arms up, mouth wide, eyes huge, cape sodden and pinned to his flank. One flat palm still grips the rope and the line runs taut for a body length before ending in a frayed knot well inside the frame — he never let go of the tie-off — the yellow hat knocked off onto its cord and resting brim-up against his shoulder.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. No puddles, no damp smears, no cast shadows on pavement, no dock planks, no curbs, no rope lying loose on a floor, no scattered crumbs. Only contact effects that touch the body are allowed: the grit and spray off the planted palm in land, the water crown at his ribs in splash, the fire licks at his heels in coffee.

NOTHING TOUCHES A FRAME EDGE OR A DIVIDER LINE. The splash tie-off line, the flee loops, the magnet bight and the cheer halo all end well inside their own cell with a clear magenta margin. Every rope end is inside its own cell or the cutter reads two components and slices the rope off.

COLOUR LAW. Hat yellow and rope tan locked to ONE value each across the whole sheet — at 59px those two colours are the entire silhouette read and a half-step darker frame will flicker in the hop cycle. Steam is pale cream-white, the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy’s own; saturated PINK or MAGENTA is what the knockout bites out — blue-dominant violet is safe and is what the hero uses.

NO LETTERING ANYWHERE. The paper cup, the clam-strip tray, the brass cape clasp and the hat carry texture and shape only, never words, headlines or a logo — it is illegible at 59px and it mirrors into gibberish.

ENVELOPE. Every frame including its effects sits between about 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x the idle box. The check is the HEAD: it must be the same number of pixels in all eighteen. The cape flares in leap, dash-run and cheer — let it crowd the gap, never shrink the raccoon to make room for it.

THE HAT AND THE ROPE NEVER LEAVE THE BODY. The hat is on its chin cord in all eighteen; a loose hat anywhere in a cell becomes its own sprite when the sheet is cut. Same for the rope — shoulder, paw with the line running back to him, or wrapped around him, and nothing else.
deckhand.runL: Must be painted separately — the coil rides his right shoulder and the brass cape clasp sits offset at his right throat, so mirroring run-r puts both on the wrong side.

market.stance: Upright biped at rest — hind feet planted, heels down, stubby tail as counterweight — dropping to plantigrade all-fours ONLY in the six travel frames (crouch, leap, land, run-r, dash-run, flee), where the bag-carrying left forearm still never reaches the road; he is never four-square, because the bag always occupies one arm.
market.wardrobe: In all eighteen: brown kraft grocery bag on the LEFT forearm (full-length baguette, carrot tops, celery, one apple inside), green box satchel on a single diagonal strap over the RIGHT shoulder to the left hip, one scallion (teeth, or behind the right ear when the mouth is busy) — no clothing; the takeaway cup, the umbrella and the dome are power-up props belonging to their one frame only.
market.anatomy: He is a raccoon, so every pose in Jimothy's own pack works skeletally — the constraint is the hand budget, not the body: the left forearm is permanently spent on the grocery bag, only the right paw is ever free, and the two frames that need both forelimbs (magnet, shield) put the bag over the head or open across the chest, never on the floor. Jimothy body canon holds in all eighteen: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY ringed tail — never the long streaming rope of a lean trash panda. Plantigrade always: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heels down; no knuckles, and no tiptoes even in cheer. Head size is the scale check — the skull must be the same pixel height in every frame; the bag is the thing that changes shape (full, crushed, open wide, tipped, splitting), never him.

frames.desc: Upright on his hind legs facing camera, heels down, stubby tail counterweighting behind; left forearm cradling the overfull kraft bag at his hip, right paw hanging loose and open, scallion clamped sideways in his teeth. The bag is stuffed past its rim with free carrot tops three different stallholders kept adding, and his eyes cut just off camera with the mild embarrassment of a raccoon who did not ask for any of this.

Sitting back on his haunches off duty, the bag leaned against his thigh with one flat palm resting on top of it out of habit, satchel slid into his lap with the clasps undone, scallion still in his teeth like a toothpick. Ears relaxed, eyes half-lidded on nothing in particular — the quiet frame: he shopped for a bigger household than the one waiting at home.

Sitting beside the slumped-open bag with the baguette out and visibly half gone, one broken end held up in his right paw and the other cheek packed full, scallion parked behind his right ear. Eyes squeezed shut in bliss, crumbs caught in his chest fur and in the open satchel and none falling free — dinner, several hours early.

Three-point and loaded: both hind feet and his flat right palm down, haunches up, left forearm clamping the bag hard against his chest with the baguette standing straight up out of it like a mast. Shoulders tilted from the missing limb, eyes locked forward, scallion clenched in his teeth, the produce already leaning back from the launch.

Fully airborne, belly forward, back legs kicked wide, bag hugged to his chest with the baguette raked back along his spine like a rudder, its tip no more than a head past his rump, satchel flown up on its taut strap. One escaped carrot hangs against his ear and overlaps it, and he is grinning far too wide to have noticed.

Weight absorbed low, right palm planted flat with fingers spread and a tight spray bursting off it, left forearm still clamping the bag to his chest, satchel swung forward and thumped against his belly. Whiskers pushed forward, one eye scrunched from the impact, a carrot and a celery stalk floating an inch above the bag mouth and still overlapping it.

Side-on sprint to the right, right flank to camera, body low and legs at full extension: the satchel streams back off his near hip and the bag is clamped under his far arm, its brown rim and one carrot showing above his chest line with the baguette raked back along his spine. Ears laid flat, scallion still in his teeth, mouth shut and grimly professional.

The same sprint flat out — legs stretched to the limit, ears pinned, eyes wide and white-rimmed, satchel flying horizontal, baguette raked back hard over the bag rim. Warm amber speed streaks tear off his heels and hips and touch him, and one carrot tumbles just behind his tail, overlapping it.

Standing dead still and vibrating: hind feet planted, heels down, fur lifted in bristles, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, jitter lines hugging his outline and a faint double image on the scallion in his teeth. A takeaway cup is wedged into the bag mouth beside the baguette because he has no paw left for it, pale blush-cream steam curling off it, small amber fire licks at his heels.

Upright with the bag hauled wide open in both arms like a net, head tipped back, mouth open in pure astonishment that the world is handing him things, scallion clamped in the corner of his teeth. Gold bottlecaps and loose produce spiral in tight and drop through the top — the outermost cap overlapping his ear — and the satchel has flapped open and is catching two of them.

Upright under an open umbrella held high in his right paw, tilted right off to his left so the bag underneath stays bone dry while his own right shoulder takes the whole soaking. Smug, ears flat, a drip hanging off his chin, short rain streaks shedding off the canopy rim only.

Braced low with the bag hoisted over his head in both arms and his eyes screwed shut, a bright blue-violet dome flaring tight around him with rain streaking off its curve. One carrot has been knocked loose and hangs against the bag mouth inside the dome, satchel swung round behind his back from the force.

Up on his hind legs, bag clutched flat to his chest with his left arm, the baguette pulled out and held up in his right paw like a sword he has no intention of using, eyes huge and rolled straight up at the sky. Ears pinned back, scallion drooping out of his slack open mouth.

Three-quarter sprint toward camera, mouth open in panic, the bag jammed under his left arm, one carrot and one celery stalk spraying tight behind him and overlapping his tail and the bag mouth. Short red-orange speed streaks off his heels and two fat exclamation marks tucked in against his shoulder.

Up on his hind legs, heels down, stretched tall, the baguette punched up on a diagonal in his right paw like a torch with its tip no more than a head above his crown, the bag hoisted in his left with celery and carrot tops popping out of it. Mouth wide open in a joyful shout, eyes shut, scallion behind his right ear, two or three bottlecaps flicking up against his shoulders.

Flat on his back, long skinny legs in the air, the bag tipped over against his head with produce spilling in a short arc across his ear and cheek and every piece touching him, baguette laid across his chest, satchel flopped open with a carrot resting on his belly. Swooning half-moon eyes, a small dazed smile, scallion still in his teeth, stars circling — first time he has been off his feet all day and he looks quietly relieved about it.

Sprawled on his side with spiral eyes and his tongue lolling, the emptied bag upside down over one ear like a hat he has given up removing, the baguette still spinning with one end resting across his shins in a blur arc. Scallion drooping from his slack mouth, one lone carrot balanced on his nose, and a tight swirl of motion arcs instead of stars so he never reads as the ko.

The instant of the burst: soaked through, right arm thrown up, a white and pale-cyan water crown exploding around his waist, the sodden kraft bag going soft and splitting inside his own left grip. The baguette lies across the crown at his elbow and one carrot is plastered to his shoulder, scallion stuck flat to his cheek, his face pure shock — not at the water, at the bag.

sheetNotes: ENVELOPE IS THE KILL RULE. Every frame, effects included, sits between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside one box no more than ~1.2x the idle box; the character's HEAD must measure the same pixel height in all eighteen. cheer is the one most likely to blow it — that is why the baguette goes up on a diagonal, tip a head above the crown, not vertically to the sky.

NO GROUND, ANYWHERE. No puddles, cast shadows, kerbs, drains, drying smears, skid marks or spilled crumbs — the cutter keeps every non-magenta island and they come out as grey scum floating under him. Contact effects that touch the body are correct: the spray off the landing palm, the fire licks at his heels, the water crown at his waist.

DETACHED PIECES: half a body width, and they must overlap his bounding box. Every loose carrot, celery stalk and bottlecap in leap, land, dash-run, flee, magnet, shield, cheer and ko is tucked against fur, ear, tail or the bag mouth. Nothing floats out on its own or it cuts as a second sprite and shrinks him.

CENTRE-ANCHORED, NOT BOTTOM-ANCHORED — the engine centres the sprite on the lane point, so a high baguette or a trailing satchel drags the whole animal off his line. Keep his body mass at the middle of the painted content in every frame.

NO LETTERING ON THE PROPS: plain kraft bag with a rolled fold and creases, satchel with stud and latch texture only — no shop name, no print, no logo, it mirrors and it is illegible at 59px. Continuity: baguette full length in seventeen frames and half eaten only in eat; the scallion never vanishes. Lay out 6x3 with white divider lines and a clear magenta margin — nothing touches a divider or a frame edge.
market.runL: Must be painted separately: the bag rides the LEFT forearm and the strap crosses right shoulder to left hip, so mirroring swaps the entire costume — and it is not the same picture reversed anyway, because in run-r the bag is on his far side and half-occluded behind his chest, while in run-l it is near-side and fully visible.

hardhat.stance: Quadruped at rest — plantigrade raccoon, four flat palms down, heel down; he rears onto his hind legs ONLY in coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared and cheer, and never knuckle-walks.
hardhat.wardrobe: In all 18 frames: scuffed orange hard hat on a thin chinstrap; hi-vis sash running LEFT shoulder to RIGHT hip, two reflective stripes, small brass clip where it crosses; a BLANK orange-and-white octagon paddle on a short pole, slung on his back under the sash by default (comes into paws only in sit, eat, umbrella, shield, and lies on his chest in ko); a dented steel thermos on a short cord clipped at his right hip. The black lunch pail is the one extra, in eat only, and it rests on him.
hardhat.anatomy: He is hero Jimothy's skeleton exactly, so every pose transfers one for one — round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a STUBBY ringed tail in all eighteen frames (never streaming, never a rope of water). Hands are the giveaway: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down, plantigrade in every frame including the runs. The honest work on this skin is wardrobe physics, not anatomy — the chinstrap is what lets the hat survive leap, land, dizzy and splash, and the sash is a loose loop that swings and skews but never leaves the left-shoulder-to-right-hip diagonal. A frame that needs a paw for a prop must rear him up; four-square means no free limb, which is why the paddle rides on his back.

frames.desc: Standing four-square facing camera, round and scrunched, weight even on four flat palms, stubby ringed tail hanging straight down, no limb free. Hat level and scuffed on its chinstrap, both sash stripes catching the streetlight, blank octagon slung on his back with the pole angled past his right shoulder, thermos still on its hip cord — face calm and faintly tired, a raccoon who has stood in this exact spot for thirty years.

Sat back on his haunches on nothing — no curb, no kerbstone, no pavement — with the paddle pulled round and tucked under one arm so the octagon props behind his shoulder like a backrest. Hat pushed back to show the sweat-flattened dent ring in his head fur, both flat palms cupping the thermos lid with one curl of pale cream steam; shoulders down, eyes soft, off duty for exactly ten minutes.

Sitting with the paddle laid flat across his lap as a tray and the open black lunch pail resting on it against his chest, half a wax-paper sandwich held in both palms mid-bite, cheeks full. Hat tipped back, thermos lid balanced on the pail lid, one crumb on his chin — the joke is that somebody at home still cuts it in half for him.

Flattened low on all fours with his chest almost down and his haunches loaded high, palms spread flat, stubby tail low — nothing painted under him. Hat brim shoved down so his eyes glint out from beneath it, sash swung forward loose on his chest but still on the same diagonal, octagon riding flat on his back, whiskers pinned.

Fully airborne, limbs thrown wide but tucked inside the frame, round belly forward, stubby tail flicked up, mouth open in a delighted whoop. The hat lifts a half inch and is caught by the chinstrap under his jaw, the sash flags back off his shoulder, and the back-slung octagon swings out level with his hip — nothing trails, nothing sprays.

Front paws planted hard on flat spread palms with the elbows bent, body low and round, stubby tail up for balance, whiskers forward. The hat drops over his brow on impact and the sash swings across his chest; a tight puff of grit sprays off his palms and stays touching them — no dust cloud, no cast shadow, no gravel lying on a floor.

Side-on hop to the right, spine bowed and compact rather than stretched long, back legs extended, one flat palm reaching forward. Hat pinned low over his eyes, sash streaming back with the two stripes smearing into a short light trail, octagon riding above his hip on his back, thermos bouncing on its cord.

The same side-on sprint flat out — legs at full stretch, ears flat, eyes wide, cheeks pushed back by the wind, body still round. Hat brim pressed flat, sash horizontal like a banner, and short orange-and-white speed streaks plus warm gold sparks starting at his hind claws and touching him, none reaching more than half a body width back.

He is NOT MOVING: reared up on his hind legs with both heels flat and planted, whole body vibrating in place, fur bristled, pupils two different sizes, teeth clenched in a wired grin. One paw round the thermos lid slopping over the rim, the other clamped on the hat brim to hold it down on his shaking head, pale blush-cream steam, short jitter lines at his elbows and small warm-gold heat licks at his feet — no lean, no stride, no speed streaks.

Reared up with the hat lifted off and held upturned in both flat palms as a bucket, chinstrap still round his throat so it never leaves him, the sweat-dent ring in his head fur finally showing, mouth open in astonished delight. A tight spiral of gold bottlecaps and fries pours in and touches his paws and the hat rim the whole way; the ones he misses ring off the rim with little warm-orange impact sparks.

Reared up holding the blank orange-and-white octagon flat overhead in both paws with the elbows bent so it clears the hat brim by about an inch — never at full arm stretch. Short rain ticks tight around him and two proper gutter streams pouring off the hat brim; eyes half-lidded, thoroughly smug, because the paddle is decoration and the hat is doing all the work.

The instant of the hit — the blank octagon snapped up flat in front of his chest with a bright blue-violet dome flaring off its face, rain and grit streaking around the curve and staying inside half a body width. Head turned away, one eye squeezed shut, hat knocked down over his brow, one hind heel skidding back: braced, flinching, saved.

Reared up with his head cranked back to the sky, both flat palms clamped down on the hat brim because three generations of instinct say the hat handles it. Eyes huge and white-ringed, mouth a small flat line, sash jumped up loose on his chest but still on the same left-to-right diagonal, thermos swinging out on its cord.

Sprinting to the left in open-mouthed panic, one flat palm jammed on the hat so it cannot fly off, the other pumping, hind legs at full stretch. The thermos stays clipped and bounces off his hip with a short arc of coffee flicking back onto his own flank, short red-orange streaks at his heels and one small white shock-burst at his shoulder — nothing dropped, no spill trail, no painted punctuation.

Reared up tall, one arm punched up with the elbow bent so the fist stops just above the hat rather than at full stretch, the other paw a fist at his chest, mouth wide open in a whoop. Hat knocked back on his head, both reflective stripes lit, octagon riding on his back — the road is still never finished, but this bit is.

Flat on his back, all four skinny limbs in the air, tongue out, eyelids swooning half-moons, three gold stars circling close enough to touch his ears. The hat has tipped onto its side against his ear and stays touching him brim-up, the sash lies slack across his belly, and the octagon has swung round to lie flat on his chest — his face says occupational hazard, third time this shift.

Sprawled on his side with spiral eyes and his tongue lolling, stars orbiting close overhead and overlapping the hat. The hat has been spun clean backwards so the brim sits over the back of his neck, the octagon has slid round and lies across his upper flank still hooked under the sash, and two stray broom bristles and a little grit are stuck in his fur.

The instant of the burst: soaked through, both arms up, mouth open in shock, fur plastered flat to a much smaller raccoon inside an exploding white crown of water that touches him all the way round. Hat tipped back on his crown with water bursting past and under the brim so it is still the one dry thing in the picture, stripes glowing hard in the dark water, octagon just clearing his shoulder — nothing detached, nothing going under.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND IN ANY FRAME. He floats on magenta and is drawn over lane art, so there is no curb in sit, no pavement under crouch, no gravel scattered by land, no spill puddle behind flee, no cast shadow anywhere. Contact effects that touch the body are correct and wanted: grit off the landing palms, sparks off the dash claws, heat licks at the coffee feet, the splash crown bursting against his fur.

NOTHING DETACHED, EVER. The cut keeps non-magenta islands, so every loose element must touch him and sit inside half a body width: ko's tipped hat rests against his ear, magnet's bottlecap spiral touches paws and hat rim, ko and dizzy stars overlap ears and hat, splash water touches fur. The thermos stays on its hip cord in all 18 and never tumbles free.

ENVELOPE AND HEAD TEST. Every frame including effects must land between about 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside roughly 1.2x the idle box; the checkable version is that his HEAD is the same pixel size in all eighteen. That is why umbrella's paddle sits an inch above the brim and cheer's fist stops just above the hat instead of at full stretch, and why rain, streaks and water crowns stay short and tight.

ZERO TEXT, ZERO LOGOS. The paddle is a BLANK orange octagon with a plain white border ring on a short pole — no lettering, no numerals, no symbols. Nothing printed on the hat, sash, thermos or lunch pail either; texture and shape only.

COLOUR LAW. The knockout eats the magenta family, so no hot-pink or magenta anywhere: coffee steam is pale blush-cream (green channel high), the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy’s own. The sash cross-clip is small BRASS.

CROP MARGIN AND SCALE. Leave 8-10px of clear magenta above and either side of the hat brim (his widest and highest point) and around the raised paddle, the raised fist and the outer water crown; nothing touches a divider line or a cell edge. Match his SHOULDER height to hero Jimothy, not his overall height, or the hat makes him tower over the roster. Draw the divider lines first, uneven rows, generous gutters.
hardhat.runL: Must be painted separately — the sash diagonal (left shoulder to right hip), the brass cross-clip, the right-hip thermos and the back-slung octagon all reverse under a mirror, so the whole costume would read backwards on every leftward hop.

scout.stance: Upright plantigrade biped at rest — heels down, flat palms free, never four-square — dropping onto all fours ONLY in the six travel/impact frames (crouch, leap, land, run-r, dash-run, flee) plus the painted run-l; locked, no silent switches anywhere else.
scout.wardrobe: In all 18 frames: navy patch vest with the top two buttons fastened and the hem left open, brass buttons down the placket, a wordless square cream merit patch on HIS RIGHT chest, a small round brass badge low on HIS LEFT hip, and a cream neckerchief knotted square at the throat — nothing else is permanent.
scout.anatomy: This is hero Jimothy's body in a costume, so every reference pose transfers one-to-one: round and spherical with NO visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY tail that never streams, ropes or curls out behind him in any frame. Plantigrade throughout — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down; the word "knuckles" does not appear on this sheet. The vest is stiff and swings as one unit from the shoulders, flaring only from the open hem, while the neckerchief is loose cloth that streams, flops and soaks. The single checkable rule: his HEAD is the same pixel height in all 18 frames — if an effect shrinks the head, the effect is too big.

frames.desc: Standing upright at attention on his hind legs, heels flat, chest pushed out, chin level, long skinny arms straight at his sides with flat palms turned in. Vest square and formal, neckerchief knot dead centre, rain beading on his shoulders and both badges catching a little streetlight.

Sitting upright on his haunches, back straight and knees together, one flat palm smoothing the merit patch against his chest and the other laid on his knee, stubby tail tucked. Off duty and still sitting like he expects to be inspected, mouth a small content line.

Sitting on his haunches toasting a marshmallow on a bent wire held with enormous procedural correctness, cheeks already packed, neckerchief tucked into the vest as a bib; the little Sterno tin rests against one hind foot and the dented enamel mess-cup is hooked in his other paw. A second marshmallow is already threaded on the wire for a troop that did not come — this is the quiet frame.

Flattened low on all fours, haunches up, elbows out, flat palms spread wide, eyes locked up-street. Neckerchief tails hang forward past his chin and the brass hip badge glints — coiled like he is demonstrating correct technique to a troop that is not there.

Fully airborne, limbs spread but reaching no further than a body width, belly forward, mouth open and delighted, stubby tail up. The open hem of the vest flares back off his ribs while the fastened top holds the square merit patch flat and readable, and the neckerchief streams straight back like a troop pennant.

Front paws slammed down flat with the fingers splayed, knees deep, stubby tail up as counterweight, vest dropping back against his chest and the neckerchief flopping over it. A tight ring of spray bursting off his own palms and nothing else beneath him — whiskers forward, extremely satisfied with the landing.

Side-on sprint to the RIGHT, body low, front and back legs at full extension, neckerchief streaming back to the left, vest hem flaring from the waist. His right flank is to camera so the square cream merit patch and the brass placket buttons read clearly along the near side.

The same rightward side-on sprint pushed flat out, ears pinned, legs at full stretch, warm gold-white speed streaks kept short and overlapping his hindquarters. One corner of the merit patch has torn loose from its stitching and flutters against his chest — eyes wide, faintly appalled at his own speed.

A STANDING frame, not a run: upright with both heels planted and going nowhere, a dented enamel camp percolator mug clutched in both flat palms at his chest. All the energy is in the body — fur bristled out, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, jitter ticks off his ears and elbows, pale blush-cream steam boiling past his mask and small warm fire licks curling off his heels.

Upright with both arms thrown wide and his mouth open in astonished delight as gold bottlecaps and snack scraps spiral in tight toward his chest, the innermost few already stuck flat to the navy vest like brand new merit badges. He is not grabbing anything — he is being awarded it, and he knows it.

Standing dead straight at parade posture under a small, carefully hand-mended umbrella gripped in one flat palm, canopy tucked low over his ears and barely wider than his shoulders, rain bouncing off it close around him. Neckerchief bone-dry and perfectly knotted, one eyebrow raised: he brought this, obviously.

Crouched hard with one forearm slammed across his face and the other palm flung out flat, a bright blue-violet energy dome ringing him tight with rain streaking off its curve. Eyes screwed shut, teeth gritted, the vest and both badges lit cold by the glow.

Up on his hind legs with both flat palms clutched over the badges on his chest, ears flat, eyes enormous, head tipped back at whatever is lining up on him. His neckerchief knot has pulled crooked for the first time in his life — he is guarding the badges, not himself.

Panicked three-quarter run straight toward camera, veering to his own left so BOTH the chest patch and the hip badge stay readable, mouth open, ears back, vest hem flapping wide from the waist. One palm is clamped flat over the merit patch to stop it shaking loose, with short warm amber-white streaks tight behind his heels.

Standing tall on the spot, one arm up in a crisp three-finger scout salute that has completely lost its composure into a whoop — elbow bent so the paw stays close over his skull — the other palm pressed to his chest. Mouth wide open, eyes shut with joy, small gold sparks popping right at the badges.

Flat on his back with his legs straight up and his arms flopped out either side, mouth open, eyes closed into swooning half-moon lids, a tight ring of stars circling close over his skull. The neckerchief has flipped up over one eye and the little brass hip badge has popped its pin and come to rest on his own belly — mortified about the uniform, not hurt.

Sprawled on one hip and trying to sit back up wrong, spiral eyes and tongue out and NO stars at all, vest dragged half off one shoulder and the neckerchief spun round so the knot sits at the back of his neck. One flat palm is still gamely attempting a salute and missing his forehead by a mile.

Soaked through and clearly out of play inside a white and pale-cyan crown of water bursting around his waist, arms up, mouth open in shock, mask fur plastered flat and the vest gone black with wet. One corner of the merit patch has lifted and the water is pulling at it, still stitched at the other end — plainly the worse tragedy.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND IN ANY FRAME. No asphalt, pavement, puddles, cast shadows, drains, kerbs or scattered litter anywhere in the 18 — the cutter is a magenta border flood and every one of those survives as floating grey scum under a character who has nothing beneath him. Contact spray that touches his own palms (land, splash) is correct and welcome.

Sprites are CENTRE-anchored, not bottom-anchored (the old sheet note was wrong), and every frame is normalised on its own, so anything a frame adds is subtracted from the animal. Keep every frame between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x the idle box, with his body mass at the centre of the painted content — umbrella canopy, cheer salute, ko stars and the splash crown are the four that will blow it, so keep all four tucked in close.

Anything not touching him — bottlecaps, sparks, stars, speed streaks, rain — must sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, or the cut orphans it into its own sprite. Nothing may touch a divider line or a frame edge; draw the white dividers first and paint a visible margin inside them, magenta #FF00FF everywhere else, and do not use an even grid.

NO lettering, numerals or punctuation anywhere, props included: the merit patch is a wordless embroidered shape (a simple fir-tree silhouette), the brass badge a plain stamped disc, and there are no '!!' or shock letters behind the flee frame. It is illegible at 59px and it mirrors into gibberish.

Colour law and the 59px read: steam is pale blush-cream with the green channel up (never hot pink), the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. At 59px he must read as one dark navy block, a bright cream diagonal at the throat, one pale square on the right chest and one gold dot at the left hip; keep those four values far apart and everything else quiet.

One-frame props only, and all of them in physical contact with him: Sterno tin, marshmallow wire and mess-cup (eat), percolator mug (coffee), umbrella (umbrella). Nothing else ever leaves the body — the popped badge in ko lands on his own belly, the peeling patch in splash stays stitched at one end. Badge placement is otherwise identical in all 18; the only allowed deviations are the torn patch corner in dash-run, the popped hip badge in ko and the lifted patch corner in splash.
scout.runL: Must be painted separately as a real 19th frame: the square cream merit patch (his right chest), the round brass hip badge (his left hip) and the placket buttons are all asymmetric, so a mirror throws his badges onto the wrong side and flips the neckerchief knot — paint run-l as a side-on sprint to the LEFT with his LEFT flank to camera so the brass hip badge and the neckerchief tails read on the near side, same pose and same head height as run-r.

firstfrost.stance: Upright bipedal at rest — he stands, waits and gestures on his hind legs (idle, sit, eat, coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer), and drops forward onto his ONE free front palm only for the six travel frames (crouch, leap, land, run-r, dash-run, flee); the cup paw never touches the ground in any of the eighteen, so he is never four-square.
firstfrost.wardrobe: In all 18: the red hand-knit scarf, double-wrapped at the throat with its fringed end down his viewer-LEFT chest, and the kraft-and-white takeaway coffee cup with a brown lid, always in his viewer-RIGHT front paw and always physically touching his body — the only frame-only additions anywhere on the sheet are the donut (eat) and the small slate-blue umbrella (umbrella), both held against him.
firstfrost.anatomy: Jimothy's body canon holds exactly: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY ringed tail — never a long streaming trash-panda tail in any of the eighteen. He is plantigrade — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down — and never knuckle-walks, in the crouch, the land or anywhere else. Because one front paw is permanently occupied by the cup, every two-paw pose the hero solves with two paws (cheer, magnet, umbrella, shield, splash) is re-solved here with one free paw plus the scarf and the jaw, and the answer is always the same character truth: he protects the coffee first and himself second. The scarf is his second limb — it streams, catches, wraps and covers an eye — and the breath fog is his signature effect, faint at rest and heavy under exertion.

frames.desc: Standing upright and settled on his hind legs, front three-quarter high angle, scarf double-wrapped with the fringe down his viewer-left chest, stubby ringed tail curled out to his viewer-left, free paw hanging relaxed, cup up at shoulder height in the viewer-right paw. Eyes squinted content against the chill, one faint white breath plume at the muzzle, pale blush steam rising no higher than his ears — this is the existing painting and it is the master for camera, scale, lighting and costume.

Sat back on his haunches with the stubby tail curled around his own feet like a lap blanket and the scarf loosened one turn so it pools in his lap, both paws finally cradling the cup together under his chin, eyes half closed, steam and breath merged into one soft plume across his face. The only frame where he gets to hold it properly, and he is in no hurry — nobody is expecting him anywhere this early.

Sitting, cup hugged low and upright against his belly in the cup paw (it never leaves his body), dunking a half-eaten old-fashioned donut into it with the free paw, cheeks packed, eyes shut in total bliss. Sugar already dusted down the red knit and a fat puff of breath fog blooming around the donut.

Compressed low on all threes, hind legs folded, the free palm flat and spread on nothing — plantigrade, five long fingers, heel down — while the cup paw stays up and out at shoulder width, rock steady in a barista carry so nothing tips. Head low, ears back, eyes locked forward, scarf bunched at the jaw, one tight jet of breath from the corner of his mouth and a crackle of frost crystals ONLY where the palm presses; no pavement, no shadow.

Airborne in a compact arc, belly toward camera, hind legs tucked rather than trailing, free paw thrown forward and the cup paw bent so the cup rides dead level no higher than his ears — not a drop moving, and he knows it. Mouth open in a delighted hup, scarf curling in one short red S behind his shoulder and two beads of breath at the muzzle; nothing trails further than half a body width in any direction.

Free palm and both hind feet slamming down, knees folding deep to absorb it, body low, the cup swung in against his chest with the coffee crested up at the lip and not one drop over. Whiskers forward, eyes wide, scarf flopped up past his cheek, one breath punched out of him, and a tight collar of frost dust bursting right at the paws — the grit touches him, and there is nothing painted on the ground below it.

Side-on to the right in a low fast lope, hind legs at full extension, stubby ringed tail level behind him, cup carried forward and perfectly level in the lead paw like a lantern. Scarf streams back in a curling banner no longer than his own body, breath comes off as three short beads over his shoulder, expression cold-eyed and businesslike — he has somewhere to be and it is thirty-four degrees.

The same rightward sprint flat out, but the crop held tight: cup pulled hard in against his chest under the free arm (he protects it), scarf curling in one short whipped loop instead of a rigid banner, pale cold-vapour speed streaks only half a body long. Eyes huge, mouth open, breath reduced to three short beads at the muzzle and frost glitter flicking off the heels where they break contact — aspect must not exceed 1.35:1.

STANDING FRAME, held up to seven seconds: hind feet planted flat and dead still, every hair bristled, cup tipped to his mouth mid-gulp, ears bolt upright, pupils shrunk to pinpricks — the whole animal vibrates without travelling an inch. Baked in: short jitter lines tucked either side of him, a dense pale blush plume no taller than his own head, and two tight vapour rings hugging his shoulders that lift the scarf off his chest.

Standing, cup held high and safely out of traffic in the cup paw while the free paw pulls the scarf end out and open like an apron basket to catch the haul. Gold bottlecaps and fries spiral in tight — the nearest already touching the scarf hem, two ringing off the lid — mouth open and eyes wide with pure astonished delight, a laughing puff of breath; nothing orbits further than half a body width.

Standing under a small folding umbrella in pale slate-blue, canopy half-open and tipped forward into the weather, foreshortened so it is no wider than his shoulders plus a head, held in the free paw with the cup in the other and its steam pooling under the canopy like a small warm room. Sleet beads ice along the rim and bounces off short of the frame edge; chin up, eyes half-lidded, scarf hanging dead still in the dry air — the smuggest raccoon in Seattle.

Hunched and braced at the instant of the hit, knees bent, free paw flung up across his face, the cup hauled into his chest and hugged — he is shielding the coffee, not himself, and nothing spills. A blue-violet dome (never blue-violet) flares tight to his silhouette with a hot white impact ripple where it was struck, sleet skating off it, eyes screwed shut, teeth gritted, scarf blown flat, one shocked plume squeezed out.

Up on his toes, ears flat, head craned back and up at whatever is lining up above him, eyes enormous with the whites showing, free paw clutched to his chest over the scarf fringe and the cup paw out no further than his own shoulder width, still perfectly level. He is holding his breath, so instead of a plume there are two short frozen-vapour exclamation marks sitting within a head's height of his ears and overlapping his silhouette.

Sprinting flat out in full panic, mouth wide open, eyes rolled back over his shoulder, hind legs at full stretch, stubby tail straight out, scarf whipping across in front of his own chest rather than out of the cell, cup clutched hard against his ribs. The one frame where the coffee genuinely loses three or four dark drops — painted overlapping his body — with pale blue-white panic streaks half a body long and frost spray only where his heels break contact.

Standing tall on his hind legs, head thrown back, mouth wide open in a shout, free arm punched up but bent so the paw clears his crown by no more than a head, cup raised to eye level in a full toast. Scarf loops up behind him in a short red arc, steam and breath pop together in one dense low burst just above his head with frost sparkles held inside half a body width, and the first low sun of the morning rakes warm across his chest and muzzle — light on the fur, not a painted beam.

Flat on his back with his legs in the air, scarf fallen loose around his throat and back over his ears, mouth open in a soft ahh, tongue just showing, eyes gone to swooning half-moons with stars circling close above his head. The cup landed upright and leaning against his cheek, lid still on, still gently steaming — the coffee is completely fine and he is not, and he looks quietly proud of that; one last breath plume drifts off sideways.

Sprawled on his haunches and wobbling, spiral eyes, tongue out, ears at two different angles, the scarf wound right around his head by the sweeper brushes so it covers one eye and the fringe hangs over his nose. The cup is still gripped but upside down, the last of the coffee draining in one thin dark thread straight down his own muzzle and chest — no puddle, nothing on the ground — with stars circling above and wobble arcs tucked either side.

The instant of the burst: caught inside a cold blue-white crown of water with cracked skim-ice at its rim, fur plastered flat, free paw flung up, scarf curling wet around his throat inside the crown, eyes wide and mouth a small shocked oh — soaked and clearly out of play, nobody going under. The cup is still held as high as one arm reaches with its lid popped off and one fat icy drop landing in it; keep the crown low and tight so his body mass stays at the centre of the painted content.

sheetNotes: CROP HAZARDS ARE THE TWO PLUMES. The pink cup steam and the white breath fog are the character, but they are also what shrinks him: cap both at roughly his own head height, keep the scarf curl and every speed streak inside half a body width, and leave a clear margin so no plume, scarf tail or streak touches a divider line or a frame edge. Every frame, effects included, sits inside about 255 x 270 px at aspect 0.80:1 to 1.35:1 — the same envelope as the existing idle.png (255 x 270, 0.94). The checkable test: his HEAD is the same number of pixels in all eighteen.

NEVER PAINT THE FLOOR. No pavement, no frost sheet, no puddles (including the one deleted from dizzy), no cast shadows, no curbs, no scattered crumbs — the cutter floods magenta from the border and every one of those survives as floating grey scum under a character with no ground. Frost crackle, frost dust, spray and grit are allowed ONLY where they touch a paw or a heel.

COLOUR LAW, MEASURED OFF THE MASTER. The knockout eats the magenta family, and idle.png's steam sits at roughly 240/150/200 — it survives only because its green channel is up at 150. Paint the cup steam as pale blush-cream with green at 155 or above, never a saturated hot pink, and paint the shield dome BRIGHT blue-violet.

NO LETTERING ANYWHERE, PROPS INCLUDED. Blank kraft cup with a wordless band or ring, plain umbrella, plain donut, no logo on the lid. run-r is the frame that mirrors, and text flips into gibberish and is illegible at 59px regardless.

THE COFFEE NEVER SPILLS, AND THE CUP NEVER LEAVES HIM. Only flee (three or four drops, painted overlapping his body) and dizzy (draining upside down onto his own muzzle) break the gag — do not add a spill anywhere else, including the leap, the land and the shield hit. The cup must physically touch him in all eighteen; in ko it leans against his cheek, because a detached prop cuts out as its own sprite or inflates the crop and shrinks the animal.

WHAT HAS TO READ AT 59px: the red scarf mass, the kraft cup, the black bandit mask. Keep the scarf a single saturated red block rather than fringe detail, keep the cup silhouette clear of the scarf so the two do not merge into one shape, and keep the stubby tail short in every frame — a streaming ringed tail is a different raccoon and it also blows the envelope.
firstfrost.runL: Must be painted separately — the cup lives in his viewer-RIGHT paw and the scarf fringe hangs down his viewer-LEFT chest, so a mirror swaps both and on an epic skin the coffee visibly changes hands mid-run.

garage.stance: Quadruped at rest on the hero's own skeleton — plantigrade, flat palms down; he rears onto his hind legs only for coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared and cheer, and sits on his haunches for sit, eat and dizzy.
garage.wardrobe: In all 18 frames: sleeveless denim vest worn OPEN (never buttoned), deep plum-violet bandana knotted at the throat with the knot off-centre to his left, exactly three enamel pins on the left lapel (pale eye button top, amber sunburst middle, small orange dot bottom), a coiled quarter-inch amp cable over his RIGHT shoulder, and one guitar pick that never leaves him — plus two rationed set pieces, held on the body only: pizza box (eat, magnet) and guitar-case lid (umbrella, shield). The practice amp is CUT from the sheet entirely.
garage.anatomy: He is the hero's skeleton, so every pose maps one-to-one — but hold Jimothy's body canon: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs and a SHORT STUBBY tail that never streams, curls out behind or ropes water. Raccoons are PLANTIGRADE: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down, in every contact frame — there are no knuckles anywhere on this sheet, that gait belongs to the Sasquatch. The costume must not inflate him: vest shoulders and the cable coil sit tight to the body, and his head must measure the same number of pixels in all eighteen frames, which is the only checkable scale test. Cloth and rope behave — vest hangs open at rest, flares in the air, presses flat in a sprint, goes dark and heavy when soaked; the cable stays a coil, not a trailing line.

frames.desc: Standing four-square facing camera, all four palms flat and turned slightly out with the fingers spread, weight rocked back, vest hanging open, cable coiled on his right shoulder, pick tucked under the bandana knot. Ears up, brows faintly raised, patient and hopeful — he unlocked the garage twenty minutes ago and nobody has turned up; this is the sheet's quiet frame.

Sitting upright on his haunches, back rounded, the whole cable coil resting in his lap with one hind foot hooked through it, stubby tail tucked at his side. Eyes half closed, ears drooped a touch, pick clamped in the corner of his mouth, humming something and still half listening for footsteps at the door.

Sitting on his haunches with the open pizza box balanced on his knees and touching his chest, a folded cold slice held up in both flat paws, cheek packed, eyes shut in contentment, pick parked behind his right ear and one short sag of cheese running slice-to-chin. A second slice lies untouched in the box, cut for somebody who never came — nothing on the floor, no plate, no crumbs.

Flattened low on all fours with both palms flat and splayed, haunches up, elbows out, vest bunched around his shoulders, bandana shoved up under his chin, cable coil pulled tight against his back. Eyes locked dead forward, pick gripped crossways in his teeth — the held breath of a count-in before the downbeat.

Fully airborne and stretched, limbs spread wide with the palms open and fingers splayed, belly forward, denim vest flared off his ribs like two stiff wings, bandana streaming back, stubby tail up. Mouth open in a delighted whoop with the pick parked behind his ear; the cable stays coiled on the shoulder with one short loop of slack, half a body long, curling straight back into the coil.

Both palms slapped FLAT with the fingers splayed and the elbows bent to absorb, body low and compressed, shoulders up around his ears, vest slapping back down against his ribs, one pin still swinging on its clasp. A tight puff of grit bursts off each palm, whiskers and eyes forward, pick behind his ear — a drum hit arriving exactly on the beat.

Side-on sprint to the right, body long and low, plantigrade heels striking, vest streaming back so all three pins turn to camera and the bandana flies horizontal. The cable stays coiled on his right shoulder with a single short whip of slack curling back into it; pick crossways in his teeth, ears laid back.

Flat out and side-on, legs at maximum stretch, denim pressed flat to him, ears pinned, eyes wide with white showing all round, pick in his teeth. Baked in tight to the body: warm amber amp-glow streaks off his flanks, a few orange sparks off his heels, two small sound-wave rings overlapping his hindquarters, and the coil throwing one short snapping loop of slack — no long line behind him.

STANDING frame, not a run: reared on his hind legs with both feet planted flat and the whole body vibrating in place, a paper cup gripped in one flat paw, the other paw frozen mid-windmill on an air guitar, jaw clamped on the pick, fur bristled, pupils shrunk to pinpricks. Pale blush-cream steam shivers off the cup, short orange fire licks at both heels and jitter lines hug his outline — he can hear the entire song at once and he is not moving an inch.

Reared on his hind legs holding the empty pizza box open at his chest like a collection plate, mouth open in an astonished laugh, one hind foot lifting as the pull takes him. Gold bottlecaps and two spare picks spiral in on a tight bright-amber ribbon that hugs the box rim — every loose piece overlapping his silhouette — tugging the bandana sideways as they arrive; his own pick stays under the knot.

Reared on his hind legs holding the battered guitar-case lid over him at a three-quarter TILT, no more than about 1.3x his own width, so his face, bandana and one raised brow read clearly underneath and rain sheets off the near edge only. Wordless sticker shapes on the case, smug little line of a mouth, bone dry, cable still coiled on his shoulder and the pick under the knot.

Reared and crouched behind the tilted case lid with both flat palms braced against it, one eye screwed shut, all three pins rattling on the denim as the hit rings the case like a gong. A blue-violet energy dome flares close around him with rain streaking off the curve, one white shock ring and a thin feedback shimmer at the contact point — nothing dark violet, nothing reaching the frame edge.

Reared up on his hind legs, both flat paws clutched to his chest over the vest, ears flat, eyes huge and fixed up-screen, whole body leaning back from whatever is lining him up, bandana flopped half over one eye. The pick has just slipped from his teeth and hangs an inch from his nose, still overlapping his face — it never leaves him.

Sprinting to the left, mouth wide open in panic, vest flapping, one flat paw clamped over the bandana knot so he doesn't lose it and the other pinching the pick he snatched back out of the air mid-stride. The cable stays coiled with one short whipping loop of slack, warm orange-red panic streaks come off his heels and two small exclamation marks sit tucked close beside his ear.

Reared tall on his hind legs, head thrown back, mouth open in a joyful whoop, one arm up (elbow bent, so the frame stays square) with the pick pinched glinting between two claws, the other fist punched against his chest, vest thrown wide and bandana snapping. A warm amber amp-glow halo sits close behind his shoulders with three small sound-wave rings and a tight scatter of gold sparks, all inside the idle envelope.

Flat on his back, all four legs loose in the air with the palms open, vest splayed around him like a burst cushion, bandana over one eye, mouth open in a soundless ow, eyes gone to swooning half-moons — never X's — under a ring of circling yellow stars. All three pins stay on the denim with one swinging on its clasp, the pick spins in the air just above his belly, and one hind foot is still tapping out the four-count, because the set isn't over.

Sprawled on his rump with his legs out in front, wound ankle to shoulder in his own amp cable like a maypole gone wrong, bandana spun round so the knot sits at the back of his neck, stubby tail flat under him. Spiral eyes (spirals belong to dizzy alone — no stars in this frame), tongue out one side, ears pointing two different directions, one pin swinging and the pick stuck flat to his damp forehead.

Caught in the instant of the burst: both flat palms up, soaked through, fur spiked, denim gone dark and heavy, bandana clinging to his throat and the pins dulled to grey, eyes shocked wide and mouth open. A white-and-cream crown of water explodes around his middle with droplets frozen mid-air, and one paw still holds the pick clear above it — the only thing worth saving. He does not sink.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND, IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. The cutter floods magenta and keeps every non-magenta island, so wet pavement, puddles, cast shadows, the old greasy paper plate in eat and the two pins that used to 'wobble to a stop on the asphalt' in ko all survive the cut as floating grey scum under a character with no floor. Contact effects that touch him are correct and wanted: grit bursting off both palms in land, sparks off the heels, the splash crown at his waist.

THE PRACTICE AMP IS CUT. It was a torso-sized object present in only two of eighteen frames, so his apparent size changed in exactly those two — sit now runs on the cable coil in his lap, eat balances the pizza box on his knees against his chest. Set pieces are rationed and always in contact with the body: pizza box in eat and magnet, case lid in umbrella and shield, nothing else, ever.

ENVELOPE. Every frame including its effects must land between about 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside roughly 1.2x the idle box (the hero's own idle is 192x221). The five hazard cells are leap, magnet, umbrella, shield and cheer — trailing cable, bottlecap swirl, case lid and raised arm all want to blow the crop, and a bigger crop paints a smaller raccoon. The one checkable test: his head is the same pixel count in all eighteen.

THE CABLE IS A COIL, NOT A LINE, AND THE PICK NEVER LEAVES HIM. Travel frames (leap, run-r, run-l, dash-run, flee) get the coil on the shoulder plus one short whip of slack, half a body long, curling back into the coil — a long trailing line defines the crop and shrinks him in the frames the player sees hundreds of times a run. Pick ledger: under the bandana knot (idle, magnet, umbrella, shield), in his teeth (sit, crouch, run-r, run-l, dash-run, coffee), behind his ear (eat, leap, land), hanging by his nose (scared), pinched in claws (flee, cheer), spinning above his belly (ko), stuck to his forehead (dizzy), held clear of the water (splash).

DETACHED BITS AND MARGINS. Spare picks, bottlecaps, sparks, the falling pick and the exclamation marks must each sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, or the connected-components cut emits them as their own sprite. Nothing touches a frame edge or a divider line — draw the dividers first, then paint with a visible margin inside them. Paint idle, leap and cheer FIRST and send those three for a 59px lane test before committing the other fifteen.
garage.runL: Must be painted separately — the three pins on the left lapel, the off-centre bandana knot and the cable coil on the right shoulder all jump sides under the engine's mirror; in a true run-l the coil is the near-side read and the pins are largely hidden behind the far shoulder, which a flip cannot fake.

pigeon.stance: Two-legged ground bird: body carried level and forward over two coral feet in every standing frame, never reared upright like a person, and "four-square" never applies to him because he has two feet, not four.
pigeon.wardrobe: No costume and no carried kit — the only thing present in all 18 frames is the dried fleck of white crosswalk paint centred across the base of his tail; props appear in exactly three frames (fry cone in eat, takeaway cup in coffee, blown-out umbrella in umbrella) and every one of them touches his body.
pigeon.anatomy: He has wings instead of arms and a beak instead of hands, so every raccoon "holding" pose becomes standing IN the container with his head down inside it, and every "arms up" pose becomes a wing throw — wings go up, out and mantled forward over the crown, and never cross the chest, never point, never hold. He has no grip: pigeon feet are weak walking feet, so unlike the crow and the gull he never pins, clamps or tears food — he pecks and swallows whole, and his own body weight is the only thing that ever holds a prop still. He cannot fold onto his haunches, so sit is a settled curb loaf with the feet tucked away underneath, and on his back the two stiff coral feet point straight up. He can technically fly and never does: the hop in leap is the only air he ever gets, and flee is him hammering his wings and still not lifting off — that failure is the character.

frames.desc: LIVE ART — do not repaint. Both feet planted wide, body level, chest out, head up and cocked so the orange-ringed eye reads to camera; slate wings folded tight with the two black bars showing, green-violet neck sheen catching the streetlight, nothing painted under him. He owns the crosswalk and knows it.

THE QUIET FRAME. Settled into a full curb loaf, feet folded away out of sight, head sunk so deep between the shoulders he has no neck at all — a warm grey brick with one eye, feathers puffed a size larger against the rain, lids half down and aimed at nothing in particular. The swagger switches off the moment nobody is watching; no concrete, no puddle, no ground.

Standing INSIDE a tipped-over paper cone of fries with both feet, head down in the mouth of it and his own body weight — not a grip — stopping it rolling, one fry crosswise in his beak and the visible eye rolled up at camera mid-theft. Cone completely blank, no printing; nothing scattered on the ground.

LIVE ART — do not repaint. Body dropped low and horizontal, legs folded deep, feathers slicked flat to the skin, wings unlatched and just cracked open at the shoulders; head thrust forward, eye locked up-screen, tail dropped low. Loaded like a spring, nothing loose, no ground.

One hop's worth of air: wings only HALF-open with the wrists lifted and the tips no wider than about 1.25x his idle silhouette, breast forward, tail fanned, coral feet trailing curled beneath him, beak open in a delighted coo. Two loose down feathers hang right at his tail, overlapping his body — this is one of only three frames allowed to shed.

LIVE ART — do not repaint. Wings swept back and cupped hard against the air to brake, tail fanned wide and angled down like a flap, both coral feet stabbing down with the toes splayed, head low and neck feathers blown backward by his own stop. A tight burst of grit and rainwater breaks off the toes and touches them — contact only, no puddle beneath.

Side-on to the right in the flat-out pigeon scurry, wings clamped shut against the body, head thrust forward on a stretched neck mid-bob, one coral foot forward and one back at full stride. Body tipped nose-down, tail up with the white paint fleck centred on it, all business, no flying involved.

The same scurry absolutely committed: neck at full extension, wings half-cocked out for balance, both feet blurred into a coral smear, crown feathers streaming back. A short spray fan bursts off his own toes and two speed streaks trail off the tail — both stay tight to the body and well clear of the frame edge; no puddle, no ground.

A STANDING FRAME, held up to 7 seconds: both feet flat and planted, whole body rigid and vibrating, bill sunk into the mouth of a takeaway cup lying on its side against his chest with the lid leaning on its rim — pigeons drink by suction, so the head stays down but the eye clears the rim, enormous with a pinprick pupil, cut straight to camera. Pale blush-cream steam vents around his neck and warm orange jitter licks flicker up his own legs; cup blank, feet never leave the spot, nothing on the ground.

Standing tall on one foot with the other tucked, beak open in an astonished coo and one wing half-raised as if checking whether this is really allowed, eye enormous and shining with pure disbelief. Three gold bottlecaps and a chip arrive in a tight ring that overlaps his chest and wings, nothing further out than half a body width — delight at being chosen, never appetite.

A full human-sized umbrella, blown out with its ribs folded inward, has come to rest ON him: the crook of the handle hooked over his back between the wings, the shaft lying along his spine, the canopy tipped over his skull like a roof no wider than about 1.3x his own width. He does not look up — chest out, eye to camera, bone dry and entirely smug, with rain skidding off the canopy edge only; no storm drain, no dry circle, no ground.

Braced low with both wings mantled UP and FORWARD over the crown, wrists meeting above the skull into a feathered roof — never crossed in front of the chest — head pulled down between the shoulders, one eye peeking out from under a wing edge, tail splayed for balance. A bright blue-violet dome snaps tight around him with rain streaking off its curve; no shed feathers anywhere.

Frozen rigid, neck periscoped straight up and beak pointed at the sky, one foot still lifted mid-step, neck hackles ruffed out into a collar, the visible eye huge and white-ringed. A gull's wing shadow crosses his chest, neck and one wing and stops dead at his outline — none of it falls on the ground.

Sprinting flat out with his wings hammering the air and still not lifting off — that failure is the joke — beak wide open, neck stretched dead ahead, coral feet a blur. Short red speed streaks and two shed feathers trail off his tail, and a small wordless shock burst sits tight above his crown, touching it; no lettering, no punctuation marks.

HIS FRAME ALONE: up on his toes in a full courting strut with the iridescent neck inflated into a glossy green-violet balloon bigger than his own head, beak open in a triumphant coo, tail fanned and dragging low, wings only slightly out and DOWN — never thrown up into a V. A little confetti of loose down drifts close around his shoulders, overlapping the body.

Flat on his back with both stiff coral feet straight up and one crossed over the other, wings splayed loose to either side, beak ajar and both eyes shut into blissful half-moons — he reads less knocked out than suspiciously comfortable, like a pigeon sunbathing on purpose. Stars circle his head and a little drizzle drifts through; no X eyes, no shed feathers, no asphalt.

Still up on his own two feet but buckling, one foot crossed over the other mid-stagger, neck gone completely rubbery so the head hangs back upside-down over his shoulders, wings drooping loose at his sides. Spiral swirls where his eyes were and stars orbiting the crown — spirals belong to this frame only; no sweeper bristles, no litter, no shed feathers, no ground.

The instant of the burst: a pale grey-white crown of gutter water explodes around him, wings flung up, beak open, eye bulging with pure personal offence, his soaked neck iridescence running down his front like petrol on a puddle. He stays inside the crown, out of play and deeply insulted — nothing sinks, no ripples, no floating feathers, no ground.
