The four live PNGs (idle, crouch, leap, land) are all 191x250 portrait — paint the other fourteen on that same canvas proportion, effects included, and never let a frame go wider than tall or the engine flips to width-sizing and the bird visibly changes size mid-hop. The checkable test: his head is the same pixel height in all 18. If leap is regenerated with the corrected half-open wing arc, regenerate and swap all four live frames together — never mix a new leap with the old three.

CENTRE-ANCHORED, NOT BOTTOM-ANCHORED (the old sheet note had this backwards). The engine centres the sprite on the lane point, so keep the bird's mass at the centre of the painted content in every frame, ko, dizzy and splash included — content above him pushes him below the lane line and content below pushes him up off it.

THERE IS NO GROUND IN A SPRITE. No asphalt, wet concrete, puddles, dry circles, ripples, cast shadows, storm-drain grates, crumbs, salt or scattered litter in any of the 18 — they all survive the magenta cut as floating grey scum under a bird with nothing beneath him. Contact effects that touch his body are correct and wanted: grit off the toes in land, spray off the toes in dash-run, fire licks up his own legs in coffee, the water crown in splash.

COLOUR. Keep the violet half of the neck sheen away from the silhouette edge — ring the neck in slate grey — because a violet pixel touching the background can open a bite in the knockout. No magenta, hot pink or dark blue-violet in any effect: steam is pale blush-cream, the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy’s own, the water crown is pale grey-white. The coral feet and the orange eye ring are the only warm colours on an entirely grey animal and they are the whole read at 59px — keep them saturated.

NO TEXT OR PRINTING ANYWHERE: blank takeaway cup, blank fry cone, blank umbrella, and no '!!' over his head in flee — a wordless shock burst instead. SHED FEATHERS APPEAR IN EXACTLY THREE FRAMES: leap, flee and cheer. Never on a held death frame, where drifting debris reads as plucking and injury.

SIZE JOKE RUNS IN REVERSE FOR HIM. The engine draws every character at one height, so sell 'small bird' through the props: the takeaway cup is nearly as tall as he is, the fry cone reaches his chest, and the umbrella is a full human one that swamps him. Do not paint him smaller to make the point — it does nothing.

crow.stance: Ground-standing two-legged bird — horizontal body carried level over two scaly feet, three-quarter to camera facing right, hopping rather than walking, wings acting as arms and never as hands; he is never "four-square" and never stands upright like a raccoon.
crow.wardrobe: No costume and no permanent prop — nothing is worn in any frame; the only constants are black plumage with an oil-slick blue-green sheen, shaggy throat hackles, a cool pale blue-grey rim light down the top and back edge, and the full-saturation gold-amber eye on the camera. Frame-local props exist in exactly six frames and touch his body in every one: the dull gold bottlecap (sit, magnet, dizzy, splash), the paper fry carton (eat), the torn takeaway cup (coffee), the found umbrella (umbrella), the single chip (shield).
crow.anatomy: A crow has no hands, so the bill and one pinning foot do every job Jimothy's paws did — nothing is ever held in a free limb; props are stood on, mantled over, or gripped in the beak. The wings are the arms but they only travel up, out, and forward-mantled over the crown: a wrist may fold across the top of the head, but a wing never crosses the chest, never points, and never carries. The legs bend the bird way — the visible joint is an ankle that folds backward — so he can loaf, squat and fold his feet up beside his own flanks, but he can never stick straight human legs out in front of him. He stands on two feet, so "four-square" applies to no frame on this sheet, and the gold-amber eye finds the camera in all eighteen, including the two where he is on his back.

frames.desc: Standing squarely on both feet, three-quarter to camera facing right, wings folded tight so the oil-slick blue-green sheen runs across the coverts and the nape hackles sit slightly ruffled. Head level, beak straight out, gold-amber eye locked on the viewer — calm, unhurried, absolutely taking notes; nothing whatsoever painted beneath the feet, not asphalt, not shadow, not grit.

Sunk into a loaf on nothing at all: feet vanished up under the belly feathers, body one rounded black cushion, neck gone into the shoulders, rain beading and running off his back. Sheltered under his own breast is a single dull gold bottlecap he is keeping dry — his entire fortune — and one half-lidded gold eye still finds the camera. This is the quiet, sad frame of the sheet.

Head cranked low over a spilled paper fry carton with one scaly foot planted flat on top of it, pinning it the way crows actually do, three fries already jammed crosswise in the bill while he tugs a fourth free. Every loose fry stays touching the carton mouth or his own toes — none scattered on the ground — and one gold eye rolls up to the camera, daring you to come closer.

Body dropped horizontal over deeply flexed legs, plumage slicked tight so the silhouette narrows to a loaded dart, tail angled down, wings cracked open a hand's width at the wrists. Head thrust forward and low, beak level, eye wide and fixed dead ahead: all spring, no lift yet.

Airborne and climbing, wings beating down and forward in a tight half-spread with the primaries fanned but the whole span held inside about 1.4x his body height, feet folded back under the tail. Chest thrown toward the camera, beak slightly parted, gold eye on the viewer — no trailing feather, no spray, nothing left behind him.

Wings cupped hard forward to brake with the tail fanned wide beneath as an airbrake, both feet thrown out ahead and the toes spread to grab. Head already coming back up and the eye forward on the next row, with a small tight crown of water droplets bursting right at the toes — contact spray touching the feet only, no puddle and no cast shadow under him.

Mid two-footed side-hop travelling right, both feet together and just clear, body low and level, wings tucked but flicked half-open at the wrists for balance with the tail flared to steer. Head stays square to the camera even as the body travels sideways — cocky, watching you the whole way across; nothing asymmetric anywhere in the frame so this one mirrors cleanly.

A grounded full-tilt bounding scramble — both feet slapping forward together, wings hammering a hard downbeat that half-lifts him and never quite gets him up, body stretched long and level, tail flared for steering. He does NOT fly: the joke is a city crow too heavy with chips to get airborne, so wings stay short of full extension, spray is two small bursts at the wingtips and feet, and streaks run no longer than half his body.

Feet planted and going absolutely nowhere, one foot clamped on the rim of a torn-open takeaway cup tipped in against his chest, bill up, beak parted, wired to the eyeballs and holding still. Every feather bristled, hackles standing straight up, pupil pinned to a black dot inside the gold iris, jitter lines shivering off the whole body and pale blush-cream steam curling tight off the cup — warm cream, never pink.

Wings tented forward and down in the full crow mantle, but the face is pure astonishment — beak wide in a delighted caw, both gold eyes huge, head lifted: things are coming TO him and he cannot believe his luck. Fries and gold bottlecaps arrive in a close ring that overlaps his wings and body, on warm gold-cream trails no longer than half a body width; nothing streaks in from off past the edges.

Standing bone dry and deeply smug on one foot with the other tucked up into the belly, feathers perfectly smooth, under a blown-out found umbrella whose bent ribs lean against his own shoulder — the prop touches him, and there is no curb and no ground anywhere. Canopy tilted low and back so his body stays the centre of mass, faded teal-and-ochre fabric (never pink), rain running off the rim in short strings well inside the frame, head tilted at the camera: yes, this is mine now.

One wing hooked up and over the crown as a roof of feathers while the OTHER stays mantled down over a single chip he flatly refuses to abandon — this is the crow's own solve, never the two-wings-over-the-face the other birds use. A bright blue-violet dome flares tight around him with rain streaking off the curve, two or three loose black feathers knocked free and hanging over his own outline, one gold eye glaring out from under the wrist; feet braced, no skid marks, no road.

Crouched low with the head cranked straight up at the sky, beak wide open in an alarm caw, nape and throat hackles flared into a spiky ruff. Wings half-lifted off the body ready to bail, tail clamped hard down, both eyes huge — a crow being bullied by a bird with worse manners.

Panicked half-flying scramble travelling left: feet still pedalling, wings beating badly out of sync, body tipped forward past its own balance, beak open mid-caw. Warm red-orange speed streaks kept to half his body length behind him and a thin trail of three or four shed black feathers overlapping his own outline — no floating symbols, no exclamation marks, no lettering of any kind.

Head thrown all the way back, chest arched forward, beak wide in a rattling caw with the shaggy throat hackles flared out into a beard — the crow's own cheer, not the gull's shriek and not the pigeon's balloon. Both wings go UP but crooked hard at the wrist so the tips stay inside about 1.15x his idle height, tail fanned, one foot lifted in a little hop, and two loose feathers popping free BELOW the wingtips so nothing adds height.

On his back and rolled slightly toward the camera, legs bent with both tarsi folded to one side and the toes curled loose in the air, one wing flopped up across his own face because he cannot bear to be seen like this. The other wing lies limp on the near side, beak open, and one gold eye peeks out from under the wrist while pale stars circle the head — dazed and mortified, wounded pride only; no X eyes, no spirals, no loose feathers.

Sat back on his rump with both legs bent the bird way — tarsi folded so the feet come back up beside his own flanks, toes curled loose, knees buried in the belly feathers — and both wings drooping off the shoulders like empty sleeves. Head lolling onto one shoulder, beak hanging open, gold eyes spiralled, and three tiny gold bottlecaps wobbling in a close orbit around his head instead of stars; no wing over the face, no loose feathers.

Caught in the instant of the burst — a white and pale-blue crown of water exploding up around him, wings out and up in an appalled shrug, beak wide, both gold eyes outraged, soaked to half his own width with the feathers plastered to a scrawny pencil neck and knobbly bare legs. One gold bottlecap is still pinched in the tip of his bill, because the water got the bird but not the treasure; he is inside the burst and never under it, and nothing sinks.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND IN ANY FRAME. Struck from the draft: wet asphalt (idle, run-r), the curb (sit, umbrella), fries scattered on the ground (eat), puddles (dash-run), skid marks on wet road (shield), and every cast shadow. The four existing paintings need the same pass — assets/chars/crow/idle.png has a small grey grit island at the bottom right that will cut out as its own floating sprite; clean it. CONTACT effects that touch the body are correct and wanted: the droplet crown at the toes in land, the spray bursts at wingtips and feet in dash-run, the water crown in splash.

ENVELOPE AND SCALE. The four existing paintings are all exactly 219x242 px, aspect 0.905, three-quarter facing right — that box IS the anchor. Paint the other 14 into it and match camera, lighting and head size exactly, or repaint all 18 in one sitting; never mix two sittings. Every frame including its effects must land between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x that box, and the one checkable test is that his HEAD is the same number of pixels in all 18. Wingspan capped at roughly 1.4x body height in leap, land, dash-run and flee; cheer wingtips inside 1.15x idle height. Paint cheer, magnet and umbrella first and cut-test them at 59px — those three are the envelope risks.

COLOUR AT 59px. He is a near-black bird on a dark lane, so the cool pale blue-grey rim down the top and back edge plus the full-saturation gold-amber eye ARE the silhouette; without them he is a hole in the road. The cutter deletes the magenta family, so: coffee steam is pale blush-cream with the green channel up around 150+, never pink; the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy’s own.

LOOSE BLACK FEATHERS are capped at three frames — shield, flee and cheer only. Ko and dizzy get none: on a frame held 1.55 seconds under a camera lean, drifting feathers accumulate into a plucked, injured read, which is the opposite of funny-sad. Leap also loses the trailing feather it had in the draft.

DELIBERATE RECONCILIATION ON THE TWO DEATH FRAMES. The reviewer notes on dizzy and on ko both asked for a wing across the face, which would have made the two 1.55s frames the same silhouette under the same camera treatment. The wing-over-face is assigned to KO alone (on his back, wounded pride, pale circling stars, one eye peeking); dizzy keeps the corrected bent-tarsus rump sit with empty-sleeve wings, spiral eyes and three orbiting bottlecaps. Spirals never appear on ko, stars never on dizzy, and the two silhouettes — a rolled bundle versus an upright slump — read apart instantly.

LAYOUT AND ENGINE FOLLOW-UP. Lay out in rows of three or four with hand-drawn dividers and generous gaps, never an even grid; a shaved primary reads as a broken bird, not a fast one. Nothing touches a frame edge or a divider, and every detached element (stars, orbiting caps, streaks, incoming fries) must sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box. Once the art lands, the roster entry at index.html line 699 needs full:1 alongside art:1 or all 14 new poses fold straight back onto idle/crouch/leap/land — and keep this bird visually distinct from sprites/haz-crowdive.png, the diving crow hazard.

seagull.stance: Bipedal bird: upright on two pale-orange webbed feet at rest, never on all fours — "four-square" is a quadruped word and does not apply to him in any frame.
seagull.wardrobe: No clothing at all — his costume is ONE stolen french fry: crosswise in the yellow bill in idle, sit, eat (mid-swallow), crouch, land, run-r, dash-run, shield and dizzy; pinned under his LEFT webbed foot in coffee, umbrella and magnet; detached but still overlapping him in cheer (tossed), scared (falling), ko (lying by his bill) and splash (streaming off); absent ONLY from leap, deliberately. Other props, all completely BLANK — no logo, letters or numbers, ever: a red-and-white fry carton (eat, magnet, flee, splash), a plain black umbrella (umbrella), a plain takeaway cup (coffee).
seagull.anatomy: He has no hands, so every raccoon "hold" is re-solved three ways: the bill grips, a webbed foot pins, and anything too big to grip is bitten high on the shaft so it rests on the body. Wing arc is strict — up, out and forward-mantled over the crown only; a wing never crosses in front of the chest, never points, never holds and never props him up. He stands on two legs, so rest is a one-legged hunch or a folded crouch, never a lap and never all fours. Body lock from the four existing PNGs: tall and narrow beside Jimothy's sphere, slate mantle, black wingtips with white mirrors, yellow bill with the red gonys spot, pale-orange webbed feet, short stubby tail, dark eye — same head size in all eighteen frames.

frames.desc: Standing square on both pale-orange webbed feet, wings folded tight with the black primaries crossed over the stubby tail, neck drawn in against the drizzle. One stolen fry clamped crosswise in the yellow bill, dark eye locked dead on camera with absolutely no guilt in it — and no pavement under him.

The gull's own rest, not a loaf: up on ONE leg with the other foot drawn into his breast feathers, body hunched, rain beading along the mantle, eye half-lidded and looking at nothing in particular. The fry is still crosswise in his bill, unstarted — he is not eating it because when it is gone the day is over.

One webbed foot planted flat on the tipped blank carton, head thrown all the way back over his spine, bill wide, a whole fry going down vertically with the throat visibly bulging. Wings cracked a few inches for balance and one eye rolled down at the viewer mid-swallow — caught, and entirely unbothered; nothing scattered loose off the body.

Compressed low and forward, tarsi folded, breast almost down to his own toes, wings cracked open a few inches to unlock, tail cocked, neck thrust out and eye fixed far ahead. Fry still crosswise in the bill, with a first flick of grit and water kicking off the webbed toes and staying tight to the feet.

A WIDE, slightly swept glide-dive: span held horizontal and angled forward with the wrists swept back so the whole shape sits about 1.3 wide to 1 tall, body and head large and unmistakable dead centre, bill level, feet tucked back. Absolutely nothing carried, no shed feathers, no spray — this same PNG is the diving-gull hazard at 69px and mirrors by direction, so it must read as one clean incoming bird and carry nothing shaped like a pickup.

Feet thrown forward with the webbed toes splayed wide, wings cupped forward to air-brake, tail fanned down like a flap, head coming back up as the weight settles — and the fry still in his bill, which is the whole joke. A tight white-and-cyan burst bites up around his own feet only: no puddle, no ring on the floor, no pavement.

Side-on to the right in the ridiculous flat-out gull waddle-run: body horizontal, neck stretched forward like an arrow, both wings half-open for balance, orange feet a paddling blur, fry trailing horizontally from the bill. Deliberately symmetric — nothing side-specific in this frame, because the engine mirrors it to make run-l.

The same waddle at absolute maximum, wings caught at the bottom of a full power-stroke and STILL not airborne — the bird who could just fly and somehow never does — feet skimming, eye wide, pupil a pinprick, fry pinned flat back along his cheek by the wind. Three short white speed streaks, a low spray off the heels and two shed down feathers, all held inside the idle box.

Feet planted and holding perfectly still while everything else vibrates: the takeaway cup pinched by its rim in his bill and tipped fully upside down, lid popped, the lot going down in one. Crown feathers straight up in a startled crest, pupil shrunk to a dot, pale blush-cream steam (never pink), short orange fire licks and jitter ticks right at his feet — and the fry pinned under his left foot even now.

Head back, bill wide in a delighted open-billed scream, wings half-raised and cupped forward as if gathering it all in, every feather fluffed with sheer astonishment — the best day of his life. Fries, gold bottlecaps and one small tumbling carton spiral in TIGHT, every piece overlapping his silhouette and none more than half a body width out; the fry stays pinned under his left foot.

A cheap black umbrella bitten by the SHAFT high up, just under the canopy, so it roofs his skull like a hat with the handle dangling loose past his breast and rain sheeting off the rim in a short curtain that never leaves the canopy. Bone dry, wings folded, eye half-lidded and insufferably smug, fry pinned under his left foot because the bill is busy — nothing jammed into a grate, nothing on the floor.

His own solve and no other bird's: turned side-on into the weather with one shoulder driven straight into the blast, wings clamped hard to the body, head low, feet braced, fry held dead level in the bill and completely unmoved. A blue-violet dome flares around him with a hot white spot where the hit landed and rain raking off it — never violet, never dark.

Even gulls have a gull: the hard-edged shadow of a much bigger, meaner one falls across his back, breast and half his face, painted only where it lands on his body. Neck fully periscoped, bill open in a squawk of pure indignation, eyes rolled up, wings half-lifted and shivering — and the fry has finally slipped, caught mid-fall an inch below his bill with one sharp exclamation tick beside his head.

Full panic sprint to the left, body low and horizontal, neck stretched, both wings hammering, webbed feet a blur — with the ENTIRE blank red-and-white carton clamped in his bill, because he grabbed the whole thing on the way out. Red-orange speed streaks and one or two shed feathers rake off his tail, kept tight to the body.

The gull long call, which belongs to him alone: chest thrown out, head thrown right back over the spine, bill wide in a full-throated shriek at the rain, wings held low and slightly out — never a raised V, that is the other birds. One fry flips end over end just above his crown and overlapping his head, a few chip fragments falling close beside him, warm gold rim-light on his outline instead of a background sunbreak.

Down on his right side, right wing pinned under him, left flopped over his flank, both legs out together with the toes curled, bill hanging open. Eyes are swooning half-moon lids with small gold stars circling tight above his head, and the fry lies one beak-length from that open bill, uneaten — he went out reaching for it.

Folded down onto his rump with both legs splayed out in front like a dropped toy, wings limp at his sides, head lolling back, little pink tongue out and spiral eyes (spirals are dizzy's alone — no stars in this frame). The fry hangs half out of the drooping bill by one end, a wobble arc either side of his head, and the whole silhouette is deliberately nothing like ko's.

Swept hard sideways by the burst: a bright blue-violet crown explodes at his chest and shoves him off downstream, body angled with the flow, one wing braced uselessly against it and the other thrown up, soaked through, eye locked on camera and deeply offended. The blank carton tumbles away just ahead of his bill with two fries in the spray, everything still overlapping him and clear of the frame edge — no water surface, no kerb, no grate anywhere.

Contact effects only: the burst at his own feet, grit off his toes, spray off his heels.

The one checkable test: his HEAD must be the same number of pixels in all eighteen. If an effect shrinks the head, the effect is too big. Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for a cut before the other fifteen.

leap HAS TWO JOBS — it is also the diving-gull hazard for the whole game, drawn at 69px and flipped by travel direction. Wide swept glide, body centred, and no fry or food-coloured object in it, or the game shows players a bird carrying the pickup and teaches them to chase the thing that kills them.

COLOUR LAW: the knockout eats the magenta family. Steam is pale blush-cream, the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. The carton stays plain red-and-white and BLANK — no logo, no numbers, no lettering anywhere on the sheet.

PALETTE AND SCALE LOCK from the four existing PNGs (idle, crouch, leap, land): slate mantle, black wingtips with white mirrors, yellow bill with the red gonys spot, pale-orange webbed feet, dark eye, short stubby tail. Match idle's head size exactly — he reads tall and narrow next to Jimothy, never smaller. Shed feathers appear in dash-run and flee only, never on the held frames.

opossum.stance: Quadruped: four-square at rest on flat plantigrade paws, heel down and five long spread fingers, and he only frees his forepaws by sitting back onto his rump — never by standing upright like a person.
opossum.wardrobe: In all eighteen frames: a faded orange hi-vis night-crew vest, always on and hanging open, two silver reflective bands with the lower one peeling on his LEFT side; a blank unlettered laminated badge on a lanyard on his LEFT chest; a dented steel thermos clipped to the vest on a short cord at his RIGHT hip. Nothing else, and nothing ever comes off.
opossum.anatomy: The prehensile tail is his spare hand and it does every job Jimothy does with a free paw, but it is anchored at the rump and only about body-length: sat back, it can reach forward between his hind feet to his own chest, or run up his spine to just behind his ears — it can never hold anything over the head of a stretched-out quadruped. Like the raccoon he is plantigrade: flat palms, five spread fingers, heel down, opposable rear thumb on the hind foot; no knuckle-walking anywhere. Reared frames sit back on the rump with both hind feet flat, which frees both forepaws honestly and keeps the tail free as a third hand rather than a fifth leg. His head must be the same pixel size in all eighteen frames, so the reared frames have to reach the same head height as the four-square ones.

frames.desc: Three-quarter quadruped foreshortened toward the camera so he stays taller than wide, four-square on flat palms, pale pointed face, pink nose, black bead eyes, nicked left ear. Tail curled under and around beside him in a tight S that touches his flank the whole way; vest hanging open with the peeling band on his left, blank badge swinging on its lanyard, thermos clipped at his right hip.

Sat back on his rump, hind feet flat, forepaws folded on his belly, ears down and eyelids at half mast, looking at nothing at the end of the shift. Tail coiled beside him in a flat spiral resting against his own foot, vest slumped open, badge hanging dead still, the dented thermos tipped empty against his thigh.

Sat back on his rump with a to-go tub of cold clam chowder brought up to his chest by the tail, which comes forward between his hind feet and wraps the tub twice. Both forepaws work a little plastic fork, cheeks packed, eyes squeezed shut with contentment, a chowder smear on his chin and one oyster cracker balanced on the blank badge; thermos at his hip.

Flattened right down on all fours, staged three-quarter and foreshortened toward the camera so the box stays tall, elbows out, haunches up, nicked ear pinned flat, eyes locked dead forward past the viewer. Tail swept around beside him in a shallow arc touching his flank rather than trailing straight back, vest bunched over his shoulders, thermos pressed flat to his ribs.

Fully airborne, all four legs splayed wide, pale belly turned to the viewer, mouth open in a delighted little gape. Tail whipped into a full loop that stays inside his own silhouette, thick and fully opaque with the tip tucked back toward his hip and never thinning to a wisp; vest ridden up around his ribs, badge and thermos flung out on their cords but still overlapping his body.

Front paws planted flat, spine bowed, hindquarters still dropping, whiskers thrown forward, eyes wide with the impact. His tail slaps down and throws a tight spray fan that touches only his tail and paws — no puddle and no road under him — while the reflective bands buckle across his chest and the thermos bounces off the vest.

Side-on bounding gallop to the right showing his RIGHT flank, body stretched long but head lifted and the tail curled up in an arc over his rump rather than streaming back, so the frame stays taller than wide. Hind feet gathered under him with the rear thumb splayed, thermos swinging forward on its cord, the badge swung across from his far side and blank on both faces.

Flat-out four-legged bound, legs at maximum stretch and still visibly not very fast, eyes huge and ears back. Exactly one trailing element: a single short arc of coffee no longer than his own tail, curving up into the box from the popped thermos cap still dangling on its cord — plus two small fire licks under his belly and nothing else behind him.

A STANDING frame, held up to seven seconds: sat back on his rump with both hind feet planted flat and absolutely still, wired to the eyeballs, tail brought up to grip the dented thermos upright while both forepaws clamp the little screw-cap cup at his chin. Pinprick pupils, fur bristled along his spine, whiskers in tight jitter arcs, steam painted pale blush-cream and never pink, two fire licks at his planted feet.

Sat back on his rump with the tail brought forward between his hind feet and curled into a scoop at his chest, already heaped with gold bottlecaps, mouth open and eyes round with astonishment that things are coming TO him. A tight inward spiral of more caps and stray fries curls in close around his shoulders, every one overlapping his silhouette and none near the frame edge; vest pockets brimming.

Sat back on his haunches so tail root and skull are close together, the tail running up his own spine to hook a small black umbrella just behind his ears with the canopy tipped FORWARD, so the dry zone covers his head and chest and his tail root is the wet bit. Both forepaws free and deeply smug — one tucked in the vest pocket, one cradling the thermos — blank badge hanging dry against his chest, rain sheeting off the canopy edges in short strokes that stop well inside the margin and never reach the ground.

The flinch: crouched low with both forepaws crossed over his face and one black eye squinting through the gap, tail clamped tight around his own ankle. A bright blue-violet dome — never violet — flares white at the point of impact just clear of his back, and inside it the reflective bands are the brightest thing on him, the blank badge flipped up and hanging on its lanyard, thermos swung out against the vest.

Reared back on his rump with the enormous opossum gape cranked wide open — teeth rounded off, no drool, no snarl — eyes rolled up and back with the whites showing in pure panic. Fur puffed out, forepaws clutched tight to his chest, tail stiff and curved up close behind his back, badge flipped up and stuck in his chin fur clear of his face; his scariest face is an obvious bluff and everyone can tell.

Sprinting left with everything he has, legs blurred into a scribble, mouth open in a panicked wail, vest flapping with the thermos and blank badge swinging wild. Two short red speed streaks and two fat exclamation marks sit close behind his shoulders overlapping his body — no skid mark, no ground, nothing touching the edge.

Reared up tall on his rump with both forepaws punched skyward but bent at the elbow so they stay inside the box, tail thrown into a triumphant question-mark curl beside his head rather than above it, mouth wide in the same huge gape — joyful this time. Reflective bands blazing, badge swinging, a low tight arc of gold bottlecaps around his shoulders, none of them near the frame edge.

Playing dead and badly overselling it: flopped on his side with the spine curled into a compact C, legs stiff and curled in the air, tongue lolled out over his teeth, tail curled up over his flank, one eye squeezed shut and the other cracked open a slit peeking straight at the viewer. Stars circle his head and two small green stink curls rise tight off his flank; vest twisted up under his shoulders with one band catching the streetlight, blank badge lying face up beside his ear on its lanyard, thermos rolled to a stop against his back.

On his back, all four feet up in the air, tail flopped in a loose corkscrew across his own chest, vest twisted around backwards with one reflective band still showing. Spiral eyes and tongue flopped sideways, wet leaves and brush bristles stuck ON him — snagged in the vest, caught in the tail, one draped over his snout — with two more circling his head in place of stars; this is the one time he genuinely was not faking it.

The instant of the burst: soaked through with his fur plastered flat so he looks half his usual size, forepaws thrown up, mouth open in a shocked gape, tail hanging like a wet rope against his leg. A white and pale-cyan crown of water explodes around his middle with the droplets kept well inside the margin, and the vest is a sodden dark orange rag with both bands still showing — he is startled, not going anywhere under the surface.

sheetNotes: FOUR FRAMES ALREADY SHIP AND THEY HAVE NO COSTUME. assets/chars/opossum/{idle,crouch,leap,land}.png are live at 216x250 and show a bare animal — no vest, no badge, no thermos. Repaint all eighteen together and replace them; fourteen vested frames delivered beside four bare ones means he puts a vest on and takes it off mid-hop. Landing the full set also ends his folded 4-frame status, which switches the engine's stand-in effects OFF (the flashing '!', the orange speed lines on flee/dash/coffee, the ko tip-over spin), so every one of those has to be painted in.

KEEP EVERY FRAME UNDER 1.12 ASPECT — target the shipped 216x250 box, about 0.86. At exactly 1.12 the engine flips from sizing by height (59px) to sizing by width (74px) and the sprite visibly jumps size mid-animation. Effects, spray and stars all count toward the box. Check it by head size: his head is the same number of pixels in all eighteen.

THE TAIL IS ALREADY FAILING THE CUT. In the three shipped frames the thin pink tail has broken into floating fragments — a severed pink shard in crouch.png and leap.png, and a stray dark blob plus a pink shard sitting off in the top-left corner of land.png, which also drags the centre-anchored body off its lane line. Paint the tail thick and fully opaque, in contact with the body silhouette along its whole visible length, and never taper it to a wispy translucent tip against the background.

COLOUR LAW. Paint the tail, nose and ears a warm salmon or putty pink with the BLUE channel kept low — a mauve or lilac pink falls inside the magenta knockout (high red, low green, high blue) and gets bitten away in ragged chunks. Same law: coffee steam is pale blush-cream and never hot pink, the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy’s own and.

NO GROUND IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. No wet asphalt, no puddles, no dry ring under the umbrella, no skid mark behind the flee, no cast shadows, no leaves or litter lying on the floor — all of it survives the cut as floating grey scum under a character with nothing beneath him. Contact spray that touches his paws, tail or belly is fine and correct.

THE BADGE CARRIES NO LETTERS IN ANY FRAME, EVER. Blank laminate: a scuffed photo shape, a colour bar, a worn corner. It shows in both run frames, and lettering is illegible at 59px and mirrors into gibberish. Nothing else on the sheet gets words either — not the vest, not the thermos, not the chowder tub.
opossum.runL: Paint it separately: run-r shows his RIGHT flank, run-l shows his LEFT — where the badge, lanyard, peeling reflective band and nicked ear all live — so a mirror puts every one of them on the wrong side, and the engine does not mirror full characters at all, meaning a missing run-l drops him to the procedural blob on every leftward hop.

soggy.stance: Hunched quadruped raccoon: four-square on all fours at rest and in every travel frame, rearing back onto his hind legs (tripod, stubby tail counterweighting) for any frame that needs a free forepaw — never a full human upright.
soggy.wardrobe: ALL 18 FRAMES: the folded newspaper hat (fold points to his right; print is fine grey column TEXTURE, never a legible word) plus a live drip line coming off him somewhere. Per-frame props, and nothing else ever: soggy cardboard fry tray (eat, magnet), takeaway cup (coffee), crook-handled umbrella (umbrella).
soggy.anatomy: Jimothy's own body under the water: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high on the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a STUBBY ringed tail that hangs or holds short — it never streams, never flicks a rope of water and never fans a wake. He is plantigrade in every single frame including both runs, the leap and the landing: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down, never a knuckle. Standing rules: he is four-square only when nothing is in his paws, and the instant a prop appears he is up on his hind legs — no frame gets a fifth limb. Soaked-fur clumping and the hat's slump state are the only things allowed to change across the sheet; his height, head size and silhouette mass are identical in all 18.

frames.desc: Standing four-square facing camera exactly as the existing master, weight even, soaked fur clumped into dark dripping spikes, the newspaper hat still holding its crisp fold. A small contented smile while drips hang and fall from his chin, elbows and hat brim — no puddle, no wet mark, nothing at all under his paws.

Sitting up on his haunches, forepaws folded on a soaked belly, water still wringing out of his chest fur in one thin steady thread. The hat has slumped a quarter turn so the brim rests across one eyebrow and he doesn't fix it — he just watches the rain over the camera's shoulder, content and a little alone. This is the quiet frame. No puddle beneath him.

Sitting with a rain-collapsed cardboard fry tray wedged against his shin and belly so it physically touches him, holding one fry up in both flat forepaws; it has gone so soft it folds double before it reaches his mouth and he watches it bend with genuine admiration. A thin stream drools off the hat brim straight down into the tray, topping it back up.

Flattened low on all fours as in the existing master, haunches up, elbows out, coiled to spring, water sheeting off his back and shedding down his flanks in short runnels that stay on the fur. The hat has slid forward into a wet paper visor and he peers out from under it, eyes locked up-screen; nothing pools between his paws.

Fully airborne, limbs spread wide, flat palms open, belly forward and delighted, throwing a tight fan of droplets off his fur that stays inside the reach of his own limbs. Stubby ringed tail short and straight behind him; the hat has lifted a finger's width off his skull by one corner, still attached by sheer sogginess.

Front paws slammed flat, body low, spine compressed, whiskers forward, a contact crown of splash bursting up around all four feet and rising no higher than his knees. The hat drops back onto his brow with a fresh slap of water off the brim; his eyes are wide and pleased.

Side-on sprint to the right, body low, legs at full extension, flat palms reaching, stubby ringed tail held short and level with two or three beads flicking off its tip — no rope, no wrung-mop trail. The hat streams back tight against his skull with one corner unfolded into a short curled ribbon flapping against his ear; hat print is grey column texture only.

Flat-out sprint, legs at maximum stretch, eyes wide, no fire on this one — a short dirty rooster tail of gutter water breaks off his heels and dies within half a body width, and the rain flashes into thin white steam off his shoulders where he is moving too fast for it to land. The hat is pinned flat to his skull, its column texture stretched taut.

STANDING STILL and vibrating: reared on his hind legs, both feet planted, both forepaws clamped around a takeaway cup the rain has already refilled past the lid, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, soaked fur bristled into spikes. Pale blush-cream steam off the cup, short jitter lines either side of him and a couple of warm orange fire licks tight at his feet — even the drip hanging off his chin is vibrating.

Reared up hugging the rain-collapsed fry tray to his chest, mouth open, eyes bright with pure astonishment that for once things are coming TO him. Gold bottlecaps spiral in on a warm amber ribbon that stays within half a body width and overlaps his shoulder, and the wet hat's ink has begun to run — one dark blue-black streak painting down his cheek like a happy tear.

Reared on his hind legs, one flat forepaw gripping the crook of an open umbrella held close over his skull, rain hammering the canopy and shedding off both edges in short curtains no wider than the canopy itself. He is still wringing wet and still dripping, but the hat is gently steaming as it finally begins to dry and his smile is quiet and enormously smug — no puddle, no dry patch of ground.

The instant of impact: crouched low, forepaws thrown up flat-palmed, eyes squeezed shut, chin tucked — and just as soaked as every other frame, same dark dripping fur spikes, same sagging hat, nothing dries. A bright blue-violet dome snaps up tight around him with rain shattering off the outside, while the water it knocks loose hangs inside the dome as a rimlit burst of droplets and a hard blue-white edge light runs the length of his near side.

Reared on his hind legs, both forepaws clutched to his chest, ears flat back, eyes enormous and fixed on something above the frame; the hat brim has flopped up on its own, so the full downpour is now hitting him square in the face. Water runs into his open, worried mouth and he does not move to stop it.

Sprinting left flat out, mouth open in panic, two small red '!!' strokes stamped in the air right beside his ear and overlapping his head, a short tight burst of filthy gutter spray off his heels. The hat has torn half off and is pinned by one soaked corner against his shoulder rather than trailing — and even now the corner of his mouth is still trying to smile.

Reared tall on his hind legs, one arm punched to the sky, mouth open in a shout of pure joy; the newspaper hat has just left his fingertips and spins at head height, overlapping his raised paw, its droplet halo kept inside the hat's own arc. Underneath, the revealed head fur is a flattened, comically wet little dome.

Flat on his back, all four legs up with flat pads to the sky and the drips now running off his upturned palms, a ring of gold stars circling his head and swooning half-moon lids on the eye that shows. The hat has landed over his face like a little pitched paper roof, headline band up and brim tented off his nose, one dazed happy eye peeking through a torn column — quietly pleased to finally be lying down. Nothing spreads beneath him.

Sprawled on his side, spiral eyes, tongue lolling, stars orbiting his head, the hat spun down over one ear at a drunk angle. Ink from the soaked newsprint runs down both cheeks in two long dark blue-black spiral smears that match his eyes exactly, and a last fat drip swings off his ear.

Caught in the burst: arms thrown straight up, flat palms spread, eyes bulging, mouth wide in shock as a crown of pale blue-white water erupts around him and blows him backwards — nothing sinking, nothing going under. The hat has finally given up and gone to warm-grey pulp, sliding down his brow in soft ribbons, and under it he is unmistakably still smiling. Wettest he has ever been.

sheetNotes: ENVELOPE AND THE HEAD TEST. Every frame, water included, lands between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside roughly the 250x243 box the four existing masters already use. The checkable rule: his HEAD is the same number of pixels in all 18 — if an effect shrinks the head, the effect is too big. leap, cheer, land and splash are the blowout risks. Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for a 59px lane cut before committing the other fifteen.

NO GROUND, ANYWHERE — this is the biggest change from the old brief. The puddles under idle, sit, umbrella and ko are DELETED; the sprite is cut off magenta and floats over lane art, so a painted puddle, damp smear or cast shadow survives as grey scum under a raccoon standing on nothing. Drips off chin and paws, sheeting runnels on the fur, and the contact splash crowns at his feet in land and splash all touch the body and are correct. A puddle never is.

DETACHED ELEMENTS STAY CLOSE AND OVERLAPPING. The magnet bottlecaps, the flee '!!' strokes and the thrown cheer hat must each sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, or the cutter emits them as separate sprites and the wider crop shrinks him. Nothing touches a frame edge or a divider line — leave a clear magenta margin all the way round every cell.

NO LETTERS. The newsprint is texture only: fine grey ruled column ticks with a darker banded block where a headline would sit. It reads as 'newspaper' at 59px and it survives the mirror; a real word does not. This applies to idle, sit, dash-run, run-r, ko and splash, which all previously specified readable print.

COLOUR LAW. The knockout eats the magenta family, so: shield dome BRIGHT blue-violet ( Running ink is dark blue-black, never pure black, and wet newsprint grey goes warmer and softer the more it soaks — ink is the only colour allowed to shift across the sheet.

TWO FRAMES ARE DELIBERATELY DRIER AND MUST NOT BE SOAKED BACK DOWN: umbrella (hat steaming, finally drying, standing in his own rain-shadow) and shield (a light trick only — his fur clumping and hat sag are identical to every other frame; the dome sheds water off him, it does not dry him). That contrast is the joke, and shield staying wet is what stops it reading as the wrong sprite popping in for half a second.
soggy.runL: Paint separately — the hat's fold points to his right, the unfolded ribbon flaps off his right ear and the ink streak runs down his right cheek, so a mirror throws all three to the wrong side and reverses the newsprint texture; run-l is the same low sprint reversed with fold, ribbon and streak re-pointed to his left.

nordic.stance: Quadruped: at rest he stands four-square on four flat plantigrade paws, and any frame that needs a hand rears him fully up onto his hind legs — never four-square while holding something, never a half-measure tripod.
nordic.wardrobe: In all 18 frames, exactly two things: the heavy navy fair-isle sweater (cream/red/white horizontal bands with pale-blue flecks, ribbed cuffs ending at the WRIST, ribbed hem to mid-thigh) and the navy knit bobble hat with its red-and-cream band and oversized oatmeal pom — the fries carton (eat), takeaway cup (coffee) and umbrella (umbrella) each appear in one frame only and stay gripped on the body.
nordic.anatomy: Nordic is Jimothy's own body, so every pose transfers one to one: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high on the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a STUBBY ringed tail — never a long streaming trash-panda tail, in any of the eighteen. He is plantigrade: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heels down, and the ribbed cuffs stop at the wrist so the bare dark paws and the short tail below the hem stay readable in every frame (this overrides the old "sleeves swallow his forepaws / every prop handled through a cuff" note, which contradicts all four shipped frames — he grips with bare hands). The sweater is a second body that lags a beat behind him and the pom is the lag weight that sells the timing, but the wool never becomes his hands; the one exception is coffee, where he tugs the cuffs down over his palms as pot-holders with the fingertips still showing. Standing rules a painter must not break: no frame is four-square and holding a prop, the hem never drags on a floor because there is no floor, and the pom never leaves clear margin at the top of the cell.

frames.desc: Standing four-square, three-quarter to camera, the heavy navy fair-isle sweater hanging to mid-thigh, bare dark plantigrade paws flat below the ribbed cuffs, stubby ringed tail low behind the hem. Calm, patient, faintly damp; the oatmeal pom droops to one side like it has given up on the weather.

THE QUIET FRAME. Sitting upright on his haunches with the sweater pooled all around him like a knitted tea cosy, only his bare back toes and the tip of the stubby tail poking out, both paws resting on the woolly belly. Hat slipped low on the brow, eyes half-lidded, waiting out rain he stopped minding hours ago — content, and completely on his own.

Sitting on his haunches with an open plain paper carton of fries hugged against the woolly belly in one paw, the other pinching a fry up to his mouth, cheerfully unbothered. Salt and crumbs caught in the fair-isle bands and two spare fries tucked down inside the ribbed cuff for later — nothing dropped, nothing scattered below him.

Flattened low on all fours, haunches up, the sweater rucked and bunched over his shoulders with the hem crumpled under his chest; flat palms spread, heels down. Hat tipped forward so the pom swings down in front of one eye and he looks past it, forward, ready to go.

Fully airborne, limbs spread wide, belly forward, the sweater ballooned with air like a knitted sail and the hem flared open. Pom lagging just behind the crown of the hat, mouth open in delight, three or four rain flecks and one stray wool fibre kept tight against his back.

Front paws planted flat with the fingers splayed, body low, weight absorbed, the sweater slumping down into a woolly ripple. Pom whips forward over his brow, whiskers forward, a small spray of droplets bursting off the paws themselves — no puddle, no pavement, no cast shadow.

Side-on lolloping sprint to the right, body low, legs extended, bare paws reaching well past the ribbed cuffs. The hem swings opposite to his stride, the pom trails close behind the hat, the stubby tail stays short and level, jaw set with grim Ballard determination.

Flat out to the right, legs at full stretch, the sweater pressed flat against him by the speed with the hem snapping behind. Pom horizontal, eyes wide, three short cream-and-rust speed streaks starting at his tail and stopping well inside the margin, and a thin curl of pale grey steam off the overheating wool.

STANDING FRAME — planted dead still, up on his hind legs with heels flat and knees locked, both sleeve cuffs tugged down over his palms as pot-holders (dark fingertips still poking out) around a plain unbranded cup at chest height. Fur bristling through the knit, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, hat shoved back with the pom standing bolt upright on static, jitter lines at the shoulders, pale steam off the sweater and small orange fire licks right at his feet.

Reared up on his hind legs holding the ribbed hem out with both bare paws like an apron pouch, mouth open in astonishment and pure delight — everything is coming to him and he cannot believe it. Gold bottlecaps and fries spiral in tight on a warm gold-and-cream swirl (never pink) and drop into the wool, two already snagged in the fair-isle.

Reared up on his hind legs, one bare paw gripping the crook of a small compact umbrella held low and tilted back over his shoulder so the canopy sits beside the head rather than above it. Dry and smug from the shoulders up with half-lidded satisfied eyes, but the hem is already dark and heavy with soaked-up water and dripping; rain streaks short and tight to the canopy, nowhere near the cell edge.

Braced and flinching, reared up with both forearms thrown across his face, a blue-violet energy dome snapping shut close around his outline — never violet or purple — with the light catching every strand so the fair-isle pattern glows through. Pom bolt upright with static, rain sliding off the dome, one eye squeezed shut and the other peeking.

Up on his hind legs, both forearms clutched to his chest, ears flat under the hat, eyes huge and locked on something up-screen. The hat has slipped so he is peering out from under the brim, pom quivering, loose wool bristling along his shoulders.

Sprinting left in flat panic, mouth open, hat blown back and hanging off one ear by its brim with the pom bouncing wildly. The hem tangles around his back legs so he is half-tripping as he runs, short rust speed streaks tight behind him and two small exclamation strokes (no letters) close over his head.

Standing tall on his hind legs, one forearm punched up but bent so the paw stays level with the top of the pom, the other paw planted on his woolly hip, mouth open in a whoop. Hat knocked askew, a tight burst of gold confetti and three flecks of wool fluff hanging right against his shoulders — nothing rises above the pom.

Seen from a high three-quarter angle so the frame stays near square: dumped on his back with the body diagonal, all four bare paws in the air, stubby tail pressed flat beneath him, sweater rucked halfway up his chest and the hat slid down over his eyes with the pom flopped beside his head. Mouth open in a stunned little O, five small stars circling above the brim — quietly embarrassed, and privately relieved the sweater took the whole hit.

Sprawled and spun out on his haunches, spiral eyes, tongue out, the hat turned fully backwards so the pom dangles over his nose. The sweater has twisted a quarter turn so the fair-isle yoke sits sideways across one shoulder, and a single loose thread loops out, curls back and ends in a little tangle against his hip — well inside the frame, touching no edge; spirals only, no stars.

The instant of the burst: soaked through, both forearms up, eyes wide, a pale white-green crown of water exploding around his middle so his mass stays centred in it. The knit sags dark and heavy and the hem stretches to just below his feet and no further (1.15x idle height maximum), pom a sodden dripping lump over one ear — mouth open in shock, less worried about the water than about the three days that wool will take to dry.

summer.stance: Quadruped raccoon, plantigrade — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heels down, four-square at rest; he rears onto his haunches ONLY in the six frames that say so (coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer).
summer.wardrobe: In all eighteen frames, no exceptions: the oversized orange-and-cream striped life ring (rope trim, visible valve stem, teal patch repeated on BOTH flanks at the same height) and the orange-framed dark shades. Everything else — popsicle, slush cup, iced coffee, parasol, towel — is a per-frame prop.
summer.anatomy: This is Jimothy's own body, so every hero pose maps one-to-one, but hold the canon: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high on the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY ringed tail that never streams, curls out behind or trails — strike every "streaming tail" from the old draft. Hands are plantigrade raccoon hands, flat palms and spread fingers with the heel down, in every frame including cheer and coffee; no knuckles, no tiptoe. The ring is a rigid torus and never a flat ellipse — highlight along the top curve, shadow tucked under the bottom, valve stem findable — painted at ONE constant outer diameter (about 1.4x his shoulder width, inner hole clearly wider than his shoulders) in all eighteen, so only its position and tilt ever change; if it must read smaller, tilt it into foreshortening, never shrink it. That deliberate oversize is what makes the costume honest: it rests on his barrel at idle only because his stance cocks it there, which is why it can then slide to the armpits, collar the neck, and drop clean to his ankles without him appearing to change size.

frames.desc: Standing four-square three-quarter to camera, weight cocked onto one hip so the oversized ring hangs tilted around his barrel — front edge low, back edge caught on the slope of his shoulders, no paw needed to hold it. Chin lifted, mouth a small satisfied line, shades dead level, one fat drizzle bead sliding down the left lens.

The quiet frame: he has sat straight down through the ring so it collars his hips like a donut chair, hind feet out over the front rim, flat palms folded on the top curve, head tipped back at a sky that is plainly not going to clear. Shades on, contented half-smile going soft at the corners, drizzle beading along the rubber.

Still seated in the ring, leaning on its top curve like a table — a paper cup of blue slush wedged against the rim at his side, a half-melted orange popsicle held up in both flat palms. He is licking a drip off his own wrist, shades on, while the rain melts it faster than any sun would have.

Repaint: coiled low and forward, shoulders down, haunches up, palms and heels flat — the same full-diameter ring has slid up to collar his neck, tipped steeply so it foreshortens into an oval instead of shrinking, squashing his cheeks out either side. Eyes forward over the top of the rubber, shades knocked one degree crooked.

Fully airborne, belly forward, mouth open in a whoop — limbs gathered inside the box rather than stretched flat, forepaws reaching and hind feet trailing close. The ring has ridden up to his armpits and rides the air with him, shades perfectly level, a short arc of water beads flicking off its trailing edge and still touching it.

Front palms slapped down flat with the fingers spread, body low and absorbing, as the ring bounces up and clouts him under the chin, shoving cheeks and whiskers forward. Shades jolted one notch down his snout so a single wide eye peeks over the top rim, and a small white splash crown bursts right at his paws, touching them — nothing else below him.

Side-on sprint to the right, body low, forelegs reaching and hind heels coming down through the stride, the stubby ringed tail short and level behind him. The ring is squashed against his ribs with two short wobble lines off its edge and one flat palm clamped on the rim holding it down; paint the teal patch on this flank exactly as on the far side so the mirror is invisible.

Three short orange speed streaks along his flanks, a white glint flashing across both lenses, and a tight fan of spray bursting off his hind paws and attached to them — no rooster tail, no puddle, no street.

Shades pushed up on his forehead — two enormous jittering pinprick pupils — with jitter lines and a motion-blur double edge held tight against the ring.

Reared up on his haunches, arms flung wide, mouth open in astonished delight as gold bottlecaps and stray fries spiral in tight around the ring — a couple pinging off the taut rubber, one already lodged in the rope trim. Two little gold streaks reflected in the dark lenses; every loose cap sits within half a body width and overlaps his silhouette.

Reared up and immovably smug: a candy-striped beach parasol gripped in one palm and leaned back against his shoulder, canopy no wider than about 1.3x him, other palm planted on his hip, ring level at his waist. Rain skids off it in hard short diagonals, the ring squashes flat on the impact side, shades jolt crooked, whiskers swept back, muzzle scrunched in a flinch.

Reared onto his hind legs with the ring hauled off his body and hugged to his chest in both arms, exactly like the life preserver it always was, head craned up and back. Shades slid to the very tip of his snout so two huge white eyes stare over the top, mouth a tiny o, and a hard wedge of gull shadow falls across his chest and the rubber.

Sprinting flat toward camera-left, mouth wide, ears pinned, the licked-bare popsicle stick still clenched in his teeth — nothing thrown, nothing tumbling loose in the air. The ring has flapped up around his neck like a horse collar, three short red streaks come off his heels, and one lens catches a hard slash of the sweeper's yellow light.

Up on his hind legs with heels down, stretched as tall as he goes, both arms punched up and the ring hoisted just over his head — tilted hard toward camera so it foreshortens into an ellipse instead of adding height. Mouth open in pure joy; the one real sunlight on the whole sheet, painted onto him as a warm gold rim-light down his fur and two sparks on the lenses, no beam and no shaft.

Flat on his back, all four legs in the air with the palms flopped open, rocking gently on the ring like a turtle on its shell and suspiciously comfortable about it. Shades sit crooked with one lens popped out and resting on his chest fur — through the empty rim, one dazed swooning half-moon eye — tongue lolling, small stars circling tight around his head.

Sprawled on his side, cheeks puffed, mouth in a woozy wobble, with spirals painted straight onto both dark lenses because the shades never came off. Sat down hard in about six inches of water, arms straight up, fur plastered flat, mouth open in betrayed shock as a big white crown of water bursts around his hips and shoulders — no flat pool, no ripple rings, nothing detached. Shades shoved up on his dripping forehead so you can see exactly how personally he is taking this, and the ring has dropped clean around his ankles like a fallen hula hoop with water blowing up through the hole. barista.stance: Upright bipedal in all 18 — plantigrade with flat palms, five long spread fingers and heels flat down, he stands, crouches, leaps, lands, runs and flees on his hind feet only; he is never four-square and never knuckle-walks.
barista.wardrobe: In every single frame: the green apron with leather shoulder straps crossing LEFT over RIGHT and a brown patch pocket, one kraft-sleeved takeaway cup with a plain white lid that lives either in the RIGHT paw or stowed upright in that pocket, and a stub of pencil behind the LEFT ear — no other props ever, no tray, no lettering or logo on anything (the coffee frame is the one licensed exception: a second identical cup in the left paw).
barista.anatomy: He is hero Jimothy's body in an apron: round and spherical with no visible neck, the head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a STUBBY tail that never streams, curls out behind or flicks a rope of water — it is a short stub in all eighteen frames. Because the stance lock is upright, the poses originally designed as three-point quadruped scrambles become two-foot squats, two-foot jumps and a hind-leg sprint, with the stubby tail and the free left arm doing all the counterweighting. The cup permanently occupies his right hand, so any pose that needs both hands stows it upright in the apron pocket — it never goes on the ground, because there is no ground. Hands and feet stay plantigrade in every frame: flat palms, spread fingers, heels down, never knuckles.

frames.desc: Standing upright and square on flat hind feet facing camera, apron hanging straight, straps taut, stubby tail behind, the cup level in his right paw at chest height with one thin curl of steam going straight up. One eyebrow raised and a small closed-mouth smile that says he already knows what you are going to order and he has opinions.

The quiet one: sat back on his haunches, apron pooled over his knees, the cup cradled in both paws against his belly, ears relaxed, eyes half closed and pointed at nothing in particular. He opened at five, the coffee has gone lukewarm, and nobody has come in yet.

Sat with a fat almond croissant gripped in both paws, cheeks packed, eyes shut in pure relief, flakes and powdered sugar caught on the front of the apron and none falling loose. The cup is stowed upright in the brown apron pocket, lid on and still steaming, because he saves the coffee for after.

Coiled low in a two-foot squat, heels flat, knees to his chest, apron crumpled against his shins, ears back, eyes locked forward on the gap he is about to take. The cup is held in close beside his ribs under the free left paw, dead level and kept inside his outline so nothing sticks out sideways.

Fully airborne off both feet, body curled forward, hind legs tucked, apron pressed flat to his belly, whiskers swept back, mouth open in delight. The cup is punched forward just past his chest, dead upright, the coffee inside not even reaching the lip — nothing trails behind him.

Both hind feet planted hard with knees deep and the body low, apron swinging forward past his knees, a tight spray ring of rainwater bursting off his soles and touching nothing else. The cup arm has snapped up level with his shoulder to keep it steady, and one single bead of coffee hangs suspended just above the sip hole, about to drop back in.

Hind-leg sprint to the right, body tipped forward, long skinny legs at full stride, ears pinned, eyes on the crossing, apron flat against his chest and the stubby tail counterweighting. The cup rides level in the leading right paw held in close to the chest, its steam trailing straight back in one calm ribbon — the only calm thing in the frame.

Same hind-leg sprint tipped further over with a longer stride, ears blown back, eyes wide and pupils shrunk to pinpricks, warm orange and gold fire streaks licking tight off his heels. Same single cup, still level in the right paw close to the ribs, its steam ripped into one hard straight ribbon behind him — no tray, no second prop, nothing overhead.

The money frame and he is not moving an inch: planted facing camera in a wide heels-down stance, fur bristled out into a halo, ears bolt upright, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, jitter lines doubling his outline, an identical cup gripped in each paw at chest height with his face left completely clear. Pale blush-cream crema steam boils up no more than one head above his crown, warm gold fire licks close around his feet, and the apron strings float straight out on the updraft.

Standing upright with his free left arm thrown wide open, mouth open in undisguised delight and eyes shining — the best tip-jar night of his life, and it is all coming to him. The cup stays resolutely level in the right paw while bottlecaps, sugar packets and wooden stir sticks spiral in on a warm gold ribbon tight against his chest and arm, every one of them overlapping his body, the apron pocket already sagging full of caps.

Standing dry and insufferably smug under a small striped café umbrella whose shaft he holds in the left paw, the canopy sitting close over his head and no wider than his shoulders. Rain streaks off the fringe in short strokes that stop dead at the hem and never reach anything below, cup level in the right paw, ankles crossed, eyes half lidded, apron spotless — he has all day and you do not.

Braced in a half crouch with one eye shut and the left paw thrown up, a bright blue-violet energy dome flaring close around him and rain streaking off its curve in hard bright arcs. The right paw has clamped the cup flat against the apron bib, and the coffee in it is still perfectly level.

Upright and leaning back, ears flat, eyes huge and white-rimmed, both paws pulled in tight to his chest with the cup pinned upright between them. He is craning up and back at whatever is lining up above him, and the steam off the lid is being blown flat sideways across his own face by the dive.

Bipedal panic sprint to screen left, mouth wide open, ears back, apron flapping up around his ribs, warm orange speed streaks kept tight behind his heels and one small exclamation mark tucked in beside his ear. His trailing right paw still holds the cup out level and unspilled behind him, because the coffee is the very last thing he is willing to let go of.

Standing tall with heels down and chest out, apron straps proud, ears straight up, mouth open in a whoop, free left paw punched out to the side. The cup is raised in the right paw only to just above his ear, not to full stretch, and a small firework of gold steam pops out of the lid.

Flat on his back with long skinny legs in the air, swooning half-moon lids, tongue out one side and a small ring of stars circling his head, the apron flopped back over his chest and the pencil still jutting up from behind his left ear. The cup has come down upright and square on his belly, lid on, one thin curl of steam rising — and under the daze he looks quietly vindicated.

Sprawled on his side with spiral eyes, tongue out, ears at two different wrong angles, the apron twisted round backwards over his hip and the pencil hanging half out from behind his left ear — spirals only, no stars anywhere in this frame. The cup is balanced improbably upright on the crown of his skull, gently steaming, which somehow makes it worse.

The instant of the burst: soaked through and plastered dark, mouth open in shock and eyes wide inside a tight crown of bright blue-violet water exploding up around his knees, apron slapped flat up his chest with one strap flying. His right arm is punched straight up out of the spray, holding the cup bone dry and dead level above the entire disaster.

Where a frame's text does not explicitly move them they stay in their locked home positions; a frame missing one reads as plain Jimothy. fishmonger.anatomy: This is Jimothy's own body, so every hero pose transfers one for one: round and spherical with no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a STUBBY ringed tail that never streams, curls out behind him or flicks a rope of water. He is plantigrade — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down — never knuckles. The one real constraint is the salmon, which is nearly as long as he is tall: in every jaws-carry frame it is angled three-quarter with the nose swung toward the lens and the tail swung back past his shoulder, so it foreshortens to roughly his own shoulder width instead of doubling his silhouette and shrinking his head. A frame cannot be four-square and also hold a prop, so any frame needing hands is written as haunches or hind legs, and every jaws-carry frame keeps all four paws free to be down.

frames.desc: Standing four-square on flat palms and heels, blue bib apron hanging straight, stubby ringed tail low, chin lifted in calm quiet pride. The silver salmon is clamped crosswise in his jaws but angled three-quarter — nose swung toward the lens, tail back past his shoulder, coral stripe turned to camera — with one bead of water hanging off its tail fin, not yet fallen.

THE QUIET FRAME: up on his haunches at the end of market day, shoulders dropped, apron rucked at the waist, the salmon laid across his lap with one flat palm resting on its flank the way you rest a hand on a sleeping animal. Half-lidded eyes aimed off past the camera at nothing, nobody left to holler at, rain beading on his ear tips — and no puddle, no wet floor, nothing painted under him.

Sitting up on his haunches with the salmon tucked along one forearm and pinned under the elbow, stripe out — he is absolutely not eating that — while the free paw tips a paper cup of clam chowder to his mouth and oyster crackers stick to the apron bib. The fish's blank glass eye happens to line up on the cup, deadpan, as though it would also like some.

Flattened low on all fours, haunches up, apron bunched under his belly, the salmon held forward in his jaws at the same three-quarter angle like a bowsprit aimed at the far kerb. Brow down, eyes locked ahead, two ice chips flicking off the fish's tail and dying within a finger's width of it — nothing floating loose out at the side of the cell.

Fully airborne, belly forward, long skinny hind legs trailing, apron ties whipping back, stubby tail tucked, salmon locked crosswise in his jaws at the three-quarter angle. Eyes wide with joy and ears laid back in a grin around the fish, with a tight comet of water beads flung off its tail that stops within half a body width of him.

Flat palms slammed down and fingers splayed, elbows buckling, body low through the shoulders, apron flaring, the salmon still gripped crosswise in his jaws with its snout dipped from the impact. A contact burst of spray and three ice chips fires up off his own palms and touches his fur; one eye is cut sideways to check the fish is still there, and there is no water painted on the ground.

Side-on sprint to the right, body long and low, heels striking flat, apron ties streaming back and the stubby tail bobbing level behind him. The salmon rides dead level in his jaws like a relay baton and his head is held unnaturally steady so it cannot wobble, with spray kicking only off the pads of his own paws.

Flat out, all four legs at full stretch, ears pinned, eyes wide and glassy, the salmon clamped level in his jaws with its nose knifing forward. Warm-white speed streaks rake close past his flanks and a spray of ice chips comes out of the apron pocket, every piece of it overlapping his body.

HE IS NOT MOVING — planted up on his hind legs with both heels flat and knees locked, apron hanging straight, vibrating hard enough to blur his outline: paper cup in one paw, salmon jammed in the crook of the other elbow with the stripe to camera. Fur bristled into spikes, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, short jitter lines hugging his edges, pale blush-cream steam off the cup and warm orange fire licks at his own back heels.

Reared up on his hind legs in astonished delight, apron swinging, the salmon held up across both flat palms at chin height like a tray being presented, mouth open and eyes huge and shining — things are coming to him and he cannot believe it. Gold bottlecaps, stray fries and ice chips spiral in tight toward the fish on a warm amber trail, every piece inside half a body width and overlapping his silhouette.

Standing four-square and enormously smug with the salmon still crosswise in his jaws; the umbrella's crook is hooked over the apron's NECK strap behind his skull so the shaft rides up his back and the small canopy opens above and slightly behind his head, tilted back so it foreshortens no wider than his shoulders plus a palm each side. Rain slides off the canopy rim in a short curtain that stops at his shoulder line — head fur dry and fluffed, paws soaked, and absolutely no dry circle or wet patch painted on the pavement.

Crouched low on all fours and curled bodily around the fish, one shoulder into the blow, apron bunched tight, protecting the salmon instead of his own face with one eye screwed shut and teeth gritted around it. A blue-violet dome flares close around them both with rain streaking off it in pale sparks.

Up on his haunches and hunched small, ears flat, apron bib crumpled, the salmon clutched upright to his chest in both flat palms like a swaddled baby with its stripe out, eyes huge and aimed straight up. A gull's shadow slides across his own face and apron — painted on him, never on the floor — with three panic droplets flicking off his ear tips.

Full-panic three-legged scramble to the left, mouth open in a yelp, apron flying, the salmon tucked under one arm like a football with a flat palm locked over its nose. Warm red speed streaks crowd in close at his heels and two hard exclamation strokes sit just above his ears overlapping his outline — nothing is dropped and nothing is left behind him.

Reared tall on his hind legs, apron swinging, both arms flung up in the full Pike Place throw caught EARLY — the salmon has only just left his palms, angled up and back with its tail fin still overlapping his fingertips so the whole silhouette stays one connected piece. Mouth open in a joyful holler, eyes tracking the fish, gold sparkles and a few ice chips bursting close around his hands, his body mass still dead centre of the painted content.

Flat on his back with the long skinny legs loose in the air, apron flopped askew across one shoulder, gold stars circling close above his head and his eyes gone to swooning sideways half-moons. The salmon has landed alongside his cheek, nose to nose and touching him, blank-eyed and utterly deadpan, and his whole expression is a small apology to the fish.

Sprawled on his side with spiral eyes and tongue out, apron flopped over one ear, stars wheeling close above him. The salmon has somehow come to rest balanced upright on his belly, standing on its tail and wobbling, touching him the whole time — perfectly ordinary, perfectly dead-eyed, no spirals and no stars of its own.

The instant of shock inside an exploding crown of grey-green water bursting at his own body: arms up, apron plastered flat, ears streaming, eyes shocked wide, thoroughly out of play. Both palms hold the salmon up clear and dead level through the chaos, stripe to camera and entirely unbothered, and the crown stays tight to his shoulders so his body mass sits centre-frame.

grad.stance: Quadrupedal at rest on flat plantigrade palms; he rears onto his haunches or up on his hind legs in any frame where a forepaw has to carry something.

Diploma wedged through the sash with one stray fry balanced on its gold ribbon; tassel swinging in front of his eye and ignored.

Flattened low on all fours, haunches up, weight forward on spread plantigrade palms, mortarboard tipped down over his brow with the tassel dangling in front of his nose. Front paws slapped down flat with fingers spread, body low, weight absorbed through the shoulders, a tight ring of spray bursting off his own palms and hind feet and touching nothing else. Mortarboard slumped over one eye with the tassel across his face, diploma back through the sash, head coming up, whiskers forward.

The diploma has come untied in the sash and unrolled about a hand's length, the loose end curling back over his shoulder and no further — no paper tail leaves his box; tassel a rigid straight line behind him.

FEET PLANTED, NOT RUNNING: up on his hind legs vibrating in place, takeaway cup raised in one paw, diploma clamped under the opposite arm, mortarboard knocked askew with the tassel caught mid-whip in a full blurred circle around his head doing all the motion work. Pupils tiny in enormous eyes, fur bristled, jitter lines, warm fire licks and pale cream steam curling up around his own back feet — one corner of the diploma very slightly singed.

Up on his hind legs, diploma half-unrolled between both paws at chest height, mortarboard level again, mouth open in pure astonished delight that the world is bringing him things. Gold bottlecaps and fries spiral in on a tight gold-and-cream arc that overlaps his silhouette, two already landed in the curl of the paper, tassel lifted on the swirl.

Up on his hind legs under a black umbrella whose canopy is only a little wider than his shoulders and tilted to keep clear of the frame edge, mortarboard perfectly dry and perfectly level beneath it, diploma pressed to his chest under the sash. Rain streaks off the rim into a short spray that touches his own feet — no puddle, no wet ring, no ground; small smug closed-mouth smile.

Braced low on his hind feet, both forearms up with the diploma held horizontally across his face like a professor blocking a thrown eraser, eyes squeezed shut, teeth gritted. A bright blue-violet energy dome flares tight around him with rain streaking off it; mortarboard knocked back on his crown, tassel flung upward.

Up on his hind legs, both paws clutching the rolled diploma to his chest like a very small shield, head craned back and up at the sky. Eyes huge and white-rimmed, ears flat, mortarboard slid back but still hooked on his skull with the tassel standing bolt upright, drizzle lines slanting past close.

Quadruped sprint to the left, mouth open in panic, short warm-red speed streaks hugging his flanks, ears flat, stubby tail bottled out. Mortarboard jammed low with the tassel whipping forward past his cheek, diploma still wedged in the sash with only its ribbon end flapping — nothing tears loose and no marks or symbols in the air.

Up on his hind legs, one arm bent up with the diploma raised, the other paw open just below the mortarboard he has flicked a thumb's width clear of his crown — the cap still overlaps his own head, tassel whirling. Gold ribbon sparks and confetti burst in close around his shoulders, mouth wide open, rain lit gold.

Flat on his back, all four legs in the air with palms up, dazed half-moon lids and a small satisfied smile, gold stars circling his head — wounded dignity, entirely pleased with himself. Mortarboard tipped upside down against his shoulder and still touching him, tassel draped over his arm, and the diploma has unrolled across his belly to reveal a child's crayon drawing of a round raccoon beside a gold seal and ribbon — no lettering.

Slumped back on his haunches, spiral eyes, tongue out, stars looping close around his head. The mortarboard has rotated a quarter turn so the tassel hangs dead in front of his nose and he is going cross-eyed at it; the diploma sags in a floppy bent arc from one slack paw, still gripped.
