The instant of the burst — soaked, arms flung up, mouth open in shock inside an exploding crown of bright white and cyan water that closes around his middle. Mortarboard gone to sodden cardboard folded over one ear, tassel plastered flat to his cheek, diploma limp and unfurling in one raised paw with the gold seal bleeding a soft halo — no ink lines, no letters.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND IN ANY OF THE 18. No wet asphalt, puddles, ripples, drying smears, cast shadows, scattered fries or a dropped cap lying on the floor — the cutter keeps every non-magenta island and they all survive as grey scum under a floating raccoon. Every effect must touch him: spray off his own palms, steam around his own feet, water crown closing on his body.

ENVELOPE. The mortarboard corners are the widest and highest point of his silhouette and sit above the skull line, so leave clear margin all round every cell and let nothing touch a divider. Every frame including effects must land between about 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside roughly 236x224px — the widest offenders were dash-run's paper tail and cheer's cap toss, both now pulled back inside his box.

PROP LEDGER — mortarboard, gold tassel, navy sash and cream diploma roll appear in ALL EIGHTEEN. The diploma never leaves his body and never touches ground; it is a firm tight roll in every frame except the three where the damage is the joke (dash-run half-unrolled, dizzy floppy, splash limp). Held extras appear once each: fry carton (eat), cup (coffee), umbrella (umbrella).

NO READABLE TEXT ANYWHERE. The diploma is blank cream paper with a gold seal and ribbon — never a word, never a date, never a crest with lettering. Ko's reveal is a wordless crayon drawing. No '!!' marks in flee, no numbers, no badge type.

COLOUR AT 59px. Navy board and sash against gold tassel and ribbon is the entire silhouette read — keep those exact navy and gold values identical in all 18. Effects stay pale cream, gold, warm red or bright blue-violet: pink steam, magenta water and blue-violet domes get bitten apart by the magenta knockout.

SCALE AND ANCHOR. Match his BODY to hero Jimothy's idle first, then add the cap on top — he must be the same raccoon size as Jimothy and the same size as himself in all 18, checkable by the head being the same pixel count every frame. Sprites are centre-anchored, so keep his mass at the centre of the painted content; a high cap toss or a low spray ring will push him off his lane line.
grad.runL: Must be painted separately — the tassel hangs off the viewer-left corner, the sash knots at his right shoulder and falls in an asymmetric V, and the diploma sits left-of-centre in the sash, so a mirror jumps all three sides mid-stride on hard props the eye tracks; the engine's mirror fallback is not wired for fully animated characters anyway, so a missing run-l falls through to the procedural blob.

labcoat.stance: Plantigrade raccoon quadruped — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heels down — travelling on all fours in crouch, land, run-r, dash-run and flee, but reared up on planted hind feet whenever he is at rest, because the clipboard permanently occupies a forepaw and he is therefore NEVER standing four-square.
labcoat.wardrobe: In all 18 frames: rain-spotted warm off-white lab coat worn OPEN and unbuttoned (never fastened, never buttoned shut), narrow blue tie, stethoscope round the neck with both ends hanging down the chest, brow mirror centred on a headband, two pens in the coat's breast pocket, and the wooden clipboard with its metal clip and wordless chart pages carried in the LEFT forepaw — the pen comes out into the right paw in idle and sit only, and the pens leave the pocket in flee only.
labcoat.anatomy: Identical body to the hero, so every pose ports one-for-one: round spherical torso, no visible neck, head perched high on the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY ringed tail that stays close to the body and never streams, curls out behind or flicks water in any of the eighteen. The job costs him a limb, so the clipboard is a permanent extension of the left forepaw and is re-staged in every frame — lap desk when he sits, clamped under the elbow when both paws are needed, pressed flat beneath the palm on all-fours frames, riot shield when he is hit — which frees the right paw to do whatever plain Jimothy's right paw does. Because a paw is always occupied, he is never four-square: at rest he rears up on his haunches with both hind feet planted, and he gallops three-legged with the chart pinned to his ribs. The brow mirror, stethoscope and tie ride the head and neck and supply the trailing motion the hero gets from his whiskers and tail.

frames.desc: Reared up on his haunches with both hind feet planted and the round body square to camera, clipboard held flat against his chest in the left forepaw, capped pen loose in the right. Calm, unhurried, faintly bored bedside face, ears easy, stubby tail tucked close; the one hard white glint on his brow mirror is the brightest note in the frame.

Sat back on his haunches, coat hanging open around his belly, clipboard flat across his knees as a lap desk with the pen working down a row of wordless ink squiggles. Head tipped, eyes half-lidded, ears relaxed — the exact posture of a man doing his paperwork on a bus bench because there is nowhere better to be.

Sat on his haunches with the clipboard clamped under his left elbow against his ribs so both forepaws are free around a half-unwrapped deli sandwich, cut on the diagonal by somebody at home. Cheeks packed, eyes shut in bliss, brow mirror slid crooked down over one eye and no attempt made to fix it.

Flattened low on four flat palms with heels down and haunches loaded, the clipboard pressed flat beneath his left forepaw, coat rucked up over his shoulders. Stethoscope swung forward and hanging clear under his chin, whiskers back, eyes locked forward down the street, absolutely about to go.

Fully airborne and stretched long, belly forward, hind legs trailing, clipboard thrust out ahead in the left paw like a doctor twelve minutes late to rounds. Coat tails and stethoscope stream back close behind him, tie flipped up over his shoulder, stubby tail tucked, and he looks openly delighted about it.

Front palms slapped down wide and body low, the clipboard taking part of the weight flat under the LEFT forepaw, coat billowing forward past his shoulders from the stop. Ears up, whiskers forward, a small spray of wet grit bursting off the palms and touching them.

Side-on three-legged gallop to the right: the near left forepaw pins the clipboard to his ribs the way a chart gets carried down a corridor while the far forepaw and both hind feet do the work. Coat hem flaring back, stethoscope swung out on the curve, mouth shut, eyes on the far side of the street.

Flat-out horizontal sprint, legs stretched fore and aft, coat streaming straight back, brow mirror flashing, eyes wide with pinprick pupils. Orange fire licks at his paws and exactly ONE chart page tears back over his stubby tail, still caught in the clip and overlapping his body, with speed streaks no longer than half a body.

Feet planted and body vibrating in place, standing bolt upright, fur bristled all over, a cafeteria paper cup in the right paw trailing pale blush-cream steam and the clipboard clamped under his left arm. That free left paw has the stethoscope bell pressed to his own chest and his eyebrows are climbing at what he can hear; pinprick pupils, short jitter lines tight to the body, small orange fire licks at his feet — all the energy, none of the travel.

Standing tall on his hind feet, mouth open in an astonished delighted grin, clipboard held up flat in both forepaws like a serving tray while bottlecaps, fries and wrapped snacks swirl in toward it. The swirl stays tight and overlapping his silhouette, his coat pockets are already overflowing, and one bottlecap has landed square in his brow mirror — pure joy that things are coming TO him.

Standing on his hind feet under a black umbrella hooked in the crook of his right elbow, canopy tipped toward camera and no wider than his open coat, the clipboard slid inside the coat against his chest and held there by his left forearm where the paperwork will stay dry. Rain breaking off the rim in short grey strokes that stop well inside the frame; utterly smug, utterly dry, one eyebrow up at the weather.

Dropped onto his haunches with the clipboard snapped up flat in front of his face like a tiny riot shield and the free right paw braced behind it, one eye squeezed shut, teeth gritted. A BRIGHT CYAN-WHITE energy dome flashes tight around him with rain streaking off its curve and two chart pages blown up off the board, still tethered at the clip.

Up on his hind feet, clipboard clutched flat to his chest in both paws like a shield he has not thought to raise, head tipped back to watch the sky. Eyes huge and white-rimmed, ears pinned flat, brow mirror tilted up and catching the light, stethoscope swinging loose off his neck.

Bolting three-quarter away toward the lower left, mouth open in flat panic, clipboard tucked under his left arm like a football, coat unbuttoned and flapping wide behind him. Red speed streaks off his heels and exactly two pens shaken out of the breast pocket, both close in and overlapping the flying coat so they cut as one shape.

Up on his hind feet, clipboard punched up in the left paw to just above the crown of his head and the right forepaw fisted at shoulder height, mouth wide open in a joyful whoop, eyes shut with the size of it. Brow mirror catching a star of light and one chart page fluttering up off the board, still clipped at its corner.

Flat on his back with all four long limbs in the air, coat splayed open around him, stethoscope tangled comically across his snout, stubby tail pinned beneath him. The clipboard has landed face up on his belly and the trace on the chart dips flat then kicks straight back into a fat healthy bounce — one eye cracked open reading it with an eyebrow up, the other a dazed half-moon, gold stars circling his head.

Sprawled sitting up crooked with his tongue out and both eyes drawn as full spirals, the clipboard fallen flat across the top of his head at an angle like a slipped roof tile, its edge down over one spiralled eye. Headband shoved right round so the brow mirror sits behind one ear, chart pages fanned loose but still caught in the clip with one slid down over that ear, one forepaw half-raised in apology — spirals only here, no stars.

Soaked through and shocked rigid inside a bursting white and pale-cyan crown of water at his hips, both forepaws thrown up, coat plastered translucent to his fur and the brow mirror running with drips. The clipboard is still up in his left paw and its chart has gone to grey pulp, peeling off the board in one sad wet curl but never leaving it — he is far more offended about the paperwork than about the water.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND, ANY FRAME. No pavement, puddles, damp smears, cast shadows, kerbs, drains, skid marks or pages scattered on the road — all of that survives the magenta cut as floating grey scum under a character with nothing beneath him. The only legal ground-adjacent effects are the ones TOUCHING him: grit bursting off his palms in land, fire licking at his paws in dash-run and coffee, the water crown at his hips in splash.

ENVELOPE, MEASURED FROM THE HERO'S OWN 20 FILES: 180-236 px wide by 174-224 tall, aspect 0.81 to 1.33. Every frame including its effects stays inside that, and the checkable test is his HEAD — it must be the same number of pixels in all eighteen. If an effect makes the head smaller, the effect is too big. The engine centre-anchors, so keep his body mass at the centre of the painted content: no tall stack of content above him in cheer or scared, nothing spread below him anywhere.

TETHER LEDGER. Loose chart pages appear in exactly four frames — dash-run (one), shield (two), cheer (one), splash (one peeling) — and every single one stays physically caught in the metal clip and overlapping his body. Flee's two pens overlap the flying coat so they cut as one shape. Nothing floats free, nothing sits further than half a body width out, and nothing touches a frame edge or a divider line; leave a clear magenta margin all the way round every cell.

COLOUR LAW. No magenta or hot pink anywhere in any effect — the knockout eats that family and leaves ragged bites. Coffee steam is pale blush-cream with the green channel up, the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. Keep the coat a warm off-grey-white rather than pure white so it does not blow out against the rain, with a fine warm-grey ink outline all the way round the coat edges so the cutter has an edge to find.

NO LETTERING ANYWHERE. Chart pages are wordless rows of ink squiggles plus one wavy trace line; no name tag, no badge, no print on the coat, no numbers on the mirror. The draft's floating red '!!' marks in flee are CUT — they are detached islands that inflate the crop and push him off his lane line; the panic reads from the open mouth, the flat ears and the heel streaks instead.

READ AT 59px. The silhouette cues are the round no-neck body, the hard white glint on the head-high brow mirror, and the pale wedge of the open coat. Keep the stethoscope a dark hard line against that coat and keep the clipboard warm wooden brown against the white — never white-on-white, or both props vanish at lane size. He carries no scale key, so he must sit at exactly the hero's height in the lane, coat and all.
labcoat.runL: Must be painted separately: the clipboard rides the LEFT forepaw, and in run-r that is the near, camera-side arm pinning the chart to his ribs — mirroring throws the clipboard, the breast-pocket pens and the three-legged gallop to the far side of the body and the whole doctor read collapses.

skunk.stance: Quadrupedal plantigrade at rest — heel down, flat palms, all four feet on the ground — and he rears back onto a haunches-plus-tail tripod whenever a frame needs front paws; he never stands upright without that rear-up.
skunk.wardrobe: None — no costume and no carried prop in any frame; the tail is his only permanent equipment. The four frame-local props are: takeaway box + grub (eat only), gold bottlecaps and fries (magnet only), paper coffee cup (coffee only), folded thrift-store umbrella (umbrella only) — they appear nowhere else.
skunk.anatomy: He is a short-legged plantigrade quadruped with no true hands, so every pose that needs arms is solved the way a real striped skunk solves it: he rears back on his haunches into a tripod of two hind feet plus the tail and works with two dextrous front paws. The great plume is the third limb and does the jobs Jimothy's arms do — parasol, windbreak, cushion, banner, backstop — but it is NOT prehensile: it fans, arches over the back, bottle-brushes and drapes, and it never grips, wraps, carries or scoops anything. He is famously near-sighted, so the squint is always aimed slightly wide of whatever he is actually looking at. Standing rule: four-square only when both front paws are empty and on the ground (idle only); any frame with a prop or a raised paw must be sat back on the haunches or reared on the hind legs.

frames.desc: Standing four-square at three-quarter camera, glossy black guard hairs beaded with rain, the double white stripe running clean from forehead over the back, the great plume carried high like a parade banner and curling forward past his ears. Small amber eyes in a polite near-sighted squint, a faint contented smile, and nothing at all under his paws — no puddle, no reflection, no shadow; this is the existing idle.png and his head size here is the measuring stick for the other seventeen.

Sat back on his haunches, back rounded, front paws tucked into the white chest fur, eyes half-lidded and aimed slightly wide of whatever he is watching — the near-sighted stare at a blur of lights he cannot quite resolve. The plume has swept down and forward to lie against his forefeet like a dropped stole, so he is sitting warm inside his own tail while the rain keeps coming down; this is the sheet's quiet, slightly lonely beat.

Sat up on his haunches with a rain-softened takeaway box tipped open between his hind feet, fries ignored, one fat pale garden grub held in both front paws like corn on the cob, eyes shut in genuine bliss. The plume arches over his back and curves down behind the box as a windbreak so the rain cannot get in — considerate, slightly gross, entirely him.

Flattened low on all fours, haunches up, chest almost to the ground but with nothing painted beneath it, whiskers forward, eyes locked up-screen. The tail is pressed low and long behind him like a loaded spring with the plume tip waved up to stay inside the box, and his forepaws blur mid-drum in the little warning stamp a skunk does before anything happens (existing crouch.png).

Fully airborne and stretched, all four short legs spread wide, belly forward, mouth open in delight, near-sighted eyes as wide as they go. The plume streams back and then CURVES UP behind him into a tall banner arc — tip painted, never cropped, never stretched flat across the cell — so the frame stays the same 207x250 portrait as idle and he does not shrink for the middle of every single hop.

Front paws planted with a tight splash ring bursting off the pads and up his forelegs — contact spray only, no puddle and no ring on the floor — chest low, haunches still dropping, weight visibly absorbed. The tail has whipped forward over his own back and overshot past his nose, plume fanned across his face, so he is momentarily half-buried in his own tail and squinting out through it.

Side-on to the right, body low and stretched long, short legs at full extension, the plume held back and waved up in a lazy S so it climbs inside the box rather than lengthening the cell. In profile the forehead stripe and one amber eye carry the identity, and his face wears a small determined scowl, because he is not fast and he knows it.

Flat out and side-on, legs at full stretch and barely touching down, ears pinned, eyes huge, tongue out the side of his mouth, the plume swept back and curved up into a white torpedo with short speed lines that stop well inside the margin and two loose plume hairs tumbling in the streak. A soft pastel mint-and-cream clover puff blooms at the tail's base like a little booster — sparkly, aimed back at empty road, never yellow-green or brown, never a cloud or a jet, and nothing in frame reacts to it.

Reared up on his hind legs and DEAD STILL, both feet planted flat, a paper cup clamped in both front paws, coffee slopping over the rim onto his own wrist, steam curling off in pale blush-cream (never hot pink). Every hair of the plume has stood on end and bottle-brushed to twice its width with jitter lines ticking off it, pupils shrunk to two dots, two small warm-orange fire licks curling off his hind feet — all the energy is vibration and bristled fur, no speed lines, no travel.

Sat up on his haunches with both front paws cupped open at his chest, mouth open in pure astonishment and delight — things are coming TO him and he cannot believe his luck. The plume is fanned wide and vertical behind him as a catcher's screen: gold bottlecaps and fries fly in from just inside the frame, stick in the fur, bounce off it and cascade down the plume into his paws — the tail is a backstop, never a basket, and nothing collects on a floor because there is no floor.

Sat up on his haunches with the whole plume arced forward over his head as a fat white parasol, rain sheeting off it in bright ribbons and not one drop reaching him. A cheap folded thrift-store umbrella is tucked unopened under one front paw, purely for show, and his squint is enormously smug about owning two roofs.

The instant of the hit: flinched down flat, ears back, eyes squeezed shut, one front paw thrown up over his face. A blue-violet energy dome snaps tight around him — never blue-violet or purple, which the cutter eats — dented outward at the crown where the bolt-upright plume shoves against it, rain streaking hard down the outside.

The real skunk warning display: front half dropped low, back arched high, all four feet down, both forepaws blurred mid-stamp in a panicked drum roll, plume snapped bolt upright and fanned into a full flag. His head twists up and back but the near-sighted squint is aimed at the wrong patch of grey sky, one ear cocked, a single fat painted exclamation mark tucked against the plume so it overlaps his silhouette, and the faintest pastel mint sparkle at the tail base.

Sprinting left, low and scrambling, mouth open in panic, wet fur plastered over eyes gone huge, a tight burst of water flicking off the pads themselves (on the paws, never on a floor) and short warm orange-red speed streaks stopping inside the margin. The plume drags in a wobbling panicked wave instead of a proud banner, because for the first time in his life the thing behind him is not getting out of his way.

Reared up on his hind legs, compact rather than stretched, both front paws flung up beside his head, eyes squeezed shut in a huge grin, chest stripe blazing. The plume fans straight up into a white firework and the whole celebration stays INSIDE that fan — pastel mint and cream clover puffs and sparkles held within the plume, none of it near the frame edge — so the cell keeps the 207x250 box and his head stays exactly idle-sized.

Flat on his back with all four short legs sticking straight up, tongue lolling to one side, one ear folded over, eyes closed into swooning half-moon lids (never X's) and three little stars circling his head. The great plume has spread flat beneath him like a fur fainting couch so he has landed in completely unearned luxury, rain falling gently on his upturned white belly — suspiciously comfortable, funny-sad, never grim.

Sprawled belly-down and splayed out like a dropped rug, spiral eyes, tongue out, stars wobbling around his head. The plume is bent up above him into a lazy question mark and his back is dusted with swept-up leaves and wet grit that all sit ON the fur — nothing scattered on the ground, and no loose hairs drifting free in this frame.

The instant of the burst: front half heaved up inside an exploding crown of water, both forepaws thrown skyward, mouth open in shock, eyes enormous, soaked through and plainly out of play. Behind him the glorious plume has collapsed into a sad wet rope a third of its size with a few bubbles off the tip — the ruined tail is the joke and the small heartbreak — and there is no separate water plane or surface line painted below him.

sheetNotes: CANVAS AND SCALE (this replaces the old note entirely). All 18 frames go on the same 207x250 portrait cell as the four existing files — aspect 0.83, well inside the 1.35 cap and safely on the height-sized 59px branch, matching Jimothy's own envelope of 180-236 x 174-224. The old instruction that 'his cells are simply bigger than the other critters' cells' is WRONG and will halve him: every frame is normalised on its own, so a bigger cell shrinks the animal. His body and head are painted at one constant size in all eighteen and the TAIL arranges itself to fit the box — it never sets the box. The single checkable test is that his head is the same pixel count in every frame.

NO GROUND PLANE, ANYWHERE, IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. Struck from the old sheet: the wet gutter reflection under idle's paws, and any pile of caps at his feet in magnet. There is no pavement in a sprite — puddles, reflections, cast shadows, curbs, litter rings and scattered props all cut out as floating grey scum under a character with no floor. Contact effects that touch his body are correct and wanted: the splash ring bursting off his pads in land, spray off the paws in flee, the water crown around his body in splash, grit and leaves sitting on his fur in dizzy.

COLOUR LAW. The knockout eats the magenta family, so: shield dome BRIGHT blue-violet, Against that, near-black fur is the other real hazard — keep a thin warm rim-light along the top of the guard hairs in all eighteen so the silhouette survives a dark lane, and keep the white stripe crisp. The stripe and the plume are the only two things a player actually sees at speed.

THE SPRAY GAG appears in exactly three frames and nowhere else: the booster puff on dash-run, the confetti burst on cheer, and the faintest hint at the tail base on scared. Pastel mint and cream only, shaped as clover puffs and sparkles — never yellow-green, never brown, never a cloud, never a jet, never a stink line. It is always aimed behind him at empty road, and no bystander, hazard or object ever reacts to it. It is fireworks, not weaponry: he is a shy, polite animal who simply has the whole lane to himself.

CENTRE-ANCHORED, AND NOTHING TOUCHES AN EDGE. The engine centres the sprite on the lane point, so the body's mass must sit at the centre of the painted content in every frame — this matters most where the plume goes straight up (coffee, scared, cheer) and where water goes up (splash), all of which will otherwise push him below his lane line. Keep a clear magenta margin all the way round every cell, including full clearance for the tail tip, which is never cropped; speed lines, sparkles and incoming magnet items all start inside the frame and overlap his silhouette, never at or beyond the divider lines.

FOUR FRAMES ALREADY EXIST AND ARE GOOD — idle, crouch, leap and land at 207x250. The fourteen new ones must match their camera, lighting and scale exactly; if you would rather repaint, repaint all eighteen in one pass and never mix an old scale with a new one on the same sheet. Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for a 59px lane check before committing the other fifteen. Note for the build: run-l ships mirrored, so the engine's mirror fallback must be enabled for full 18-frame characters or every leftward hop falls through to the procedural blob.

slug.stance: Prone gastropod — never bipedal, never four-square, no limbs at any point: one muscular foot on the deck with the front third reared up, and his body length always spent in a curve or an S so the head rides high and the painted box stays near-square.
slug.wardrobe: No costume and nothing held in any frame — the constants in all 18 are his own body: banana-yellow gloss, the identical black leopard-spot map, the darker olive mantle saddle over the front third, the pneumostome painted as a same-tone dimple on the right flank, one long specular highlight down the back, two eyestalks plus two lip-feelers, and a SHORT glossy slime stub touching his tail at the same length every single frame.
slug.anatomy: The two eyestalks do every job an arm would do — pointing, splaying, flinching, cheering — but they are hydrostatic, fluid pressure with no skeleton, so they invert into the head at the lightest touch: they can never bear weight, never prop anything up and never hold. Props therefore only ever stick to his slime, lie against his flank, or drape over his back; nothing is gripped. The travelling muscle wave banding down his foot does every job a leg would do, so speed is sold by how tight and fast that banding reads, never by how long a trail is. He rears by lifting the front third off the deck, which means he is never four-square and never has a spare limb — there was never a limb to spare.

frames.desc: Front third reared up off the deck with the rest of him curled into a shallow S beneath, both eyestalks tall and splayed, the two lip-feelers tasting the rain, mouth a calm soft line. Wet gloss down the back, the short slime stub curled at his tail, and nothing else in the cell.

Off duty: body settled into a fat comma, mantle relaxed, both eyestalks drooped to half mast and lazily crossed at the tips, eyes half-lidded in the rain and mouth a small content line. A thin glossy collar of slime is pressed out tight around his own outline, no wider than a lip-feeler — the last one still out here, and perfectly happy about it.

Nose-deep in a fallen chanterelle stuck to his own chest by the slime, rasping a neat scalloped bite out of the cap, one eyestalk tipped down to watch the food while the other stays up on lookout. A soggy Pike Place fry is glued flat against his flank with one identical scallop already taken out of it, abandoned as too dry.

Gathered to spring: concertina'd to half his length and twice his height, ridged like a squeezed accordion, mantle flared, both eyestalks pulled halfway back into his head and aimed up-screen. The slime stub is bunched into a tight glossy pleat at his tail, loaded like a spring.

Fully airborne on a steep diagonal, arced belly-forward like a thrown banana with his nose up-screen and tail low so he fills the cell corner to corner, both eyestalks streaming back like ribbons, mouth open in undignified delight. The stub has snapped clean at his tail into a short curl and three flung dew droplets, all of it tucked in against his own outline.

A belly-flop: the front third splatted wide and flat with a tight ring of slime squirting out right at the contact edge, the back half still arriving in a visible ripple down his foot. Both eyestalks have whipped forward past his own face from the impact, eyes crossed for a beat, grinning anyway.

Side-on and travelling right in a low shallow S, the muscular wave banding down his foot like rolling light, eyestalks laid back streamlined, jaw set with total determination. The stub stays short at his tail and the motion arcs hugging his flank are honestly, comically tiny — this is his top speed.

The same side-on sprint flat out: body drawn thin, the foot waves compressed into a blur of banding, eyestalks pinned straight back, eyes wide, mouth open. Warm amber friction licks and one pale cream steam curl come off the foot's contact edge while the tail stub throws a tight spray of droplets — every effect touching him.

Dead still and visibly vibrating: reared up on his back third with the foot planted, double-image blur on both eyestalks, pupils shrunk to pin dots, the whole front of him glossed espresso-dark because he crawled straight through the spill rather than carrying it. The tipped takeaway cup lies against his own flank giving off pale blush-cream steam, with short jitter lines at his mantle and warm amber fire licks flickering at the stub.

Reared up with his mouth open in a delighted round O and both eyestalks splayed wide in pure astonishment, because with him everything sticks: gold bottlecaps already glued along his back like sequins and one fry stuck flat to an eyestalk. Three more caps spiral in on short curved arcs that overlap his body, close enough to be about to land on him.

He crawled UNDER it — a fallen big-leaf maple drapes over his back and mantle with its stem still hooked at the tip of his tail so it reads as deliberately dragged into place, the front edge lifted just enough that his head and both fully extended stalks poke out clean. Rain sheets off the leaf's drip tip in one bright stream, and one fat drop has got through onto his back, which he is plainly thrilled about: eyes half-lidded and smug.

The hit lands: both eyestalks snap fully inside his head leaving two dimples, the body clenched into a tight tense hump, mantle flared, mouth a shocked little slot. A bright blue-violet dome flares tight around him with rain streaking off it, and the maple leaf is still stemmed to his tail but flipped back over itself and crumpled.

Coiled back tight with his front end craned up-screen, both eyestalks stretched to full periscope height and bent to point dead at the sky, pupils huge, one bead of slime-sweat wobbling on his mantle. The diving gull's shadow falls as a hard dark bar across his own back and mantle only.

Absolute maximum slug velocity, which is nothing: body stretched to its longest inside the same box, foot waves frantic, eyestalks streaming back with a bold red double exclamation mark sitting right on top of them, mouth open in panic, a fine mist of slime flung off his flank. The red speed streaks are so short they are the joke.

Reared as tall as he goes on the last third of his foot with the rest of him looped beneath for width, both eyestalks flung skyward in a wide V with the little feelers up too, mouth open in a whoop, back arched proud in warm gold light. The stub at his tail curls up into one short glittering silver loop — a victory streamer the size of a shoelace.

Rolled foot-up and still gently rocking, pale glossy belly-foot to the sky with only the curve of his back touching down; all four tentacles flop backward and DOWN over his own upturned face, the two long ones drooping past his eyes like wet noodles and the lip-feelers splayed sideways. Eyes are two dazed little dots pointing in slightly different directions, mouth slack, three stars circling close above him, and one bright slime smear still glossing the flank he skidded on.

Sprawled in a loose S with both eyestalks crossed and tied in a soft overhand knot, a spiral in each eye, mouth slack in a woozy smile, his back striped with brush-bristle dust and street grit. The tail stub is corkscrewed into one tight turn and three stars circle close above his head.

Caught inside the burst, not under it: soaked and water-darkened with a crown of pale cyan-white exploding around his middle, both eyestalks flung up and out in shock and his mouth a round startled O. His slime stub is dissolving into pale milky curls at his tail — the actually sad part, and he knows it.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND, EVER — in any of the 18. No pavement, no puddle, no cast shadow, no slime road, no skid mark leading in from off-frame, no scattered litter. The engine paints its own ground shadow under him; anything wet that you paint must physically touch his body or it cuts out as a floating grey smear beneath a slug standing on nothing.

THE SLIME STUB IS A LOCK. Same short length, touching his tail, in all 18 — the trail was previously a road in idle, run-r, dash-run, flee, cheer and dizzy at six different lengths, which changed the crop and therefore changed his size every frame. Speed lives in the muscle-wave banding down the foot, never in track length.

ENVELOPE, AND THE ONE CHECKABLE TEST: every cell including its effects must land between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside roughly 236x224px, and his HEAD must be the same number of pixels in all 18. He is a long animal in a near-square box — spend the length in a curve or an S with the front third reared, never as a straight horizontal bar, or he draws half-size mid-animation.

NOTHING TOUCHES A CELL EDGE OR A DIVIDER — keep a clear magenta margin all the way round. Detached bits (the magnet caps, the leap droplets, the circling stars, the exclamation mark) sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, or the cutter emits them as their own sprite.

COLOUR LAW: the knockout eats the magenta family, so no hot-pink or magenta effects anywhere. Steam pale blush-cream, the shield dome bright blue-violet ( At 59px on wet grey lane art his banana-yellow is carried by the black spot map and the single specular stripe — keep the darker mantle saddle so the head end still reads.

WET GLOSS IN ALL 18, ko, dizzy and splash included; a matte slug reads as a dead slug rather than a knocked-out one. Spot map, mantle saddle and the right-flank pneumostome stay in identical places every frame, and the pneumostome is a same-tone dimple, not a contrasting mark. No readable text on anything, and no X eyes — dazed dots plus stars for ko, spirals for dizzy only. Once these 18 exist the engine stops compositing its stand-in umbrella and dome, so the maple leaf and the cyan dome must be painted into their own cells.
slug.runL: mirror — his only asymmetry is the pneumostome, and painting it as a same-tone dimple makes the flip invisible at 59px; note for the build that a full character with no run-l.png falls through to the procedural blob, so either export the mirrored file or add the mirror fallback before marking him full.

otter.stance: Quadruped at rest — long low spine, short bandy plantigrade legs with flat palms and heels down — who rears onto his haunches with the thick rudder tail braced behind as a third leg whenever he needs his forepaws.
otter.wardrobe: No clothing and no costume: one prop only, a smooth green river stone, present in all 18 frames — held in a forepaw or clamped chin-to-chest when he is still, carried in his jaws when he is travelling, and loose at his own hip in flee alone.
otter.anatomy: He has a raccoon's dexterous forepaws and none of a raccoon's legs: long low spine, short plantigrade limbs, and a tail thick enough to work as a third leg, so every raccoon standing pose becomes a rear-up onto the haunches with the tail braced behind, and every raccoon run becomes the true humpback otter bound or a belly slide. He is four-square in idle only, and a four-square frame cannot also hold something in a forepaw — that is exactly why the stone rides in his jaws there. There is no armpit pouch and no chest-anvil floating on his back: that is a sea otter, and nothing he carries may depend on either. He is never dry in any frame — wet fur peaked into dark spikes along the spine, all eighteen.

frames.desc: Standing four-square, all four palms and heels flat down, long body in a lazy S with the thick tail laid in a shallow arc to his right and the green stone carried gently in his jaws. Head up, whiskers dripping, eyes soft and a little far away — an otter who has been waiting on this corner a while.

Sat bolt upright on his haunches, tail flat behind him doing the work of a third leg, both forepaws folded on his pale belly cradling the green stone. Shoulders dropped, eyes half-lidded, rain running off his chin in a steady thread — no puddle and no floor, he is simply soaked and in no hurry to be anywhere.

Hunched belly-down and angled three-quarter to camera, elbows out, hind feet splayed behind, tail flat; the green stone is pinned under his left forepaw as an anvil while the right brings a mussel down onto it, head cocked to watch the crack. A tipped paper tray of fried clams and two shell halves lean against his elbow and shoulder in physical contact — nothing loose, no puddle, no pavement painted.

Coiled low with the spine compressed into a tight hump, elbows tucked under the chest, hind feet planted wide, chin almost down and eyes locked up-screen. The stone is clamped in his teeth ready for the jump, tail laid straight behind him, nothing painted beneath him.

Airborne on a rising diagonal toward the camera, body curved like a banana rather than stretched flat, forepaws reaching forward, hind feet trailing and the tail curled up behind to keep the box square. Mouth open in a delighted hoot, the stone clamped in the crook of his left elbow against his chest, a tight shake of water beads coming off his fur no further out than a paw's width.

Front paws slapping down flat, spine humping up behind them, hind feet skidding in underneath, whiskers thrown forward and the head coming back up. A low crown of rain bursts right at his palms where they make contact and the tail whips upward for balance; stone still in the crook of his left elbow, no ground and no cast shadow under him.

Side-on humpback bound to the right in the true otter rhythm, back arched high at the middle, fore and hind paws gathering underneath him, ears pinned flat, tail arced up and behind rather than streaming out flat. The stone rides in his jaws on the centre line — deliberately, so this frame mirrors clean — with spray flicking off the paws themselves and no puddles painted behind.

Belly slide angled three-quarter toward the camera with the spine curved rather than dead straight, forelegs tucked back along his flanks, hind feet still shoving, chin an inch off nothing, stone switched into his teeth. Cheeks pushed back, eyes wide with glee; wake is two short curls at the shoulders and the speed streaks run no longer than half his body — box capped at 1.35:1, run-r's silhouette is the target.

Standing dead still and vibrating: reared on both hind feet with the tail braced behind as a tripod, a takeaway cup already half crushed in both forepaws, the green stone clamped under his chin against his chest. Pinprick pupils, whiskers straight out, every wet spike bristled, pale blush-cream steam off the lid, short jitter lines hugging his outline and small warm heat licks touching his own feet — no fire on the ground, no forward lean, no travel in this pose at all.

Up on his haunches with the tail as tripod, head back and mouth open in pure astonishment, both forepaws juggling three gold bottlecaps in a low arc that rises no higher than his own crown — delight at being given things, never appetite. More caps and a few fried clams spiral in and touch his chest and shoulders, everything inside half a body width; the stone stays clamped under his chin and the tail thumps hard enough to fling water off its own tip.

Sat upright on his haunches, one forepaw on the shaft of a small plain umbrella held at a lazy tilt low over his left shoulder, the other cradling the green stone in his lap. Half his face still gets rained on and he could not care less — eyes lidded, deeply smug; one short bright curtain of rain sheets off the canopy rim and stops well inside the frame, and there is no lettering or logo anywhere on the canopy.

Dropped low and braced, both flat forepaws up in front of his muzzle, whiskers flattened back, eyes screwed shut, tail clamped tight along his own flank. A bright blue-violet dome flashes close around him with rain and grit streaking off its skin, and the stone is jammed between his chin and chest where he clamped down on it.

Reared into the bolt-upright periscope stand otters really do, hind feet together and the tail curved out behind as both tripod and wide base, neck stretched as tall as it goes. Both forepaws clutched to his chest around the green stone, eyes huge and rolled upward, mouth a small round O, every wet hair on his back standing in spikes.

Panic belly-slide to the left, angled three-quarter to camera with the spine curved, forepaws thrown out ahead, mouth wide open, tail thrashing behind. The green stone has bounced out of his teeth and tumbles just off his hip, overlapping his own tail — clearly dropped but still on him; short white shock spikes and flung water beads only, no punctuation marks, no fanned water on a floor that does not exist.

Reared to full height on both hind feet with the tail arced out behind as a broad tripod, one forepaw punched up holding the green stone overhead like a trophy, elbow bent so the stone clears his crown by no more than a head. Head thrown back, mouth open in a whooping chirp, a short bright arc of water flung off the tail tip, belly fur gloriously soaked.

Flat on his back but rolled three-quarter toward the camera so the box stays near square, all four short legs in the air, thick tail flopped out flat to one side. Swooning half-moon lids, tongue out the corner, gold stars circling his head, and the stone has landed on his belly and simply stayed there — he looks suspiciously comfortable, as though this was always the plan.

Sprawled on his side in a loose comma angled toward the camera, tail curled up over his own nose, spiral eyes, tongue lolling, ears at half mast. One forepaw pats vaguely around for the green stone, which is resting against his own pads the entire time — spirals only here, no orbiting stars, so he stays visually distinct from ko.

The instant of the burst: caught inside a wide low white water crown that rises no more than a head above him, soaked flat, forepaws thrown up with the stone still clamped in the right one. Ears pinned, whiskers plastered, eyes wide and jaw open in an outraged squeak — the one animal on the roster built for this and he is deeply offended by it; nobody sinks, nobody swims, the burst is the whole read.

sheetNotes: ENVELOPE: every frame 0.80:1 to 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x the idle box. The tail is a third of his silhouette — arc it up, curl it, or lay it along the body, but never let it stream out flat behind, because that alone width-normalises him down to half height mid-animation.

HEAD TEST: his skull must be the same number of pixels in all 18 frames. dash-run, flee, eat, ko and dizzy are the five that will fail it — all of them are angled three-quarter to camera for exactly that reason, and the head stays forward and full size.

NO GROUND, ANY FRAME: no puddles, no wet pavement, no cast shadows, no drains, no shells or crumbs resting on a floor. Water is only allowed off the body — contact spray at the palms in land, curls at the shoulders in dash-run, flick off the tail tip in cheer and magnet.
COLOUR LAW: steam is pale blush-cream (never pink), the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. Saturated magenta, hot pink and blue-violet get bitten out by the cutter.
NO LETTERING ANYWHERE, props included: the cup, the umbrella canopy and the clam tray carry texture and pattern only. flee gets shock spikes, not exclamation marks.
Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for the 59px cut test before committing the other fifteen — they are the three most likely to blow the envelope.
otter.runL: mirror — the stone was moved off his side and onto the centre line (in his jaws) in run-r specifically so the flip is clean, and nothing else on him is asymmetric, so no separate left-facing painting is needed.

heron.stance: Upright biped — he stands over two long stilt legs with the body carried vertically and the neck folded into an S; never on all fours, never "four-square", and a wing is never used as a hand.
heron.wardrobe: No costume and no permanent prop — the heron is bare; props appear in exactly four frames and always touch the body: plain paper chip cone in the bill (eat), plain takeaway cup skewered on the bill (coffee), incoming chips/battered scraps/bottlecaps on tight arcs (magnet), plain umbrella hooked over the gape (umbrella).
heron.anatomy: He has no hands, so the bill and the gape do every carry: the dagger skewers or grips, and food goes down the throat whole in one visible travelling lump. The wings only go up, out and forward-mantled over the crown — they never cross the chest, never point, never hold, and never take weight. Where Jimothy panics with his whole body, the heron panics from the ankles up: feet planted, face unchanged, stillness as the gag. Because his neck folds and extends, his total height is the one thing that can wreck the sheet — every frame is capped at about 1.15x the idle height so his head stays the same pixel size in all eighteen.

frames.desc: Standing square on both stilt legs, dead still, neck folded into a shallow S so the head rides low over the shoulders and the yellow dagger bill points level at the camera. Shaggy slate chest plumes hang without stirring, the single black crest feather trails off the back of the skull, the gold eye is fixed on the viewer and very slightly narrowed — nothing on him moves, and that is the pose.

The quiet frame: one leg vanished entirely up into the belly feathers, the whole bird settled into a soft grey bell on a single stilt, neck folded flat so the bill lies along the chest, eyes half-lidded. Rain beads on his back and the plumes puff over the tucked foot — a wet lawn ornament nobody is coming to look at. No loose feathers, nothing painted beneath him.

Bill tipped straight up with a plain paper cone of chips gripped in the bill tip and tipping its last inch down the throat, a fat comedy lump already halfway down the long neck and visibly stretching the feathers. Both feet planted, cone touching the bill and nothing spilled or scattered anywhere, one gold eye rolled down to hold eye contact with the camera the entire time he swallows.

Coiled to strike: hocks folded back deep, body dropped low over the toes, neck compressed into a tight spring-loaded Z with the bill aimed forward like a nocked arrow. Wings shut tight to the body, crest feather flattened back, gold eye wide and locked on the row ahead — all the energy stored, none of it leaked out yet.

Airborne with the wings only HALF-spread, wrists high and cupped and the primaries closed rather than fanned, and the long legs folded up tight under the belly instead of trailing. Neck tucked into the shoulders, bill forward, two or three flecks of loose down close in under his chest — this is a hop that never quite becomes flight, and the frame is no wider than idle.

Wings cupped forward to brake but still only half open, toes splayed enormous and reaching down, knees folding to absorb it, neck flung out forward for balance with the bill level. One tight white splash-ring bursting at the touching foot and physically touching it — no puddle, no pavement, no cast shadow.

Side-on to the right at a long heron stride, one leg fully extended forward and the other trailing straight back, wings cracked barely open as outriggers held close to the body, neck folded neatly into place. He is moving fast and looks like he is merely walking somewhere on purpose; a slight forward tilt is the only concession to speed. He carries nothing and has no asymmetric marking, so this frame mirrors cleanly.

Flat out: legs at full scissor stretch, body low and level, wings held half-open and steady, short white speed streaks touching his shins and a tight spray flicking off the back toe and staying attached to it. The neck stays folded and the face stays utterly composed — the legs are a blur, the head glides along a perfectly straight line.

Standing absolutely still and badly wired: the dagger bill run clean through the sip hole of a plain unmarked takeaway lid so the cup hangs skewered at eye level, pale blush-cream steam curling past the gold iris, coffee already running back down the bill. Feet planted and going nowhere, crest bolt upright, chest plumes fanned electric, pupil shrunk to a pinprick in a huge gold iris, one stilt leg blurred with vibration.

Feet rooted, bill cranked wide open at the sky like a delivery chute, gold eye huge and bright with pure astonishment as chips, battered scraps from a paper tray and gold bottlecaps spiral in on short tight arcs that all overlap his body, one chip already dropping down the gullet. Wings barely lifted — he has not taken a single step toward any of it, and he is quietly thrilled that he did not have to.

The umbrella's crook hooked over the base of his upper mandible right at the gape, shaft running up and back so the open canopy rides above and slightly behind his skull like a parasol on a stick. Bill level, gold eye clear and thoroughly smug under the rim, one leg tucked away, rain streaking off the canopy edge only — no dry circle, no pavement, no print on the fabric.

The instant of the hit: both wings mantled up and forward over the crown, wrists nearly meeting above the skull with the primaries curtaining down past his cheeks, and a bright blue-violet energy dome flaring tight around him with rain sparking off it. One gold eye peers out under the wrist, and his feet have not moved a millimetre from where they were.

Reed alarm, capped: neck stretched and slimmed to a stick but only about 1.15x the idle height, bill raised to roughly 60 degrees rather than vertical, every feather clamped flat to the body. Eyes rolled to the top of their sockets doing all the work, crest feather quivering, two thin nervous motion-ticks tight either side of the head — the most dignified terror in Seattle.

Sprinting at a full comic stride, wings half-open for balance, short red speed streaks touching both heels, two small exclamation ticks close over his head and a couple of body feathers shaken loose beside his flank. The neck is still folded and the bill still level — he is running for his life with his head travelling along a perfectly flat line, which somehow makes it worse.

The courtship display let loose but capped like leap: wings thrown up and out only HALF-spread, lacy chest plumes fanned into a shawl, head arched back and bill wide open in a great creaky rusty-gate honk, both feet finally off the ground by an inch. Rain-glitter close around him and no loose feathers; the whole frame stays inside the idle box — a lifetime of composure spent all at once.

He does not go feet-up, he FOLDS: collapsed straight down onto his keel like a deckchair, legs concertina'd underneath him, wings slack out to either side, neck poured down into a loose loop. Bill primly shut, eyes swooned to half-moon lids (no X's), three stars circling the skull — mortified, and quietly determined that nobody saw.

Sprawled on his side, neck gone completely loose in a dropped-garden-hose S, one wing trapped under him and the other folded up over the crown and drooping across one eye. Spiral eyes, bill hanging ajar, crest feather bent in three directions, both stilt legs crossed at the ankles in the air — nothing painted underneath him.

The instant of the burst: chest-deep in an exploding white and pale-cyan crown of water, one wing thrown up and the other half-spread slapping the surface, plumes plastered flat so the mighty neck reads as a soaked pipe cleaner. Bill wide open in an outraged squawk, gold eye enormous — a water bird betrayed by water and taking it extremely personally. He stays inside the crown; he is not going anywhere and he is certainly not going under.

sheetNotes: SCALE IS CHECKED ON THE HEAD, NOT THE FEET. The engine centres each sprite on the lane point and normalises every frame on its own, so the old 'lock the ground line' note is wrong: centre his body mass in the painted content of all 18 (including the wide ko/dizzy/splash frames), keep every frame between 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x the idle box, and paint him so his head is the same number of pixels in every frame.

NO GROUND PLANE ANYWHERE. No puddles, no dry circle under the umbrella, no wet pavement, no cast shadow, no storm drain, no spilled carton, no scattered chips. Only contact effects that physically touch him are allowed: the splash ring at the landing foot, the toe spray in dash-run, the water crown at his chest.

DETACHED ELEMENTS STAY CLOSE. Stars, exclamation ticks, speed streaks, magnet arcs, down flecks and steam must all sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, and nothing may touch a frame edge or a divider line — the crest plume and the toes are the parts most likely to stray into the gutter.

THIN PARTS DIE IN THE KNOCKOUT: the single black crest plume, the needle tip of the bill, the wire legs and the splayed toes. Paint every one of them a few pixels thicker than feels natural, and no aggressive despeckle or auto-trim — a heron missing a leg reads as a floating bird.

COLOUR LAW. The yellow dagger bill and the gold eye stay the highest-chroma thing in every frame, including under the canopy, under the dome and inside the water. Steam is pale blush-cream (green channel high), the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. .

NO LETTERING OF ANY KIND: plain cup, plain lid, plain paper cone, plain umbrella fabric, no logos, no headline, no branding. Loose feathers appear in exactly TWO frames — leap and flee — and nowhere else; on held frames like sit, ko and dizzy they read as plucked and injured, which is the opposite of the joke.

seal.stance: Pinniped, not quadruped and not biped: belly-down on his ribs in every frame, chest lifted only by the arch of his own spine, back half a heavy sausage that never leaves the ground except in leap, ko, dizzy and splash.
seal.wardrobe: None — he wears nothing in any frame; the only constants are bare silver-grey spotted hide, cream belly and a rain sheen along the spine. Every prop is single-frame and named in that frame: chip basket (eat), takeaway cup on the nose (coffee), flying chips and gold bottlecaps (magnet), black umbrella bitten by the shaft (umbrella, and the same umbrella blown inside out in shield). Nothing else appears anywhere.
seal.anatomy: He has no hands and no hind legs, so every raccoon solve is done with the belly: he balances things on his nose instead of holding them, pins things under a flat flipper instead of gripping, and rears only from the ribs up. LOCKED FLIPPER LAW — the fore-flippers reach OUT and DOWN only: they steady him at his flanks but never bear his weight (the chest comes up off the spinal arch, never off a propping flipper), never rise above the shoulder line, and never touch the face. When he is inverted in ko and splash, "out and down along the body" points at the sky, and that is the only way a flipper is ever up. He can never stand four-square and can never hold a prop in a limb.

frames.desc: Three-quarter to camera with the rear half foreshortened away so his box stays near square: chest lifted on the arch of his spine, fore-flippers lying flat at his flanks, head high and tipped a fraction back, big black wet eyes on the lens, whiskers relaxed. Rain sheen down the spine and the belly visibly flattened where it meets the ground — nothing painted underneath him, no smear, no puddle, no shadow.

Fully off duty in the harbour-seal banana, head and rear flippers lifted together so he rocks on his ribs, one fore-flipper laid low across his belly, eyes half shut and mouth curved in a small closed smile. This is the quiet one: he is looking past the camera up the canal at a boat that already went by, and the waiting is as real as the contentment.

Head thrown back mid-gulp with a battered cod half swallowed and its tail still out of his mouth, a red-and-white paper basket pinned flat under one fore-flipper against his chest — matchbox-sized against a seal — and one chip stuck to a whisker. A hard-edged gull-wing shadow falls across his own back and across the paper (no gull, and no shadow on the ground); he is side-eyeing it without stopping.

Poured flat and loaded forward: spine compressed into a low hump behind the shoulders, chin almost on the deck, fore-flippers flat and turned in at his sides steadying rather than pushing, rear half foreshortened toward camera, eyes locked up-screen. A tight fan of spray flicking off the outer edge of each fore-flipper where he has already begun to shove — touching him, nothing on the road.

Airborne and briefly beautiful: body arched into a shallow banana at three-quarter, fore-flippers swept tight to his sides, rear flippers trailing and fanned open, belly forward, mouth slightly open in delight. A compact burst of water breaking off his own belly and rear flippers with every droplet touching that mass — no trail, nothing reaching for the frame edge.

Belly-first touchdown, chest low, shoulders taking the whole weight, fore-flippers splayed out and down for balance, a ripple travelling backwards through his blubber, whiskers forward, eyes squeezed half shut. A low contact crown of water bursting at the impact and clinging to his chest, kept inside the same box as idle.

Side-on three-quarter travelling right mid-galumph: fore-flippers planted flat and turned out, spine humped into the inchworm arc, rear flippers whipping forward to catch up, head craned round just enough for the camera to get his face. Spray flicks off the flipper edges only — no drag streak, no wet road, and nothing asymmetric anywhere on him, because this frame gets mirrored.

The same galumph flat out — inchworm arc snapped straight at full extension, flippers blurred, eyes wide, mouth open in a bark of pure commitment. Warm orange-and-white speed streaks laid along his flanks and belly so they touch the hide, plus one short tight burst of water off the rear flippers; no rooster tail, no long trail.

He is NOT moving: planted dead still at three-quarter, chest up on the spinal arch, a lidded takeaway cup balanced perfectly on the very end of his nose because he cannot hold one, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, whiskers buzzing, mouth a tight flat line. Pale blush-cream steam off the lid (never pink), short warm fire licks and jitter ticks hugging his flanks — all the energy in the fur, none of it in travel.

Pure astonished delight: reared up from the ribs, mouth wide open, catching one hot chip clean out of the air, eyes enormous and lit up like the world just started working. Chips, fries and gold bottlecaps spiral inward on a tight orbit that overlaps his body all the way round, each piece touching the next so the ring cuts as one mass; no live fish, no spilled basket, nothing on the ground.

A big black umbrella bitten by the SHAFT just under the canopy and laid back along his own spine so it rides over his shoulders like a lean-to roof, handle dangling past his chest; it covers his head and shoulders and comes nowhere near his back half, which is getting hammered. He is propped at three-quarter under the front rim looking straight down the lens, half-lidded and deeply smug — he does not need it and he knows it — rain sluicing off the canopy behind him, no dry patch, no ground.

The hit lands: a bright blue-violet dome flares tight around him (never violet, never dark), and he turtles — chin jammed into his chest, neck compressed to nothing, whiskers flattened back, eyes screwed shut, fore-flippers clamped flat to his flanks. The umbrella is still in his teeth and blown clean inside out, ribs snapped upward into a bowl above him — the prop never leaves his body, and the whole thing stays inside the idle envelope.

Reared as high as a seal can rear: chest and neck stretched straight up while the back half stays a heavy sausage, foreshortened toward camera to keep the box near square. Head cranked back at the sky, eyes enormous, whiskers splayed, fore-flippers pinned in tight and low against his chest — only the top third of him is physically capable of panic.

Galumphing away in complete undignified terror, spine buckling in a big travelling wave, blubber a beat behind the motion, one rear flipper flailing clear, mouth open in a bark, head glancing back over his shoulder. Warm red-orange speed streaks painted onto his flanks and two small wordless shock marks tucked in close behind his head so they overlap his silhouette and survive the cut.

The money shot — the one job his body is better at than anyone else's on the roster: reared up tall on his belly, head thrown back, mouth wide open barking with joy, both fore-flippers caught mid-clap LOW across his chest at belly height where a seal actually claps, never overhead. Water flicks off the flipper tips and a couple of gold sparks are caught between them, all of it touching him, and the reach stays inside the idle box so his head does not shrink.

Rolled onto his back on the road with all four flippers hanging out and up — inverted, so that is simply out-and-down along his body — tongue out the side, eyes closed into swooning half-moons (never X's), a ring of stars circling his head with each star touching the next so the ring cuts as one piece. One rear flipper crossed lazily over the other: he looks suspiciously comfortable, as though the nap was always the plan.

Belly-down and splayed, turning slowly flat on the spot like a compass needle that has lost north — he is a torpedo, never a coin balanced on edge — spiral eyes, tongue lolling, whiskers bent the wrong way. Motion arcs curl off both fore-flipper tips with a short spray ring flicking off them and a few sweeper bristles and grit grazing his flank, everything touching him; nothing whatsoever painted on the road.

Buoyant and furious: rolled onto his back inside a bursting white-blue-grey crown of water and carried off sideways at speed, whiskers bent back, one fore-flipper folded on his chest and the other flung out in a can-you-believe-this appeal to nobody, wearing an expression of enormous personal offence — this half of the map was supposed to be his. He rides high in the froth the whole time, mass centred, crown kept tight and well clear of every frame edge.

sheetNotes: ENVELOPE, the one checkable rule: match the four existing frames at 219x178 (aspect 1.23). Every frame including its effects must land between 1.0:1 and 1.3:1, and his HEAD must be the same number of pixels in all 18. Stage him three-quarter with the rear half foreshortened toward camera in every frame — a flat side-on seal reads 1.7:1 and the engine then draws him 74 wide by about 43 tall while cheer draws 59 tall, so his head visibly changes size mid-animation.

NEVER PAINT THE FLOOR — this is the single biggest hazard on this character. No damp smear under the belly, no drag streak behind the galumph, no skid marks, no dry patch under the canopy, no ground-level gull shadow, no puddle, no cast shadow. The cutter is a magenta border flood and every one of those survives as a detached grey stain floating under a bottomless seal, and it drags the centre-anchor so he lifts off his lane line. His wetness reads through the sheen ON his hide and the flattened blubber contact line. Contact spray that touches his body is correct and wanted. The engine already draws its own ellipse shadow under him in drawCritter — a painted one double-stacks.

Detached bits — droplets, bottlecaps, sparks, stars, grit, shock marks — must sit within half a body width, overlap his bounding box, and chain to him or to each other. The cut is a connected-components pass: a loose speck either disappears or is emitted as its own sprite file.

COLOUR: the knockout eats the magenta family, so no pink steam (paint it pale blush-cream with the green channel high) and Water is white-blue-grey. At 59px his silver-grey hide is almost exactly the colour of wet asphalt, so the cream belly and a bright rim light along the spine have to be present in all 18 or he vanishes into the lane.

LAYOUT: divider lines, never an even grid. Rows of three with generous white rulings and a visible margin inside them — nothing touches a divider or a frame edge, including the umbrella canopy, the inside-out umbrella bowl and the splash crown. His long silhouette will overrun any fixed grid and the cutter will slice him in half.

ENGINE ASKS for the owner: set scale:1.10 on the seal entry in CHARS (index.html:715) — painting him bigger on the sheet does literally nothing, because each frame is normalised independently. Add full:1 only once all 18 land, and make sure the mirror fallback for full characters is in before that, or every leftward hop drops to the procedural blob. The four existing frames (idle, crouch, leap, land) are the reference for camera height, hide colour, spot pattern and spray language; match them exactly.
Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for a 59px cut test before committing the other fifteen — they are the three most likely to blow the envelope.

coyote.stance: QUADRUPED, locked: a digitigrade canid who stands and moves on four toes-down feet in all eighteen frames — he never rises onto two legs, never has a free "hand", and the only frames where he is off his feet are leap, ko, dizzy and splash.
coyote.wardrobe: NONE — no clothes, no permanent prop, jaws empty and nothing underfoot in fifteen of eighteen frames; the only props on the whole sheet are the torn takeout bag + one long fry (eat), the sleeved paper cup (coffee), the incoming bottlecaps and fries (magnet), and ONE umbrella that appears in exactly two frames (umbrella, shield) and never once leaves his teeth.
coyote.anatomy: He has no hands, so every raccoon pose that holds something becomes jaws-and-forepaw: the cup and the umbrella are carried in the teeth, the takeout bag is pinned flat under one splayed forepaw, and every "raise your arms" beat becomes something a canid actually does — cheer is a full howl, scared is hackles up with one forepaw lifted, ko is belly-up with all four legs folded in the air. He is DIGITIGRADE, the exact opposite of Jimothy: toes down, heel and hock never touching, no flat palms, no grip, no thumb. Standing rules a painter must not break — all four feet stay under him at rest, a prop in any standing frame lives in the JAWS and never becomes a fifth limb, and the black-tipped brush tail must physically touch the body silhouette in every single frame or the connected-component cut orphans it and ships a coyote with no tail.

frames.desc: Standing four-square in three-quarter view, weight settled on straight forelegs, tall ears pricked with one rotated slightly off-axis as if already tracking the next lane, gold eyes level with the camera. Brush tail hangs low with its black tip well clear of the bottom of the frame, mouth closed in that faint unbothered line, jaws empty and nothing underfoot — no pavement, no shadow, no puddle.

Sat back on his haunches, forelegs straight and tidy, chest high, brush tail curled around his front feet with the black tip laid over one paw. Head turned three-quarters away with ears half-back and one gold eye catching low dawn light, the gaze aimed off at something the sheet never paints — the patrol briefly off duty, and this is the one quiet, lonely frame on the sheet.

Hunkered over a torn paper takeout bag pinned flat under one splayed forepaw, head swung back around to camera mid-chew with a single long fry held crosswise in his teeth the way a dog carries a stick it will not give back, one end drooping. Ears up, eyes half-lidded and entirely unrepentant; every remaining fry stays inside the mouth of the bag under his paw, nothing scattered loose outside his outline.

Coiled to launch: chest dropped low, elbows out, hindquarters bunched high over gathered back feet, tail carried low with the black tip curving up to touch his own rump. Ears flat forward, gold eyes locked up-screen, a few grains of grit ticking off the back paw and still touching it — nothing painted beneath him.

A GATHERED bound, not a stretched one: spine folded, forelegs reaching with the elbows kept in, hind legs tucked up under the belly, brush tail curved up and touching his back so the whole shape stays compact and roughly square. Ears back, mouth just open in the private delight of a working animal who is very good at exactly one thing and knows nobody is watching — he is commuting, not hunting.

Forepaws slapped down and splayed wide, shoulders sunk between them absorbing the drop, hindquarters still coming down behind and the tail flicked up against his flank for balance. Ears snapped forward, a tight burst of rain-spray and grit bursting AT the pads and touching them, spreading no wider than his own chest.

Side-on facing RIGHT in a compact diagonal trot, near foreleg and far hind leg swinging together with the stride kept short of full reach, head carried dead level, tail low and steady. Chin up, unhurried — the posture of a coyote who is not crossing the street so much as permitting it — with a thin veil of pale dawn mist lying right along his back.

Same side-on RIGHT and flat out, but painted at the GATHERED moment of the gallop: all four feet off the ground with the spine folded and the legs collected under him, tail curved up against the rump. Ears pinned, eyes wide, tongue just out, three or four short warm-white speed ticks starting at his heels and touching them — no long trail, no grit under the belly.

He is NOT running — all four feet planted and dead still, the whole body vibrating in place, because the engine holds this frame for up to seven seconds while the player stands there. A paper cup clamped by its cardboard sleeve in his teeth with the lid dented by tooth marks and PALE CREAM steam curling off it, pupils shrunk to pinpricks in the gold eyes, hackles standing in a dark ridge, tail up but angled back, jitter lines hugging his outline and small orange heat licks touching all four paws.

Up on his toes with weight rocked back and ears up, gold eyes wide with plain astonished joy as a gold bottlecap arrives right at the tip of his nose entirely by itself — he is not snatching, it is coming to him, and he cannot believe his luck. More bottlecaps and fries curve in on a tight spiral that stays within half a body width and overlaps his outline everywhere, tail sweeping a happy blur.

Standing four-square and bone dry, biting the umbrella SHAFT high — an inch or two under the canopy — so the open umbrella sits on top of his skull like a hat and the curved crook dangles down past his brisket. Head tilted slightly to balance it, ears dry under the rim, eyes half-lidded and insufferably pleased, short rain ticks streaking off both sides of the canopy; no puddle, no wet ground, nothing beneath his paws.

Braced and dropped low with forelegs splayed, head twisted away, eyes squeezed shut and ears pinned flat — and the umbrella STILL in his teeth, blown completely inside out over his skull, which is the joke. A blue-violet dome flares tight around him with rain and grit streaking off its skin: never violet, never dark, and never further off his fur than a hand's width.

Rocked back on his haunches in three-quarter view, chest lifted, one forepaw held up and out to the SIDE and the head craned up and back on an angle rather than stacked straight up, so the frame stays no taller than idle. Ears flat to his skull, hackles spiked into a dark ridge along the spine, tail tucked hard forward between the hind legs, gold eyes enormous and rimmed with white.

Full gallop to the LEFT, belly low, legs at reach but the hind pair folding under him and the brush tail curved and touching the rump so the shape never stretches into a horizontal streak. Ears pinned, mouth open in a thoroughly undignified yelp, three short warm-white ticks off his heels — all that athleticism, none of the composure — and nothing floating above his shoulders.

Front paws planted wide in three-quarter view, chest thrown out, head tipped all the way back with the muzzle pointed up in a full howl, eyes shut, ears laid back, tail high and waving. Three short song-lines curl out of his open mouth and stay touching the muzzle — no arm to raise, so he raises his voice.

Flat on his back with all four legs folded loosely in the air, tongue out one side, dazed swooning half-moon lids (never X eyes, never spirals — spirals belong to dizzy), one ear folded inside out against his own skull and the brush tail flopped along his flank inside the silhouette. A tight ring of small gold stars orbits close enough to overlap his head; the read is mortified professional dignity — the animal who never misses, caught belly-up.

Sprawled on his side with his legs still walking on nothing, spiral eyes and tongue lolling, his whole coat combed into ridiculous swirls and cowlicks by the sweeper brushes. Top ear flops back while the under ear squashes flat, tail lies in line with the body, and two wet leaves stay stuck flat IN the combed fur — no circling stars here, and no pile of sweepings on any ground.

The instant of the burst: head and shoulders exploding up inside a tight white and pale-cyan crown of water, forelegs flung high, ears pinned, gold eyes huge and mouth open in pure offended shock — soaked, out of play, and deeply insulted about it. Fur plastered so his legs and ruff read half their usual fluffy width while the HEAD stays exactly the same size as every other frame, brush tail hanging as a sad wet rope still touching his body.

sheetNotes: CANVAS IS THE WHOLE TRICK: cut the sheet, then re-pad all 18 PNGs to ONE identical canvas. His four existing frames are 214x250 (aspect 0.86) — that is the box, and same canvas plus same painted head size is the only thing that actually passes the head-pixel test, because the engine normalises every frame independently.

Every pose therefore has to be GATHERED to fit that box. For scale, Jimothy's own leap PNG is 215x210 and his widest frame of twenty is dash-run at 236x178 (1.33). A stretched, tail-streaming coyote leap measures 2.2:1 and would draw him at roughly 40% of his idle height for the middle half of every hop, popping back up on landing. Paint idle, leap and cheer FIRST and send those three for a 59px lane check before committing the other fifteen.

NO GROUND ANYWHERE on this sheet — no wet asphalt, no puddle under the umbrella, no cast shadow, no fries scattered by his toes, no drift of sweepings behind dizzy. The cutter is a magenta border flood that keeps every non-magenta island, so each of those ships as floating grey scum beneath an animal with no floor. Spray that TOUCHES his paws (land, crouch grit, splash crown) is correct and wanted.
EFFECT COLOUR LAW: pale cream steam on the coffee cup (NOT pink), warm-white speed ticks, gold stars, and a bright blue-violet shield dome. The k.

Loose pieces — the ko star ring, the magnet spiral, the cheer song-lines — must sit within half a body width AND overlap his outline, and this sheet must be cut on painted white divider lines rather than component detection or each of them ships as its own sprite. Keep a clear magenta margin all the way round; nothing touches an edge or a divider.

At 59px his entire identity is four things: tall ears, dark ruff and saddle, black tail tip, two gold eyes. Never crop an ear tip, keep the eyes the brightest note on him in all eighteen (including upside down in ko and soaked in splash). Direction: run-r and dash-run face RIGHT, flee faces LEFT — do not paint all three the same way round — and still ship a run-l file as a flipped export of run-r, because a fully animated character with no run-l falls through to the procedural blob on every leftward hop.

salmon.stance: No limbs and no feet: at rest he rears bolt upright on a fanned tail fin in a deep S-curve, a leap he never finished, and that tail-stand is his standing pose in every non-travel frame — travel is always a flip, never a run.
salmon.wardrobe: In all 18 frames: spawning colours worn as the costume (crimson flank #d4685e, warm peach belly #f2b3a2, olive-green humped back and hooked kype) plus one snapped brass spoon lure tangled around — never through — the dorsal fin on a short frayed leader; the cheap black umbrella is the only other prop and it exists in frames 11 and 12 only.
salmon.anatomy: A salmon has no hands, so every raccoon pose is solved by the spine: the body curls, coils, arches and corkscrews, and the gill covers plus the one visible eye carry all the emotion. Pectoral fins sit low and BEHIND the gill covers and swing fore-and-aft through a few degrees only — they can never reach the eye, the top of the head, or under him as a weight-bearing prop, and they can never hold anything; anything he "carries" is hooked on the tip of the kype, stuck flat to the wet flank, tangled in the dorsal, or climbed into. He rears very tall, which blows the sizing envelope, so the painted box is held near square by making the S-curve deeper or shallower — never by shrinking the fish. Nose-to-tail and head size stay identical in all 18 frames; the head is the checkable proof.

frames.desc: Reared bolt upright on his fanned tail fin in a deep S, both pectorals held low and out for balance, olive kype level, the one big round eye fixed calmly on the viewer. Baked in: a wobble blur at the tail tip, rain beading down the crimson flank, the brass lure swaying on its leader against the dorsal — water only where it touches him, no puddle, no asphalt.

Balance abandoned: slumped onto his side and curled into a comma, gills working slow, tail fin idly slapping, one eye turned up into the rain, half-lidded and quietly melancholy. The frayed leader has coiled across his own belly with the lure resting on the flank, and a thin sheen of water clings to his underside without spreading past his outline.

Curled tight around a soggy paper tray of chips pressed against his own body, kype clamped sideways on a single chip like a caught minnow, eye blissfully shut, ketchup on the chin, lure glinting on the dorsal above.
