A real mayfly hovers an inch off his nose and is completely ignored — the one meal he was built for, and he has chosen chips.

Compressed into a tight loaded C, nose down, tail wound under him, pectorals flattened hard to the flank, the one eye locked up-screen, the whole body a spring at full compression. Water squeezes out along his belly line as a tight collar that touches him all the way round; the lure is pinned flat to the dorsal by the compression.

HORIZONTAL frame, deliberately not cheer: a long low crescent travelling across the cell, tail kicked straight out behind, jaw SHUT, pale peach belly turned to camera, every scale catching the streetlight — pure speed, no celebration. A short sheet of water peels off the flank into a rope of droplets that stays on his body, lure streaming back along the dorsal.

Belly-flop: body slapped flat, head reared up with the jaw open in a silent oof, tail still up in the air a beat behind him so the box stays near square. A crown of splash bursts sideways right at his belly and stops there — no ripple, no ring, no wet road — and the lure has flipped forward over his shoulder on its leader.

Mid-flip to the right, body arced into a working comma, humped back cresting, one pectoral shoving off low while the tail whips through, head craned right, eye set and businesslike. Spray kicks off the tail close behind him and the lure and frayed leader swing back on the same beat.

The same flip flat out: body stretched long, two or three tight afterimages of the tail beat, jaw clamped, eye wild, a short rooster-tail of spray at the tail. Warm orange speed streaks run along the flank and off the tail — never under his belly, there is no road — and the lure is snapped straight out behind on a taut leader.

A STANDING frame, held up to seven seconds: planted on his tail and going nowhere, a takeaway cup hooked on the very tip of his kype and hanging clear to one side so the face stays open, coffee slopping over the rim. The whole body vibrates to a blur at the edges — gill covers flared, eye enormous with a pinprick pupil, jitter lines at the tail tip — with pale blush-cream steam (never pink) lifting off the cup and off his own hot flank.

Reared up on his tail with the jaw dropped open in flat astonishment — delight, not appetite — eye huge and shining as gold bottlecaps and chips spiral in on a short tight golden vortex that hugs his body. Four caps have already stuck flat to the wet flank like coins on glass, and the lure lifts on its leader as if it wants in too.

He has flipped a cheap black umbrella canopy-up, let it fill with rainwater and climbed in — a fish in a bathtub — with the tub tipped toward camera so his whole head, kype, gill covers and dorsal ride clear above the rim, one eye half-lidded and unbearably smug. Canopy no wider than about 1.2x his tail-stand box so the crimson body beats the black bowl; lure and leader hang over the rim.

The instant of impact: the umbrella-tub slammed sideways, water sheeting out over the bent ribs, and a blue-violet dome (never blue-violet, it gets eaten by the cut) flaring tight around fish and umbrella together. Body arched hard, pectorals splayed stiff and low, eye squeezed shut, rain streaking off the dome in bright lines, the lure flung up against the inside of it.

Rigid as a bowling pin on his tail and leaning back past vertical, dorsal fin snapped bolt upright with the lure standing up in it, both pectorals flared stiff and LOW like flinched shoulders, gill covers wide, mouth a tiny O, the one eye rolled straight up. A gull's wing shadow falls across his crimson flank only — never on any ground — and one bead of water flicks off the trembling tail tip.

Full panic flop up-frame: body zig-zagged mid-slap, three tail beats blurring, mouth wide in a silent scream, panic bubbles bursting from the gill covers, lure whipping loose behind. Three or four short run-off streaks that start and end ON his body run down past him while he angles up against them — no background wash, no symbols, no lettering.

VERTICAL, the money frame and the opposite silhouette to leap: reared at full stretch bolt upright on a fanned tail, body quivering, jaw wide open in a joyful gasp, gill covers flared pink, every scale lit gold by hard backlight. The thrown water is only a contact burst at the tail base, no more than a third of his height, and the battered lure hangs off the dorsal catching the light like a medal. He got upstream.

Flat on his side in a puddle an inch too shallow to be dignified, gills still working, one pectoral flopped limp against the gill plate where it actually lands, jaw open with one fat comic bubble at the corner, small stars circling close over his head — embarrassed, not hurt. The brass lure has swung round on its leader and lies across his eye like a hat pulled down; rain lands ON him and a thin sheen of water hugs his outline, with no water painted anywhere it does not touch him.

Wrung into a hard corkscrewed C with the tail crossing PAST his head so the fin ends up beside his own jaw and the face rotates to camera — never wrapped around his own girth — both eyes spiralled, jaw hanging, gills fluttering. Wet leaves and stiff sweeper bristles stuck all over the flank with the lure tangled in among them, and a small tight tornado of litter and orbiting stars kept close enough to overlap his body; nothing on the ground.

The burst: he explodes up inside a white crown of storm water in a joy-roll, body twisted, tumbling and clearly knocked off his line rather than swimming, crown no wider than about 1.2x his idle box. Gills finally flared pink and working properly, eye wide with relief, lure flicking off the flank on its leader, streetlight refracting gold through the spray — the one death on the sheet that is secretly a homecoming, and he is still out of the game.

sheetNotes: NO GROUND ANYWHERE. The draft's puddle rings, gutter puddle, rain rings, ripple across the puddle, wet asphalt, storm drain and speed streaks 'under his belly' all survive the magenta flood as floating grey scum under a fish with no floor. Water, spray, steam and streaks are legal ONLY where they touch his body.

Envelope: hold every painted box between about 0.80:1 and 1.35:1 and inside about 1.2x the idle box. A reared fish goes far too tall — control the box with the depth of the S-curve, never by shrinking him. The head must measure the same pixels in all 18 frames; if an effect shrinks the head, the effect is too big.

Detached elements (stars, litter tornado, mayfly, magnet spiral, bottlecaps in flight) must sit within half a body width AND overlap his bounding box, or the connected-components cut emits them as their own sprite or drops them.
Nothing readable anywhere. The flee exclamation marks are deleted on purpose — replaced with gill-cover bubbles. Litter, leaves, caps and the lure read as shape and texture only.

Crop hazards are the tail fin tip, the frayed leader and the lure. Lay out with white divider lines and generous UNEVEN gaps, never a fixed grid, and leave clear magenta margin on all four sides of every cell — a grid will slice a tail fin clean off.
salmon.runL: Paint run-l separately: the lure and its frayed leader hang off one flank and the kype hooks one way, so a mirrored run-r jumps the lure across the dorsal and swaps the eye to the far side on every leftward hop while the other seventeen frames never move it.

orca.stance: His own thing — a beached orca: belly flat on the road at rest, fluke as both engine and brake, and every lift is a SPINE-arch with the flippers flared out sideways as balance outriggers, never as legs.
orca.wardrobe: One short frond of honey-brown bull kelp looped over the base of the dorsal fin and lying flat down both flanks — mid-value so it still reads as a band under any shop finish — and that is the entire wardrobe, present in all 18; the only other props are per-frame: paper chip tray (eat), takeaway cup plus two crumpled empties (coffee), patio umbrella (umbrella and shield).
orca.anatomy: Every raccoon pose is rebuilt from four parts: a fluke that is both the engine and the push-point, an enormous belly he travels on, two stiff pectoral flippers, and a dorsal fin that carries his whole mood. STANDING RULE ONE — the pectorals are low-set paddles with no elbow and no weight-bearing role: they flare OUT and DOWN as outriggers with the tips just kissing the asphalt, and they never go underneath him, never in front of or across the face, never above the head, and never hold anything against gravity. STANDING RULE TWO — every rear is a spine rear: a big arch from mid-body, chin thrown high, chest sliding up off the road with the fluke jammed down behind as the push point, silhouette of a rising black wave with two wings, never a propped-up sea lion. He does not hop, he porpoises in wet galumphing belly-arcs, and props are wedged behind the fin, laid on the flat of a flipper, or carried crosswise in the teeth — never gripped.

frames.desc: Belly flat to the road in three-quarter view, near flipper laid forward on the asphalt, fluke curled loose behind, dorsal fin upright with the notch clean against the sky and the kelp glossy over its base. White eye patch bright, mouth a small closed smile, rain beading across the wet black hide, and only a thin lace of contact spray where his belly meets the ground — no puddle.

The quiet frame: a low spine-arch lifts his chest a few inches clear, fluke laid flat behind, both flippers slack out to the sides, dorsal fin tipping with the lean and the kelp hanging limp down his flank. Head turned away, chin low, eyes half-shut and far off — a pod animal listening for a pod that is not there.

Chin up on a low spine-arch with a battered fish-and-chips cod hanging crosswise out of his grin because he has nothing to hold it with, the soggy paper tray tipped up against his near flipper and chips stuck to the white of his jaw. The tray is no bigger than his eye patch; kelp flat along his back, rain pocking the hide.

Loaded and compressed: the whole mass pressed low, chin down, flippers flared hard out to either side with the tips just kissing the asphalt, fluke cocked up and back like a spring, dorsal fin raked forward with the gather and the kelp bunched at its base. A tight collar of spray squeezes out along the contact line under his belly; eyes locked forward, mouth a flat determined line.

A three-quarter porpoise arcing toward the camera on a shallow diagonal — head near and large, back arched, fluke kicked small and far behind so the body foreshortens into the landscape box — flippers flared wide as wings, white belly turned to the viewer, kelp lifted along his spine. Short sheets of water peel off his flanks and one small burst ring hangs tight at his tail; jaws open in absolute delight, eyes squeezed into happy crescents.

Belly-first touchdown: chin down, jowls squashed flat against the road, flippers braced forward and splayed, fluke slapping down behind, kelp thrown forward over the fin. A fat crown of street water bursts sideways along his contact line and clings to his sides, and he blinks half-shut, entirely pleased with the mess he has made.

Full side profile travelling right in a long low galumphing arc, body barely clearing the road, near flipper reaching forward to pull and the far one paddling back, fluke kicked up mid-stroke, notch and kelp reading clean along the top of the silhouette. Spray fans off his belly as a short attached fringe — he carries no prop of any kind in this frame, and there is no skid line, wake or puddle behind him.

The same galumph flat out: body stretched long and low, fluke a blur, both flippers slapping hard, kelp streaming tight along his flank, jaw open in a huge grin and eyes wide. Speed streaks rake short and tight against his flanks and the thrown water is cropped to a stubby attached rooster tail at his hip — nothing trailing off toward the frame edge.

A STANDING frame — he is not travelling: belly planted dead flat, body held still and vibrating in place, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, dorsal fin quivering between short jitter marks and the kelp trembling with it. A tiny takeaway cup sits on the broad flat of his near flipper like a side table with pale blush-cream steam curling off it, two crumpled empties tucked in against that flipper's edge, and warm heat licks flickering along his contact line.

A big spine-arch rear — chin high, chest sliding up off the road, fluke jammed down behind as the push point, flippers flared wide as outriggers with the tips only brushing the asphalt — jaws open in astonished joy, eyes round and shining, kelp slipped back along the arch. Gold bottlecaps, chips and fries spiral in tight against his chest and around the curve of his back, close enough to overlap him and glinting hard on all that black.

A full-size café patio umbrella, shaft wedged behind the dorsal fin and lashed there with his own kelp, raked hard forward so the canopy sits over his skull like a hat brim with rain sheeting off the rim in bright arcs. Head and shoulders dry while the entire rest of that enormous back is still being hammered; half-lidded eyes, faintest smug smile — the canopy has to read as a roof in pure silhouette at 59px.

The instant he eats a hit: chin jammed into his chest, head turned hard away from the impact, both flippers swept forward and cupped either side of the skull like blinkers, tips almost meeting but plainly framing the face rather than covering it. A bright blue-violet dome flares white-hot at the contact point with rain streaking off it, his mass shoved back a few inches with scraped spray at the belly line, one eye screwed shut, and the umbrella still lashed to the fin but blown inside out.

A spine-arch rear staged as a steep diagonal, never a vertical column: chest up, fluke jammed down behind, flippers flared out and trembling with tips barely touching, head craned back and up at the sky. Eyes huge and perfectly round, mouth a tiny O in all that black bulk, kelp standing on end and a single bead of sweat flicking off his brow.

Galumphing away hard to the left in a flat panic, mouth wide, flippers flailing out of rhythm, fluke thrashing, dorsal fin leaning steeply into the turn and the kelp whipped back against his flank. Two fat exclamation marks sit tight over his shoulders overlapping his back, short red speed streaks rake his flanks, eyes white-rimmed and locked forward.

A breach angled straight at the viewer on a leaning diagonal — front end thrown up and toward the camera, chin high, both flippers flung wide and open, jaws wide in a joyful open-mouthed shout, kelp flung up off the fin base but still looped on. A tight crown of spray bursts at the bottom of his own silhouette where the fluke slapped, a few gold bottlecaps confetti in close over his back, warm light catching the rain on all that wet black.

Rolled onto his side, white belly to the viewer, flippers limp in the air, fluke flopped over, dorsal fin lying flat sideways with the notch still readable and the kelp slid down over one brow. Eyes shut into swooning upturned half-moons, mouth slack in a small sheepish smile, three stars circling his head — wounded dignity, not injury, and nothing whatsoever painted on the road beneath him.

Sprawled belly-down in a loose S, spiral eyes, tongue lolling out one side of his jaw, dorsal fin bent right over like a wilted leaf with the kelp slipped down around his chin. Both flippers splayed uselessly out to the sides and three short wobble arcs tucked in against his cheek — spirals only, no stars, and no swept leaves or litter.

The instant of the burst: a white crown of floodwater explodes up around him and he is wedged in it to the shoulders, flippers flung up, a short spout puffing off his blowhole, kelp plastered flat and wet. Face caught between shock and a huge daft grin — the biggest animal in the game has finally found water and it only comes up to his chest — stuck fast and plainly out of play; he never sinks and never goes under.

sheetNotes: ONE BOX FOR ALL 18. Paint every cel into the same 230 x 185 landscape frame, aspect about 1.24. The engine width-sizes anything over 1.12 and height-sizes everything else, so a single cel that drifts under 1.20 snaps him to a different size mid-animation: never taller than wide, and never in the 1.00-1.19 dead band. The checkable test is his HEAD — same number of pixels in all eighteen. Measure him snout-to-fluke, not by the bounding box, because spray and the umbrella will fool a size-match by eye.

NO GROUND, ANYWHERE, IN ANY FRAME. The cutter floods magenta and keeps every non-magenta island, so puddles, spreading water, skid lines, swept leaves, dropped cups and cast shadows all survive as floating grey scum — and because they sit below him they drag the centre-anchor and float him above his lane line. Every puddle in the previous draft (idle, sit, magnet, ko) and all ground scatter (coffee's tipped empties, dizzy's swept litter, run-r's skid line) is deleted. Wet sheen on the hide plus contact spray that physically touches the body is the entire vocabulary.

READABILITY IS THE WHOLE BATTLE. He is #14161a on wet black asphalt and the shop finishes darken him further. Every frame needs a cool bright rim running the length of his back and dorsal fin, a white spray or steam edge breaking his outline somewhere, and the mid-value kelp band across the fin base. All FX in white, cream, cyan and pale blue — the knockout eats the magenta family, so no hot-pink steam (the draft's coffee steam is.

THE NOTCH IS HIS NAME. The notch in the trailing edge of the dorsal fin is his ID the way a hard hat is somebody else's: same edge, same position, all 18. Leave clear magenta margin above the fin so the crop never shaves it, and keep every cel well inside its divider lines — nothing touches an edge or a gutter, because the divider lines get trimmed by an inset and anything near one merges two cells into one sprite.

DETACHED BITS STAY CLOSE. Bottlecaps, chips, stars, exclamation marks, wobble arcs, spray and the crumpled empties must all sit within half a body width AND overlap his silhouette, or they cut out as separate sprites and shrink the animal. Nothing on this sheet carries readable text: the cup, the chip tray and the umbrella are pattern, colour and shape only.

TWO ENGINE ASKS AND A PAINT ORDER. Set CHARS scale 1.25 on orca (index.html:719 currently has none) — painting him bigger on the sheet does literally nothing because each cel is normalised on its own. Paint idle, leap and cheer FIRST and cut them at 59px on a real lane before committing the other fifteen. And nobody on this roster is food: eat and magnet use battered cod, chips, fries and bottlecaps, never a salmon or any silver fish, because the Sockeye is a playable castmate.
orca.runL: Mirror — run-r is deliberately prop-free and bilaterally clean (no cup, no umbrella, kelp draped centrally over the fin base onto both flanks, and the notch is in the fin's trailing edge so it flips true), so ship run-l as a flipped duplicate PNG rather than a repaint; it must exist as a file, because full characters do not auto-mirror and a missing run-l drops him to the procedural blob on every leftward hop.

ghost.stance: Quadruped at rest — a plantigrade raccoon, four-square with flat palms, five long spread fingers and heels down, hovering a thumb's width above a ground that is never painted; he rears onto his hind legs ONLY in the frames that say so (coffee, magnet, umbrella, scared, cheer) and sits on his haunches in sit and eat.
ghost.wardrobe: No costume and no permanent prop — he is bare; the only constants are anatomical (bone-white bleached fur, dark bandit mask, near-black OPAQUE sooty paws, faded stubby ringed tail, blue-white fray at shoulders, hips and tail tip), and there are exactly three frame-local props: a plain unprinted fry carton (eat, magnet), a plain unprinted takeaway cup (coffee) and one small umbrella (umbrella), each gripped in an opaque dark paw and touching the body.
ghost.anatomy: He is a raccoon, so Jimothy's staging transfers pose-for-pose; the translation here is weight and opacity, not skeleton. Plantigrade in all eighteen — flat palms, five long spread fingers, heel down, never knuckles. Body canon holds: round and spherical, no visible neck, head perched high above the shoulders, long skinny limbs and a STUBBY tail in every frame — the vapour streams, the tail never does. The standing rule is that nothing bears weight: toes hang slack, no limb compresses, there is no cast shadow anywhere, and he never floats higher than the thumb's width he already floats — the float lives in the pose, not in extra height.

frames.desc: Four-square and plantigrade three-quarters to camera — bone-white bleached fur, dark bandit mask, stubby ringed tail, and near-black sooty paws as the only fully opaque part of him. Nothing takes weight: toes hang slack, no limb compresses, no shadow, just a thin ice-blue underglow touching the pads, and his big dark eyes are calm and faintly apologetic, like he knows he shouldn't be here.

The quiet frame: sitting up on his haunches, dark paws folded on his belly, eyes half-closed, content but a shade lonely. His backside never quite settles and his hind feet hang slack; the wisps rising off his shoulders curl up and fold back into his ruff, never off the top of the frame.

Sitting with a plain unprinted fry carton tipped against his chest, one sooty paw holding a fry at his mouth that never gets any shorter. A second fry has already fallen through him and lies solid and gold on his lap fur, a faint pale-blue trail down his chest marking the way it went; cheerful and mildly puzzled.

Flattened low, haunches up, forepaws braced wide with flat palms and five long spread fingers, eyes forward and huge. Nothing is compressed — the belly hangs clear and the gathered spring reads as ice-blue vapour clinging to his underside and streaming a short, tight way back off his hips.

Fully airborne, limbs spread, belly forward, mouth open and delighted, stretched further than a solid raccoon could manage. Face and forepaws stay crisp; the hind legs give out into a blue-white vapour trail no longer than a third of his body, and the tail itself stays stubby — the vapour streams, the tail does not.

Forepaws down flat, palms and fingers spread, body low, whiskers forward, eyes startled that anything was there to land on. There is no impact: the trailing wisps fold forward and curl UP around his wrists and forelegs, attached to him — no ring, scuff or mist spreading out across a floor.

Side-on travel right, body low, legs at full extension, the near-black plantigrade paws the only solid things in the painting. His hind quarter smears into pale blue fog with exactly ONE afterimage, offset a quarter of a body width so the two silhouettes overlap heavily; stubby tail throughout.

Flat-out sprint right, legs stretched, eyes wide, mouth open — where Jimothy throws warm fire he throws cold: short ice-white contrails off the heels and frost flecks that touch his hocks. His rear third has gone to vapour but is still opaque paint inside a continuous rim, with one heavily overlapping afterimage and nothing loose in the margin.

A STANDING frame — he is holding still and vibrating: reared up on his hind legs, both sooty paws clamped round a plain unprinted takeaway cup at his chest, fur bristled, pupils shrunk to pinpricks, short jitter lines ticking off his ears and shoulders. The coffee is the most solid thing in the picture, a warm amber glow shining up through his ribs, its steam pale cream-white, with frost curls licking at his ankles where the living get fire.

Reared up on his haunches, mouth open in flat astonishment, one dark paw round the fry carton and the other thrown open wide as blank gold bottlecaps whirl in to him. The whirl hugs his torso so every cap overlaps his body — the ones passing behind him painted as dimmed, cooled discs ON his chest rather than gaps — and he is pure delight about it, never greed.

Reared up on his hind legs, smug and dry, one clearly opaque near-black paw closed round the handle of a small umbrella tilted forward over his skull, canopy compact and well inside the frame. The rain that misses it is painted as pale blue streaks ON his forearm just above the wrist, breaking into spray where it meets his paws — that contrast of solid paw and rained-through arm is the whole character in one frame.

Braced and flinching inside a close-fitting blue-violet dome that hugs his silhouette, paws up, eyes screwed half shut in relief. The dome's light pins a hard bright rim along the near edge of his fur and glows through him; short rain streaks skid off its outer surface.

Up on his hind legs, dark paws clutched to his chest, eyes huge and fixed up-screen at whatever is lining up its dive. He is so alarmed he has gone faint — the bottom third of him painted as a pale ice-blue wisp mass, still opaque inside a solid rim, curling up against his shins, with thin wisps streaming off his ear tips.

Sprinting hard to the left, mouth open in panic, both hind feet clear, stubby tail bristled. His panic reads cold rather than red — short white-blue smears and frost flecks attached to his flanks and heels, plus a small burst of ice-star shock sparks touching his head where a comic would letter punctuation; no marks, no lettering.

Reared tall with one sooty paw raised beside his head — compact, not a full overhead stretch, so his head stays the same pixel size as every other frame — mouth open in pure joy, hind feet dangling loose. Brightest and most solid he ever gets: a warm amber-gold glow rising through his chest, the fog blown back into a tight ring on his shoulders, because somebody finally saw him.

On his back, front legs up, swooning half-moon lids and solid gold stars circling and overlapping his head — never X eyes, and never a hard horizontal cut line. His lower half is breaking into pale wisps that curl back UP toward his chest in a loop, re-gathering rather than dissolving, while one sooty paw lifts in a small apologetic wave: he cannot even be knocked over properly.

Sprawled with spiral eyes and tongue out, gold stars and wisps spiralling together and touching his head. His outline has come uncoupled into a second copy offset only a quarter of a body width, so the two silhouettes share most of their area — painted solid pale blue at reduced contrast, never a genuine fade.

The instant of shock inside an exploding crown of water: both sooty paws up, round shocked eyes, comically open mouth, fur soaked flat. Nobody sinks — the crown bursts white and ice-blue against his body, the water passing behind him painted as a dimmed cooled band ON his chest rather than a hole, and no piece of him is carried off downstream.

sheetNotes: ENVELOPE: paint all eighteen on the same 242x250 canvas as the four existing frames (aspect 0.968) and check them by head size — his head must be the same number of pixels in every frame. Effects included, no frame may go below 0.80:1 or above 1.35:1, and nothing may touch a frame edge or a divider line.

THE FLOAT LIVES IN THE POSE, NOT IN THE MARGIN. The earlier note about leaving blank space under his paws is wrong twice over: the cutter crops tight to painted content so that margin is deleted, and the engine centres the sprite on its content rather than bottom-anchoring it. Sell the hover with slack toes, uncompressed limbs, no shadow and a faint ice-blue underglow on the pads.

NO GROUND, EVER, IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. No asphalt, curb, road, puddle, splash-on-pavement, drying smear, drag streak, scattered litter or cast shadow — they all cut out as floating grey scum under a character who has nothing beneath him. Contact effects that touch his body are correct and welcome.

HE IS OPAQUE PAINT THAT LOOKS TRANSLUCENT. Every see-through area is a pale blue-grey or white wash with the green channel high (150+), inside a continuous solid rim around the whole silhouette — never a blend toward the magenta background and never a background-coloured pixel inside his outline, or the flood eats a hole through his belly in every frame.

EFFECT COLOUR: cold means cyan, ice-blue and white with green up; warm means amber-gold. No hot pink, Keep every wisp, contrail, star, cap and afterimage physically attached to or overlapping his silhouette; anything loose in the magenta is dropped or shipped as a bogus sprite.

NO PRINTING ON THE PROPS — a painter will letter these by reflex. The takeaway cup is plain with no logo or sleeve print, the fry carton is a plain kraft or red-and-white box with no words, the bottlecaps are blank fluted gold discs with no cap face. At 59px his reading anchors are the dark bandit mask, the dark eye patches and the near-black paws; give the whole silhouette a thin cool grey-blue outline so a bone-white animal does not vanish against pale rain and fog lane art.
ghost.runL: mirror — nothing on him is asymmetric, there is no lettering and no side-carried prop in run-r, so only the vapour fray flips and nobody reads drift as wrong in either direction.

sasquatch.stance: Upright bipedal at rest on two flat tan feet; drops to a four-point knuckle-bound (two flat feet plus two knuckles, never fists, never palms) for every travel frame — crouch, leap, land, run-r, run-l, dash-run and flee. The words "four-square" never apply to him.
sasquatch.wardrobe: No clothing at all, bare shagged pelt only — and in all eighteen frames: a thin moss cap over his crown, plus on his LEFT shoulder a thick moss pad carrying two sword-fern fronds, a cluster of orange chanterelles, and a small rust-brown found umbrella wedged butt-down through the moss and angled back along his spine (stowed and closed in sixteen frames; lifted out and open only in umbrella and ko, and in both it stays physically touching him).
sasquatch.anatomy: He is an eight-foot, several-hundred-pound ape with full hands, so raccoon poses transfer honestly — the real translation problem is mass, and he must never read weightless. Because he stands upright at rest, both hands are genuinely free in idle, coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared and cheer; the instant he travels he is on knuckles and feet, and no frame may silently swap the two. Every "coat" on this sheet is his own soaked shaggy pelt, not a garment — he wears nothing. Everything Jimothy plays fast, Sasquatch plays one beat slow: read the speed off the swinging pelt, the flung rainwater and the streaming ferns, never off his face, which holds the same mild patient frown through idle, sit, crouch, leap, land, run-r, run-l, dash-run, umbrella and shield — that hold IS the joke, and it only breaks for eat, coffee, magnet, scared, flee, cheer and the three deaths.

frames.desc: Upright on two flat tan feet, caught mid-step-back — weight rocking onto his heels, one huge palm half-raised as if he has just been seen, eyes cut off-camera under the patient half-frown of someone who has waited out worse rain than this. Long arms hanging past his knees, shoulders sloped, rain beading white through the dark pelt, teal rim light down both edges.

Sat straight down cross-legged and enormous, knees wide, one hand loose on his own ankle and the other palm turned up in his lap slowly filling with rainwater. Head tilted a few degrees, eyes soft and off to one side, watching a corner he remembers being something else — the quiet frame of the sheet; ferns hang forward off the shoulder garden.

Same cross-legged sit, but he has reached ACROSS with his far hand and picked one chanterelle off his own SHOULDER cluster, holding it up between two fingertips like a canapé, mouth just opening, eyes fondly crossed on it. The shoulder cluster is visibly one mushroom short; a few blackberries sit in his other cupped palm, collecting rain.

Dropped into the knuckle-bound gather — both flat feet and both knuckles planted, back arched high so the mossy shoulder rises above his head line, haunches up, pelt hanging in wet ropes off his belly. Brow low, eyes forward and perfectly calm, a tight collar of spray bursting where each knuckle presses.

The airborne beat of a gorilla gallop: both long arms reaching FORWARD together, hands open and leading, shoulders and mossy back at the top of the arc, both legs gathered up under the belly, body long and heavy — mass in flight, never spread-eagle. Face completely unchanged, the same mild patient frown, pelt and ferns streaming back with flung droplets trailing off his heels and still touching them.

Four-point touchdown, knuckles and flat feet planted, knees folded, head coming back up under the brow. A tight cyan-white sheet of splash bursts at each of the four contact points, water flicks off his elbows, the pelt lifts a beat behind him before it drops — the ferns bounce, he does not.

Side-on knuckle lope to the right with the garden shoulder rolled forward and nearest camera, the leading knuckle planting no further ahead than his own body length while the far arm swings back to sell the span. Both hind legs swinging through underneath, pelt moving as one heavy mass, ferns and chanterelles leaning back, face level and unhurried, one tight flick of water off the trailing foot.

The same lope flat out — both feet clear of the ground mid-stride, arms driving fore and aft but the fingertip span held inside the aspect ceiling, pelt streaming behind him like a soaked rug, white speed streaks and a tight rooster-tail of rainwater breaking off his heels. Mouth shut, eyes calm, one eyebrow raised the smallest possible amount to acknowledge that he is now moving quickly.

STANDING STILL — feet planted flat and square to camera, holding a takeaway cup so small he has to pinch it between two fingertips, pale cream-white steam curling past his nose. All the speed is in the body: pelt lifted and bristling with static, ferns standing straight up, jitter lines off his shoulders, orange fire licking up around his planted feet, and his eyes round and WIDE OPEN — the one frame where he looks properly awake.

Standing upright with both arms spread low and open like a man about to receive a hug he has been owed for forty years, mouth open in a slow delighted "oh", eyebrows up in pure astonishment. Gold bottlecaps, fries and blackberries spiral in tight to his chest — the outer ones overlapping his silhouette and never more than a hand's width off the fur, several already stuck in the wet pelt, two lodged in the shoulder moss.

Standing dead calm in pouring rain, the little rust-brown umbrella lifted out of the moss and opened across his own shoulder line with the canopy tipped toward camera, so the silhouette plainly says COVERED — canopy topping out level with the fern crown, no higher. Rain sheets off the near rim while his own face and beard get thoroughly soaked, the ferns underneath are conspicuously fluffy and dry, and he wears a faint smug half-smile.

Braced upright with both forearms crossed high in front of his face and both feet planted, umbrella left stowed in the shoulder moss; a bright blue-violet dome flares tight around him — a hand's width off the fur, no taller than the ferns — with rain streaking off it sideways. Pelt and ferns flattened back by the shockwave, and his entire reaction to being saved is one raised eyebrow.

Hunched down small and turned half away, hiding behind his own shoulder garden and peering out through the gaps in his huge splayed fingers — the alarm is being SEEN, not the bird. A hard wing-shaped shadow cuts across his chest, his other hand cups protectively over the moss and chanterelles, eyes enormous, mouth a small open O.

Barrelling toward camera on a three-quarter angle in the airborne beat of the bound, both hands off the road — near hand clamped flat over the shoulder garden to stop the mushrooms bouncing off, far arm already reaching for the next knuckle plant. Mouth open in real alarm for the only time on the sheet, white and red speed streaks, twin exclamation strokes tight above his head, rainwater sheeting off the trailing arm.

Standing tall and square, chest out, head tipped back, both enormous arms raised in joy but ELBOWS BENT so his hands stay level with the fern crown and the frame stays exactly as tall as idle — huge open-mouthed grin, the only one he does. Second read baked into the same painting: one eye already sliding sideways to check that nobody watched him do it; water flicks off both forearms in tight arcs, warm gold light on the wet fur.

Flat on his back, arms and legs sprawled up and out, pelt spread around him like a dropped rug, mouth open in a soft "oof" and one big toe twitching; eyes are swooning half-moons with stars circling his head and a fern sprig flopped down over one eye. The open umbrella leans against his own forearm, touching him, and his free hand is half-raised in a tiny apologetic wave to nobody — mortified at having been seen go down.

Sprawled back on his backside with legs straight out, spiral eyes, tongue out the side, head lolling, stars circling. The street sweeper has scrubbed one absurdly clean bright streak straight through his soaked pelt and combed his shoulder moss into neat parallel rows, and a small tidy pile of swept leaves plus one plain dished hubcap sit in his lap, touching him.

Dropped straight down into the middle of an exploding crown of white water, water to his waist, both arms flung up clear of the burst — plainly out of play, not swimming, not sinking, the one thing in Seattle he is too big for and still losing to. Eyes wide and both eyebrows up in mild personal offence at the whole business, mossy shoulder hoisted high so the ferns and chanterelles stay perfectly, pointlessly dry above the churn.

sheetNotes: CENTRE-ANCHORED, not bottom-anchored — the engine centres the sprite on the lane point. Keep his mass at the centre of the painted content in every cell: anything painted high above him pushes the character DOWN off his lane line, anything painted below pushes him UP off it.

NO GROUND IN ANY OF THE EIGHTEEN. No puddles, no rain rings, no drying smears, no cast shadows on the road, no curbs, no scattered leaf litter, no kicked-up flecks that are not touching him — the cutter is a magenta flood and every one of those survives as floating grey scum under a character with no floor. Contact effects that touch the body are correct and wanted: spray bursting at a knuckle, water breaking off a heel, the crown at his waterline.

Aspect 0.80:1 to 1.35:1 in EVERY frame, effects included, inside one envelope no more than about 1.2x the idle box. The single checkable test: his HEAD is the same number of pixels in all eighteen — if an effect shrinks the head, the effect is too big. Worst offenders are leap, dash-run and cheer, which is exactly why cheer's elbows stay bent and run-r's knuckle plants only one body length ahead.

COLOUR LAW — the knockout eats the magenta family, so it will bite ragged holes in pink or violet effects. Coffee steam is pale cream-white (not pink), land and splash water is cyan-white (not purple-white), the shield dome is blue-violet like Jimothy's own. Keep the teal-black rim light down his edges and the white water beads through the fur in all eighteen — those two are what make him read at 59px on wet asphalt.

NO LETTERING ANYWHERE: the umbrella is plain rust-brown with one patched panel and no logo, the dizzy hubcap is a plain dished disc. And no loose-fur debris in any frame — none at all, and least of all on ko, dizzy and splash, where shed fur reads as injury instead of motion.

Do NOT pre-enlarge him; the engine already draws Sasquatch at scale 1.35, so he only has to match himself cell to cell. Sell the eight feet with props instead — the pinched takeaway cup, the toy-sized umbrella, the hubcap sitting in his lap like a coin. The tallest thing on him is a fern, not his head, so leave clear magenta above the highest frond in every cell and let nothing touch a divider line. Paint idle, leap and cheer first and send those three for the envelope check before committing the other fifteen.
sasquatch.runL: Painted separately: the moss pad, ferns, chanterelles and stowed umbrella all ride his LEFT shoulder, which is the near camera-side in run-r — mirroring would swing the entire garden to the wrong shoulder, so run-l is painted fresh with the garden on the FAR shoulder, cresting over his back line so it still silhouettes.

richuncle.stance: UPRIGHT AT REST — he sits back on his haunches or stands on his hind legs for every still frame (idle, sit, eat, coffee, magnet, umbrella, shield, scared, cheer) and drops to all fours ONLY for the six athletic frames (crouch, leap, land, run-r, dash-run, flee); he is never four-square with anything in a paw.
richuncle.wardrobe: IN ALL 18: black wet-silk top hat with an oxblood band and a soft battered brim; gold-rimmed monocle over his RIGHT eye (frame-left when he faces right) with a fine gold chain dropping to the waistcoat; cream wing collar with spread points; big oxblood bow tie with one gold stud; dark olive-brown buttoned waistcoat with small gold buttons; a heavier gold watch chain swagged across the belly of the waistcoat; and a SHORT oxblood shoulder cape over BOTH shoulders fastened at the throat — there is NO tailcoat and NO coat tails in any frame, the cape is the only garment that trails. Per-frame props only, never carried outside their frame: gold pocket watch (sit, magnet), takeaway fry box on a small silver tray (eat), doll-sized espresso cup (coffee), compact black umbrella (umbrella), and the identical gold bottlecap in dash-run, magnet, scared, flee, cheer, dizzy, splash.
richuncle.anatomy: He is Jimothy's own body — round and spherical with no visible neck, the head perched high on the shoulders, long skinny limbs, and a SHORT STUBBY ringed tail; never the long streaming trash-panda tail, in any frame, including the sprints. Plantigrade throughout: flat palms, five long spread fingers, heels down — no knuckles, ever, and the hands are half of why the character works, so keep them readable even at speed. The hat, monocle and the two gold chains are HARD props sitting on a body that squashes and stretches, so they must be re-drawn honestly in each pose rather than smeared along with the fur — a warped top hat reads as a mistake instantly. His comic engine is that the body performs the entire athletic pose while the face declines to acknowledge it, and the hat is the mood ring.

frames.desc: Reared up and settled back on his haunches the way a man settles into a leather club chair — spine straight, belly forward, chin lifted, one flat forepaw laid on the waistcoat over the watch chain, the other hanging loose. Hat dead level with rain beading on the wet silk, monocle catching a single bright glint with its fine chain hanging plumb, stubby tail curled against his hip; amused, bored, and slightly damp.

The same club-chair seat gone soft: hind ankles crossed, gold pocket watch open on his flat upturned palm, the heavy chain running taut back to the waistcoat, hat still dead level. This is his quiet frame — the monocle fogs a little with his breath and he is checking the time for an appointment nobody is coming to.

Sitting the same way with a dented takeaway fry box on a small silver tray balanced on his knee and resting against his belly, a white linen napkin tucked into the bow tie. He eats exactly one fry pinched between two claws with the pinky extended, eyes closed in mild approval, monocle fogged over from the steam and both chains undisturbed — still a raccoon eating garbage, just served properly.

Gathered low on all fours, chest near the ground, haunches up, flat plantigrade palms planted wide and loaded, stubby tail arched short over his back. Nothing in the face has changed: hat dead level, monocle seated with its chain hanging plumb, eyes forward and unhurried, like a sprinter who finds the whole business beneath comment.

Fully airborne, belly forward, long forelimbs thrown wide with the fingers spread, hind legs trailing, the oxblood cape flared back off both shoulders. The top hat has lifted half an inch clear but still overlaps his ears, the monocle is somehow still in with its fine chain flying in a bright gold arc across his chest, and his face is serene — as though he is being carried rather than jumping.

Front palms slapped flat, body compressed low, hind legs still catching up, a tight white crown of street water bursting where his paws are and touching them — no puddle, no pavement, no shadow painted anywhere. The hat is settling back down with a fine ring of rainwater flicking off the brim, monocle level, watch chain still swinging, and his face is already composed.

Three-quarter sprint to the right — turned toward camera exactly like the shipped leap and land, never flat profile, so the monocle side stays visible — body low and long, forelimbs at full reach, stubby ringed tail held short and straight out behind. One flat palm clamped over the crown of the hat to hold it down, the other reaching forward, cape and both gold chains snapping back; absolutely nothing under him, no wet-street reflection and no shadow.

Flat out, legs at full stretch, cape and both gold chains snapping straight back and the bow tie blown up under his chin — no coat tails, the cape is the trail. Short gold speed streaks touch his heels and four gold bottlecaps kick off his hind paws and stay tight behind him, while from the neck up he is entirely unchanged: hat dead level, monocle in, expression mildly bored.

Feet planted, standing upright on his hind legs and going nowhere for seven seconds, and for the first time in his life visibly rattled — fur bristling out through the waistcoat, eyes enormous with pinprick pupils, monocle popped out and swinging on its chain, back heel a tapping blur. A doll-sized espresso cup pinched between two claws with the pinky out, pale blush-cream steam and warm gold jitter lines close around his shoulders; the hat is level but vibrating, and caffeine is the one thing old money cannot stay above.

Up on his hind legs with the pocket watch forgotten and swinging open on its chain, head up, both eyes wide and mouth open in unguarded delight — the one second old money forgets itself, astonished that the world is coming to him. A tight spiral of gold bottlecaps and fries curls in close around his chest and shoulders, every piece overlapping his body, three of them already caught in the upturned brim of the hat; monocle knocked cheerfully crooked.

Standing on his hind legs under a compact black silk umbrella with a brass handle held one-pawed, canopy no wider than his own body and tilted back so it stays well clear of the frame edge, top hat still on underneath it because he sees no contradiction. Rain beads and runs off the canopy rim in a tight bright ring touching the fabric — nothing on the ground, no dry patch and no shadow; monocle glinting, both chains still, eyes half-lidded and faintly pleased with himself.

The instant the shield eats a hit: braced in a quarter-turn away, one flat palm up, a blue-violet dome flaring tight around him with rain streaking off its skin — bright and pale, never blue-violet. This is the only frame where the composure cracks: monocle knocked askew on its chain, top hat tipped down over one eye, mouth open in an undignified flinch.

Up on his hind legs, both forepaws clutched to the waistcoat, head craned up at the sky, eyes huge and round behind the monocle with its chain trembling. sheetNotes: CANVAS AND SCALE, MEASURED OFF THE FOUR SHIPPED PNGs. All four (idle, crouch, leap, land) are exactly 218x250 px, painted content between 168x229 and 218x215. Paint every frame's content — effects included — inside 218 x 229, then pad all 18 to one identical 218x250 canvas with the body's mass centred. Sprites are CENTRE-anchored, not bottom-anchored, so anything painted above his head pushes the whole raccoon below the lane line; the identical canvas plus centred mass is what keeps his head the same pixel size in all 18, which is the one checkable test on the sheet.

NO GROUND, ANYWHERE, IN ANY FRAME. The cutter is a magenta border flood that keeps every non-magenta island, so painted puddles, wet-street gold reflections, the dry patch under the umbrella, cast shadows, skid marks and caps scattered on pavement all survive the cut as floating grey scum under a character with nothing beneath him. Contact effects only: the water crown bursting at his paws in land, the spray in splash, caps landing ON him. Every loose element must overlap his bounding box and sit within half a body width, or the components cutter emits it as a separate sprite file.

COLOUR LAW. Keep the oxblood on the RED side — the shipped art measures about #7A1E28 to #8C3232 with the blue channel low, and it has zero pixels in the knockout range. THE HAT IS THE MOOD RING — paint the angle deliberately every time. Dead level: idle, sit, eat, crouch, dash-run, magnet, umbrella. Clamped or lifted: leap, land, run-r, coffee, scared, flee. Tipped over one eye: shield. Off his head entirely: cheer, ko, dizzy, splash. Keep the silk glossy and rain-beaded in every outdoor frame — at 59px on a phone that wet gloss on a black cylinder is the only thing separating his silhouette from First Frost and Nordic Jimothy.
